searchText: Abixim 100 Tablets (50x20x10's) Cefixime 100 mg DT Tab by Abbott Abbott 2040004074
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, chest, urinary tract and other areas. It does not work against viral infections like the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall, which helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Disperse the tablet in water before taking it if instructed on the product label or by the pharmacist. Do not share or reuse leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and vomiting may occur. Skin rash can also occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to cefixime, cephalosporins or penicillin-type antibiotics, and about kidney disease. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can cause resistance.

searchText: Abixim O Tablets (50x10x10's) Cefixime 200 mg, Ofloxacin 200 mg Tab by Abbott Abbott 2040003943
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime interferes with the formation of the bacterial cell wall. Ofloxacin blocks bacterial enzymes needed for growth and multiplication.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it with antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc at the same time; follow the prescriber's or product label's instructions about spacing.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion, headache, dizziness or vomiting.

Precautions
Do not use if there is a known allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporins, penicillins or ofloxacin/other quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash or breathing difficulty, unusual nerve symptoms, or pain/swelling in a tendon. Use only on medical advice during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in people with kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, seizures or a history of tendon disorders.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of acidity, heartburn, indigestion and gas-related bloating or discomfort.

How does it work?
Aluminium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide neutralise excess stomach acid. Simethicone helps gas bubbles join together so trapped gas can pass more easily.

How to take/use it
Shake the suspension well before use. Measure it with the supplied measuring device and take it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Keep a 2–4 hour gap from other medicines unless a doctor or pharmacist advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Constipation or loose stools, nausea, stomach cramps and a chalky or unpleasant taste may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease. Do not use for a prolonged period without medical advice. Consult a doctor if symptoms are severe, keep returning, or do not improve. Tell a doctor or pharmacist about other medicines, as antacids can affect their absorption.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat a range of bacterial infections caused by susceptible bacteria. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills bacteria by interfering with their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes that can make some bacteria resistant to it.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Swallow with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share this medicine or use leftover tablets.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin, other penicillin-type antibiotics or certain cephalosporins. Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related jaundice or severe diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe skin rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with potassium clavulanate injection is used to treat certain bacterial infections, including serious infections when treatment by injection is needed. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of infections.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and other factors, so it should be used exactly as prescribed. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash, injection-site discomfort and irritation of the vein may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillins, cephalosporins or similar antibiotics. Tell the healthcare professional about kidney or liver problems and any previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea or colitis. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose, and watery or itchy eyes. It may also be prescribed as an add-on treatment for asthma related to allergies, but it does not relieve a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, a substance responsible for many allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that contribute to allergic inflammation and narrowing of the airways.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. It may cause drowsiness in some people, so avoid driving until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhoea.

Precautions
This medicine is not a rescue treatment for a sudden asthma attack. Seek medical advice promptly if new or worsening mood or behaviour changes, nightmares, agitation, anxiety, depression, or suicidal thoughts occur. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines that cause drowsiness.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to help improve appetite and support weight gain in people with poor appetite or inadequate nutritional intake, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine blocks certain histamine and serotonin effects and may stimulate appetite. Tricholine citrate and sorbitol are included as supportive ingredients in the formulation.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by the doctor. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device and do not take more than prescribed. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, increased appetite, nausea and stomach discomfort. Sorbitol may cause loose stools or abdominal discomfort in some people.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and use caution with sleeping tablets, sedatives or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Tell the doctor if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate problems, asthma, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe sleepiness, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This syrup is used for temporary relief of dry cough and cold symptoms such as a blocked or runny nose, sneezing and watery eyes.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps reduce the urge to cough. Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-like symptoms, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Shake the bottle well and measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device, not a household spoon. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other cough, cold or decongestant medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea and stomach upset. Some people may experience nervousness, a fast heartbeat or increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if sleepy or dizzy. Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, prostate or urination problems, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not use with MAO inhibitor medicines or within 14 days of stopping them; check before use with antidepressants or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice if the cough is severe, lasts several days, or is accompanied by breathing difficulty, chest pain or high fever.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, difficulty passing urine or liver disease. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines, and check with a healthcare professional before use with antidepressants or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice for breathing difficulty, severe or persistent cough, or symptoms that do not improve.

searchText: Chupp LS Syrup 100ml (100x100ml) Ambroxol 30 mg, Levosalbutamol 1 mg, Guaiphenesin 50 mg Syr by Abbott Abbott 2040005136
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with phlegm and chest congestion, especially when mucus is difficult to bring up and there is wheezing or narrowing of the airways.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to cough out. Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles of the airways and helps improve breathing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Shake the bottle well before use and measure the syrup with a proper measuring device. Do not exceed the recommended amount or combine it with other cough medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, tremor, nervousness, fast heartbeat or palpitations.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain, severe palpitations, or signs of an allergic reaction. Consult a doctor if the cough persists or is accompanied by high fever or blood-stained mucus.

title: Chupp LS Syrup 60ml (200x60ml) Ambroxol 30 mg, Levosalbutamol 1 mg, Guaiphenesin 50 mg Syr by Abbott
name: Chupp LS Syrup 60ml (200x60ml) Ambroxol 30 mg, Levosalbutamol 1 mg, Guaiphenesin 50 mg Syr by Abbott
searchText: Chupp LS Syrup 60ml (200x60ml) Ambroxol 30 mg, Levosalbutamol 1 mg, Guaiphenesin 50 mg Syr by Abbott Abbott 2040005154
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve productive cough with mucus and chest congestion, and to help ease wheezing or breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus so it can be coughed out more easily. Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Shake the bottle well before use and measure each dose with a proper measuring device. Do not exceed the recommended amount or combine with other cough, cold or bronchodilator medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Trembling, nervousness, headache, dizziness, fast heartbeat or palpitations, nausea, vomiting, stomach upset and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling or breathing difficulty.

title: C-One 1000mg Injection (16x25x1g m) Ceftriaxone 1000 mg Inj by Abbott
name: C-One 1000mg Injection (16x25x1g m) Ceftriaxone 1000 mg Inj by Abbott
searchText: C-One 1000mg Injection (16x25x1g m) Ceftriaxone 1000 mg Inj by Abbott Abbott 2040000470
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones and joints, and meningitis. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, swelling or redness at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, rash and changes in blood-test results may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to ceftriaxone, cephalosporin or penicillin antibiotics, or a history of severe antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or yellowing of the skin or eyes. This injection requires special medical consideration in newborn babies and in people with liver or kidney problems.

title: C-One 250mg Injection (16x25x1g m) Ceftriaxone 250 mg Inj by Abbott
name: C-One 250mg Injection (16x25x1g m) Ceftriaxone 250 mg Inj by Abbott
searchText: C-One 250mg Injection (16x25x1g m) Ceftriaxone 250 mg Inj by Abbott Abbott 2040000471
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic injection used to treat a wide range of serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen, blood, bones and joints. It may also be used for certain sexually transmitted bacterial infections when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How to take/use it
Ceftriaxone is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and should be decided by the prescriber. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; rash; and changes in blood test results.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillin or other cephalosporin antibiotics, and about liver, kidney or gallbladder problems. Seek medical help for difficulty breathing, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Do not use it for viral infections or without medical supervision.

title: C-One 500mg Injection (16x25x1g m) Ceftriaxone 500 mg Inj by Abbott

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic used to treat a wide range of serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, blood, urinary tract, skin, abdomen and brain. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional into a muscle or vein. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, swelling or tenderness at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; and skin rash.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any previous allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillin or other cephalosporin antibiotics. Seek medical help urgently for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor if severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea develops during or after treatment. Use only under medical supervision, especially in newborn babies or people with liver or kidney problems.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This injection is used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones and joints, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps ceftriaxone work against certain bacteria that can otherwise resist some antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, age, and kidney or liver function. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early unless advised by the doctor.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; rash; and changes in blood test results may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, and about kidney, liver or gallbladder problems. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing, facial swelling, a severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. This medicine should be used in newborns and during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

title: C-One SB Injection (16x25x1g m) Ceftriaxone 1000 mg, Sulbactam 500 mg Inj by Abbott

searchText: C-One SB Injection (16x25x1g m) Ceftriaxone 1000 mg, Sulbactam 500 mg Inj by Abbott Abbott 2040000806
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin and soft tissues, blood, bones or joints. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps protect ceftriaxone from enzymes produced by some bacteria, improving its activity.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and should be decided by the prescriber. Complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, rash and changes in liver test results may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, and about liver, kidney or gallbladder problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This prescription injection is used to treat serious bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect ceftriaxone from enzymes made by some resistant bacteria.

How to take/use it
It is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose, frequency and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, so follow the healthcare professional’s instructions. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, skin rash, and pain, redness or swelling at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, other cephalosporins, penicillins or other antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, gallbladder disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe skin rash, or severe or bloody diarrhoea. This medicine requires special precautions in newborn babies and with calcium-containing intravenous solutions.

title: Co-Symoxyl 1.2g (18x10x1.2gm) Amoxycillin 1000 mg, Potassium Clavulanate 200 mg by Abbott
name: Co-Symoxyl 1.2g (18x10x1.2gm) Amoxycillin 1000 mg, Potassium Clavulanate 200 mg by Abbott
searchText: Co-Symoxyl 1.2g (18x10x1.2gm) Amoxycillin 1000 mg, Potassium Clavulanate 200 mg by Abbott Abbott 2040014579
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with potassium clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills bacteria by disrupting their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate helps prevent some bacteria from breaking down amoxycillin, making the antibiotic effective against a wider range of bacteria.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions for the route, timing and duration of treatment. Do not stop treatment early or share it with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin or similar antibiotics. Inform the doctor about previous antibiotic-related liver problems or jaundice. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

title: COSYMOXYL 625MG TABS 105 (24x12x10's) Amoxycillin 500 mg, Clavulanic Acid 125 mg Tab by Abbott
name: COSYMOXYL 625MG TABS 105 (24x12x10's) Amoxycillin 500 mg, Clavulanic Acid 125 mg Tab by Abbott
searchText: COSYMOXYL 625MG TABS 105 (24x12x10's) Amoxycillin 500 mg, Clavulanic Acid 125 mg Tab by Abbott Abbott 2040004021
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ear, sinuses, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, and teeth. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps protect amoxycillin from bacterial enzymes that can make it ineffective.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Take it with a meal or snack to help reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them for a future illness.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, cephalosporin antibiotics or this medicine. Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, and other medicines being used. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, a severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially with blood or mucus.

name: Co-Symoxyl Dry Syrup 30ml (8x25x30ml) Amoxycillin 200 mg, Potassium Clavulanate 28.5 mg Dry Syr by Abbott

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, lungs, skin, urinary tract and teeth, when prescribed by a healthcare professional. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes made by some resistant bacteria, allowing it to work more effectively.

How to take/use it
Use only in the dose and for the duration prescribed. Shake the suspension well before each use and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not use leftover medicine or share it with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics or any ingredient. Inform the healthcare professional about liver disease, kidney disease or previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

title: Dexamethasone Injection 2ml (50x24x2ml) Dexamethasone 4 mg Inj by Abbott
name: Dexamethasone Injection 2ml (50x24x2ml) Dexamethasone 4 mg Inj by Abbott
searchText: Dexamethasone Injection 2ml (50x24x2ml) Dexamethasone 4 mg Inj by Abbott Abbott 2040011307
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Dexamethasone injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce severe inflammation and allergic reactions. It may also be used for other serious conditions requiring rapid corticosteroid treatment; the exact use depends on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and allergic or immune reactions.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or clinic. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject or use it without medical supervision.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, stomach upset, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, increased appetite, fluid retention and pain or redness at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, mental health conditions, osteoporosis or any current infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Seek medical help for severe allergic reactions, unusual weakness, vision changes or signs of infection. If used for more than a short period, it should not be stopped suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

title: Diclofam Forte Gel Tube (15x20x30gm) Diclofenac Sodium 1.0% w/w, Virgin Linseed Oil 3%, Methyl Salicylate 10% w/w, Menthol 5%, Benzyl Alcohol 1% Gel by Abbott
name: Diclofam Forte Gel Tube (15x20x30gm) Diclofenac Sodium 1.0% w/w, Virgin Linseed Oil 3%, Methyl Salicylate 10% w/w, Menthol 5%, Benzyl Alcohol 1% Gel by Abbott
searchText: Diclofam Forte Gel Tube (15x20x30gm) Diclofenac Sodium 1.0% w/w, Virgin Linseed Oil 3%, Methyl Salicylate 10% w/w, Menthol 5%, Benzyl Alcohol 1% Gel by Abbott Abbott 2040000267
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This gel is used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, such as sprains, strains and arthritis-related pain.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Methyl salicylate and capsaicin provide a local warming or cooling sensation that may help reduce the feeling of pain.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the painful area and gently rub in, as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. For external use only. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Do not apply to broken, infected or irritated skin, or cover tightly with a bandage.

Common side effects
Burning, warmth, stinging, redness, itching, dryness or skin irritation at the application site. Capsaicin may cause temporary burning.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other painkillers of the NSAID type, or any ingredient in the gel. Avoid heating pads and direct heat over the treated area. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe skin irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction occurs. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, particularly in the last three months, or while breastfeeding.

title: Diclofam Gel Tube (15x20x30gm) REVIEW REQUIRED by Abbott
name: Diclofam Gel Tube (15x20x30gm) REVIEW REQUIRED by Abbott
searchText: Diclofam Gel Tube (15x20x30gm) REVIEW REQUIRED by Abbott Abbott 2040000263
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions. Rabeprazole helps reduce stomach acid and may help protect against stomach irritation caused by diclofenac.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Rabeprazole lowers stomach acid by blocking the acid-producing pump in the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Take it with or after food unless directed otherwise. Do not take additional diclofenac, ibuprofen or other NSAID painkillers without medical advice.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache or dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAIDs. Avoid use during pregnancy, particularly after 20 weeks and in the last trimester, unless specifically prescribed. Inform the doctor about blood thinners, steroids, other painkillers or medicines for blood pressure. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

name: Diclofam Hot Gel (15x20x30gm) Menthol 5% w/w, Capsaicin 0.0255 w/w, Benzyl Alcohol 1% w/w Gel by Abbott

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve nerve pain (neuropathic pain), such as burning, tingling, numbness or shooting pain caused by irritated or damaged nerves.

How does it work?
Pregabalin reduces abnormal pain signals in the nerves. Mecobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 that supports normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or split it. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, blurred vision, dry mouth, tiredness, swelling of the hands or feet, increased appetite or weight gain.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney disease. Older adults and people taking opioids or other medicines that cause sleepiness may have increased drowsiness or breathing problems. Seek medical help for facial or throat swelling, severe breathing difficulty, or thoughts of self-harm.

name: Diclofam Injection 3ml (1000x3ml) Diclofenac Sodium 25 mg Inj by Abbott

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, including pain from sprains, strains and arthritis.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling or warming sensation that may help relieve discomfort.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the painful area and gently rub in, following the product label or a healthcare professional’s advice. Wash hands after use. Do not apply to cuts, wounds, irritated skin or near the eyes, and do not cover with a tight bandage or apply heat unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, dryness or a burning sensation at the application site. Stop use if a severe rash or swelling develops.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other painkillers such as ibuprofen, or any ingredient in the gel. Do not use on broken skin or with other diclofenac or NSAID products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months, or if there is a history of stomach ulcers, kidney disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, or severe skin sensitivity. Keep away from children and avoid swallowing.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Paracetamol 1000 mg injection is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain when treatment by injection is appropriate.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the brain that contribute to pain and fever.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration are decided by the healthcare professional based on the patient's condition. Do not use other paracetamol-containing medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, and pain or reaction at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, regular heavy alcohol use, severe kidney disease, dehydration, or an allergy to paracetamol. Do not exceed the prescribed amount, as overdose can cause serious liver damage. Seek urgent medical help after a suspected overdose, even if the person feels well.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, such as sprains, strains, backache and mild arthritis-related pain.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling or warming sensation that may help relieve discomfort.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Spray onto the painful area as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not spray on broken, infected or irritated skin. Wash hands after use and avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other painkillers or any ingredient in the product. Avoid tight bandages, heating pads and other heat sources over the treated area. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty or swelling occur. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months, or if there is a history of asthma triggered by painkillers.

title: Diclofam Spray 35g (24x6x35gm) Virgin Linseed Oil 3% w/w, Diclofenac Sodium 1% w/w, Methyl Salicylate 10% w/w, Menthol 5% w/w Spray by Abbott
name: Diclofam Spray 35g (24x6x35gm) Virgin Linseed Oil 3% w/w, Diclofenac Sodium 1% w/w, Methyl Salicylate 10% w/w, Menthol 5% w/w Spray by Abbott

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain, swelling and inflammation associated with muscle aches, sprains, strains and painful joints, including some arthritis-related pain.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol provides a cooling sensation, while methyl salicylate helps produce a soothing warming effect.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Spray a thin layer over the painful area as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not spray on broken, irritated or infected skin. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and wash hands after use.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, dryness or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin or other pain-relieving anti-inflammatory medicines. Avoid tight or airtight dressings and additional heat over the treated area. Stop use and seek medical help if severe skin rash, swelling, breathing difficulty or other signs of an allergic reaction occur. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, especially in the last three months, or while breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, including pain from sprains, strains and other minor soft-tissue injuries.

How does it work?
Diclofenac helps reduce pain and inflammation by reducing the formation of substances that cause swelling and pain. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling and warming sensation that may help relieve discomfort.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Spray onto the painful area as directed on the product label and gently spread if needed. Do not spray on broken, infected or irritated skin, and avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Wash hands after use unless treating the hands.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site. Stop use if a severe rash or other allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other pain-relieving anti-inflammatory medicines, methyl salicylate or any ingredient. Do not use with heat pads or tight bandages. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months, or if there is a history of asthma or stomach, kidney or heart problems. Seek medical advice if pain or swelling worsens or does not improve.

Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling or warming sensation that may help relieve discomfort.

For external use only. Spray on the painful area as directed on the product label and avoid spraying on the face. Do not apply to cuts, wounds, infected skin or near the eyes. Wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site. Stop use if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Paracetamol 500 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, toothache, body pain, muscle aches and menstrual pain.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that contribute to pain and fever. It helps lower a raised temperature and provides pain relief.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the package or by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow with water, with or without food. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it more often than advised. Check other medicines to make sure they do not also contain paracetamol.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated when used as directed. Nausea or mild stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to paracetamol. Consult a doctor before use if there is liver disease, regular heavy alcohol use, or severe malnutrition. Avoid taking it with other paracetamol-containing medicines. Taking too much can cause serious liver damage; seek urgent medical help after an overdose, even if feeling well. Stop use and seek medical help if a severe skin rash, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs.

title: Doliprane 650mg Tablets (24x50x10's) Paracetamol 650 mg Tab by Abbott

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, including headache, body aches and toothache.

How does it work?
Paracetamol acts on pain and temperature-regulating pathways in the body to reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than the recommended dose.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when taken at the recommended dose. Allergic reactions may occur rarely.

Precautions
Taking too much paracetamol can cause serious liver damage. Avoid taking it alongside other medicines containing paracetamol unless advised by a healthcare professional. Consult a doctor before use if you have liver disease or regularly consume alcohol.

title: Embee Suspension 10ml (20x25x10ml) Albendazole 200 mg Susp by Abbott

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Albendazole is used to treat worm infections, including roundworm, hookworm, pinworm and other intestinal parasite infections.

How does it work?
It damages the worms and prevents them from absorbing nutrients, causing them to die.

How to take/use it
Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with a proper measuring device. Take it only in the dose and for the duration recommended by a doctor or stated on the label.

Common side effects
Stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease or an allergy to albendazole. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, especially during the first trimester. Seek medical advice if severe abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, unusual bruising, or a severe skin rash occurs.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Naproxen is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness, especially in arthritis, muscle and joint conditions. It may also be used for short-term painful conditions such as menstrual pain.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow it with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, heartburn, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Naproxen can cause stomach ulcers or bleeding and may affect the kidneys, blood pressure or heart. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain or breathing difficulty. Tell a doctor if there is a history of ulcers, kidney or heart problems, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or use of blood thinners. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised, especially in the last 3 months.

What is it used for?
Nimesulide is used for short-term relief of acute pain, inflammation and fever, such as pain affecting the muscles or joints.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor, preferably with or after food. Use the lowest effective amount for the shortest period advised. Do not take it with other painkillers or anti-inflammatory medicines unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness, headache and skin rash.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice, especially if there is liver disease, stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or heart disease, or an allergy to anti-inflammatory medicines. Avoid alcohol. Stop taking it and seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, black stools, vomiting blood, facial swelling or breathing difficulty. It is generally avoided during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically prescribed.

How to take/use it
Take as prescribed by a doctor, preferably after food if advised. Do not exceed the prescribed dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, dizziness and vomiting.

Use under medical supervision, especially in people with stomach ulcers, kidney or liver problems, or heart conditions. Avoid combining it with other paracetamol-containing medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling, such as those associated with muscle or joint problems, injuries, dental pain or after certain procedures, as prescribed by a doctor.

Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation, while paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever. Serratiopeptidase may help reduce inflammation-related swelling.

Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other medicines containing diclofenac, other NSAIDs, or paracetamol unless advised by a doctor.

Indigestion, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Skin rash may also occur.

Avoid alcohol and inform the doctor about stomach ulcers, bleeding problems, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Used for short-term relief of painful muscle, joint and other musculoskeletal conditions associated with muscle spasm, swelling and stiffness.

Diclofenac reduces pain and inflammation, paracetamol helps relieve pain, and chlorzoxazone helps relax tense muscles.

Take only as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take other medicines containing diclofenac or paracetamol unless advised by a doctor. Chlorzoxazone may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery if affected.

Stomach upset, indigestion, nausea, abdominal pain, dizziness, drowsiness and headache.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or regular alcohol use. Avoid alcohol. bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of acidity, heartburn, indigestion and gas-related bloating or discomfort.

How does it work?
Aluminium and magnesium antacids neutralise excess stomach acid. Simethicone helps combine gas bubbles so they can pass more easily.

How to take/use it
Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Follow the dose and frequency on the product label or as advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Antacids may affect the absorption of other medicines, so ask a pharmacist or doctor about the appropriate time gap.

Common side effects
Constipation or loose motions, nausea, stomach discomfort, and a chalky taste may occur.

Precautions
Use only with medical advice if there is kidney disease. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, keep returning, or are accompanied by vomiting, difficulty swallowing, black stools, or unexplained weight loss.

Avoid use or seek medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to diclofenac or other NSAIDs. What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone injection is used for the short-term treatment of severe inflammation, allergic reactions, and flare-ups of autoimmune or other inflammatory conditions. The exact use depends on the patient's condition and the doctor's assessment.

How does it work?
It is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation and suppresses an overactive immune response.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a healthcare professional into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition, response to treatment, and medical advice. Do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, increased blood pressure, fluid retention, indigestion, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions, liver or kidney problems, or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically advised. After prolonged treatment, it should not be stopped suddenly without medical guidance. Seek medical help for signs of infection, severe mood changes, vision problems, or a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections when treatment by injection is needed. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making and repairing their genetic material, which prevents them from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and medical advice. Do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and injection-site discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics, kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, diabetes, seizures, tendon disorders or myasthenia gravis. Used mainly to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis (hay fever), such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that can contribute to nasal and airway inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it with fruit juice. If using aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids, take them at a different time as advised by a healthcare professional. Do not use it to treat a sudden asthma attack.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, tiredness, or dizziness may occur. Montelukast may rarely cause sleep problems, mood changes, irritability, or unusual behaviour.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional about kidney or liver problems, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines being used. Stop the medicine and seek medical advice promptly if serious mood or behaviour changes, suicidal thoughts, severe allergic symptoms, or breathing difficulty occur.

Used to support joint health and help relieve symptoms such as pain, stiffness and reduced movement associated with osteoarthritis and other joint problems.

Glucosamine is a natural component involved in cartilage formation and maintenance. Boswellia may help reduce inflammation by affecting inflammatory substances in the body.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May include nausea, stomach upset, heartburn, diarrhoea, constipation or headache.

Precautions
Check with a healthcare professional before use if allergic to shellfish, as some glucosamine products may be shellfish-derived. What is it used for?
Salicylic acid foaming face wash is used to help treat acne, blackheads and whiteheads by clearing blocked pores and removing excess oil and dead skin.

How does it work?
Salicylic acid helps loosen and remove dead skin cells from the surface and inside pores, helping prevent pore blockage.

How to take/use it
Use on wet skin and gently massage over the face, avoiding the eyes and lips. Rinse thoroughly and follow the product label. For external use only.

Common side effects
Dryness, peeling, redness, stinging or mild skin irritation may occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and broken or irritated skin. Stop use if severe irritation, swelling or rash occurs. Use cautiously with other acne or exfoliating products, as this may increase dryness and irritation. People sensitive to salicylates should seek medical advice before use.

Used as a moisturiser to relieve dry, rough, chapped or irritated skin.

How does it work?
White soft paraffin and liquid paraffin form a protective layer on the skin that helps reduce water loss. Vitamin E acetate helps support moisturisation of the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry skin and gently spread. Use as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or rash may occur. The skin may also feel greasy.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes. Stop using it if significant irritation or a rash develops. Paraffin-based products can increase the risk of clothing, dressings and bedding catching fire; keep away from flames and smoking, and wash clothing and fabrics regularly.

Used to moisturise, soften and protect dry, chapped or cracked lips.

How does it work?
The oils and butter help form a protective layer that reduces moisture loss from the lips. Vitamin E and the moisturising ingredients help keep the lip surface soft.

How to take/use it
Apply a small amount evenly to the lips when they feel dry or chapped. For external use only.

Common side effects
Mild irritation, redness, itching or a rash may occur, especially in sensitive people.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to almonds, other tree nuts or any ingredient in the product. Stop using it if irritation or swelling develops. Seek medical advice if severe cracking, bleeding or sores do not improve.

Used to cleanse the hair and scalp. The conditioning ingredients may help improve softness and manageability of dry or damaged-looking hair.

How does it work?
Sodium laureth sulphate and coco betaine help remove oil, dirt and product buildup from the hair and scalp. D-panthenol, wheat germ oil, jojoba oil and vitamin E acetate help condition the hair and support a smoother feel.

How to take/use it
Apply to wet hair and scalp, gently massage into a lather, then rinse thoroughly. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild scalp irritation, dryness, itching or redness may occur, especially in sensitive individuals.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes; rinse well with clean water if this occurs. Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction develops. Do not use if allergic to any ingredient.

name: Just-Shyne Stretch Mark Oil (60x80ml) Stretch Mark Oil by Abbott

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Stretch mark oil is used to moisturise and soften the skin and may help improve the appearance of stretch marks caused by skin stretching, such as during pregnancy, weight changes or growth.

How does it work?
It helps moisturise the skin and supports its natural softness and flexibility. It may make stretch marks look less noticeable, but it cannot completely remove them.

How to take/use it
Apply to clean, dry skin and gently massage until absorbed. Follow the product label for application instructions. For external use only.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness or itching may occur, especially in sensitive skin.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes and do not apply to broken, inflamed or infected skin. Stop use if irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Test on a small area first if the skin is sensitive.

title: Just-Shyne Sunscreen Lotion (24x5x50ml) Vitamin E SPF 50+ Lotion by Abbott

searchText: Just-Shyne Sunscreen Lotion (24x5x50ml) Vitamin E SPF 50+ Lotion by Abbott Abbott 2040014365
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to help protect exposed skin from sunburn and harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation. It is suitable for daily sun protection.

How does it work?
Its sunscreen ingredients form a protective layer and absorb or block UV rays reaching the skin. Vitamin E has antioxidant properties that may help support skin protection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply evenly to exposed skin as directed on the product label, preferably before sun exposure. Reapply as directed, especially after swimming, sweating or towel drying. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or rash may occur in some people.

Precautions
Avoid applying to broken or irritated skin. Stop use if a rash or irritation develops. Keep out of the eyes; rinse with water if contact occurs. Sunscreen does not provide complete protection, so avoid excessive sun exposure and use protective clothing where possible.

title: Just-Shyne Walnut Face Scrub (8x36x60ml) Walnut Face Scrub by Abbott
name: Just-Shyne Walnut Face Scrub (8x36x60ml) Walnut Face Scrub by Abbott
searchText: Just-Shyne Walnut Face Scrub (8x36x60ml) Walnut Face Scrub by Abbott Abbott 2040013648
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Walnut Face Scrub is used to gently exfoliate the face by removing surface dead skin cells and excess oil, leaving the skin feeling smoother.

How does it work?
Small walnut particles physically loosen and remove dead skin cells from the skin's surface.

How to take/use it
Apply a small amount to damp skin and massage gently with the fingertips, avoiding the eye area. Rinse thoroughly with water. Do not use on broken, sunburned or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Mild redness, dryness, stinging or skin irritation may occur, especially if rubbed too hard or used on sensitive skin.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes. Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. People with sensitive skin or a walnut allergy should use caution and consider a small patch test first.

title: K-Gard Female Intimate Wash (60x100ml) Lactic Acid, Tea Tree Oil, Neem Extract by Abbott
name: K-Gard Female Intimate Wash (60x100ml) Lactic Acid, Tea Tree Oil, Neem Extract by Abbott
searchText: K-Gard Female Intimate Wash (60x100ml) Lactic Acid, Tea Tree Oil, Neem Extract by Abbott Abbott 2040014364
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Hydrocortisone sodium injection is a corticosteroid used in hospitals for severe allergic or inflammatory conditions and when the body needs urgent replacement of the hormone cortisol, such as in adrenal insufficiency. It may also be used for other serious conditions when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone cortisol and reduces inflammation, swelling and overactive immune reactions. It also helps support the body during cortisol deficiency.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and duration depend on the condition and response to treatment.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar or blood pressure, stomach upset, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention and pain at the injection site may occur. The risk of side effects is higher with higher doses or prolonged treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body’s ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, severe swelling, vision changes or signs of a serious infection.

title: Linzopoint I.V. (24x300ml) Linezolid 600 mg, Dextrose Anhydrous 5.0% w/v IV Infusion by Abbott
name: Linzopoint I.V. (24x300ml) Linezolid 600 mg, Dextrose Anhydrous 5.0% w/v IV Infusion by Abbott
searchText: Linzopoint I.V. (24x300ml) Linezolid 600 mg, Dextrose Anhydrous 5.0% w/v IV Infusion by Abbott Abbott 2040006245
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This syrup is used to relieve cough with mucus and breathing difficulty or wheezing associated with certain respiratory conditions. It helps loosen and clear mucus and relaxes narrowed airways.

How does it work?
Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles around the airways to improve airflow. Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to cough up.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or as stated on the label. Use the measuring device provided and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not use it for longer than advised without medical guidance.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, tremors, throat irritation or palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, seizure disorder or a history of sensitivity to any ingredient. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a fast or irregular heartbeat, or an allergic reaction. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

title: Lobate Dusting Powder 100gm (4x20x100gm) Clotrimazole 1% w/w Dusting Powder by Abbott
name: Lobate Dusting Powder 100gm (4x20x100gm) Clotrimazole 1% w/w Dusting Powder by Abbott
searchText: Lobate Dusting Powder 100gm (4x20x100gm) Clotrimazole 1% w/w Dusting Powder by Abbott Abbott 2040007594
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Clotrimazole dusting powder is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as athlete’s foot, ringworm and fungal infections in skin folds.

How does it work?
It prevents fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which stops their growth and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply the powder to clean, dry, affected skin as directed on the pack or by a healthcare professional. Keep the area dry and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, burning, itching, redness or discomfort at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole. Avoid applying to the eyes or swallowing it. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops, or if the infection does not improve or becomes worse.

title: Lunaful Cream 10g (300x10g) Luliconazole 1% w/w Cream by Abbott
name: Lunaful Cream 10g (300x10g) Luliconazole 1% w/w Cream by Abbott
searchText: Lunaful Cream 10g (300x10g) Luliconazole 1% w/w Cream by Abbott Abbott 2040006245
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain Gram-positive bacteria, including some types of pneumonia, skin and soft-tissue infections, and infections caused by vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE).

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a healthcare professional. It should be used only as prescribed, and the treatment course should not be stopped without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, and changes in blood counts such as anaemia or low platelets.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any blood disorder, liver or kidney problem, or allergy to linezolid. Medicines such as antidepressants, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and some cold or decongestant medicines may interact with linezolid. Blood tests may be needed, especially during prolonged treatment. Seek medical help for unusual bruising or bleeding, severe or persistent diarrhoea, vision changes, numbness, or weakness.

title: Lunaful Cream 30g (300x30g) Luliconazole 1% w/w Cream by Abbott
name: Lunaful Cream 30g (300x30g) Luliconazole 1% w/w Cream by Abbott
searchText: Lunaful Cream 30g (300x30g) Luliconazole 1% w/w Cream by Abbott Abbott 2040011735
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Luliconazole 1% cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch. It helps relieve symptoms such as itching, redness and scaling caused by these infections.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of an important substance that fungi need to build their cell membranes. This stops the growth of the fungus and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin as directed by a doctor or the product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not cover the area with a tight dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site may occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not apply to broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Consult a doctor if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected.

title: Lunaful Spray (216x30ML) Luliconazole 1% w/w Lotion by Abbott
name: Lunaful Spray (216x30ML) Luliconazole 1% w/w Lotion by Abbott
searchText: Lunaful Spray (216x30ML) Luliconazole 1% w/w Lotion by Abbott Abbott 2040011709
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Luliconazole 1% cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch. It helps relieve symptoms such as itching, redness and scaling caused by these infections.

How does it work?
It is an antifungal medicine that blocks the growth of fungi by interfering with the formation of an essential part of their cell membrane.

How to take/use it
For use on the skin only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by the doctor or product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not swallow or apply inside the eyes, mouth or vagina. Avoid applying to broken skin unless advised by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Use only for the condition it was prescribed or recommended for.

title: Malidens 500 (40x3010) Paracetamol 500 mg by Abbott
name: Malidens 500 (40x3010) Paracetamol 500 mg by Abbott
searchText: Malidens 500 (40x3010) Paracetamol 500 mg by Abbott Abbott 2040005876
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling, such as pain affecting muscles, joints or after minor injuries or procedures.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever. Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce inflammatory swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Allergic reactions may occur rarely.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine or seek medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or asthma triggered by painkillers. Tell the doctor if taking blood thinners or other painkillers. Avoid during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically prescribed. Stop and seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash.

title: Malidens 60ml (1000m) Acetaminophen 125 mg Susp by Abbott
name: Malidens 60ml (1000m) Acetaminophen 125 mg Susp by Abbott
searchText: Malidens 60ml (1000m) Acetaminophen 125 mg Susp by Abbott Abbott 2040000340
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Acetaminophen (paracetamol) is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, body pain, toothache and aches associated with colds.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of chemicals in the brain that contribute to pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Use the measuring device provided. Do not take it with other medicines containing acetaminophen or paracetamol, and do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
It is usually well tolerated when used as directed. Nausea, vomiting or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Use only after medical advice if there is liver disease or regular alcohol use. An overdose can cause serious liver damage, even if there are no immediate symptoms. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction, severe rash, or suspected overdose.

title: Malidens 650 () Paracetamol 650 mg by Abbott
name: Malidens 650 () Paracetamol 650 mg by Abbott
searchText: Malidens 650 () Paracetamol 650 mg by Abbott Abbott 2040005875
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold and flu symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked nose and runny nose.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and pain. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion, while diphenhydramine reduces runny nose and sneezing; caffeine may enhance pain relief and reduce tiredness.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol, diphenhydramine, phenylephrine or similar decongestants.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, headache, nervousness, difficulty sleeping, or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, alcohol and activities requiring alertness until its effects are known. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, or difficulty passing urine. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, allergic reactions, or symptoms that worsen or do not improve.

title: Malidens DS 60ml (10060ml) Acetaminophen 250 mg Susp by Abbott
name: Malidens DS 60ml (10060ml) Acetaminophen 250 mg Susp by Abbott

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Acetaminophen is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache and pain from colds.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that contribute to pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Shake the suspension well and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Do not take it with other medicines containing acetaminophen or paracetamol.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur. Side effects are usually uncommon when used as directed.

Precautions
Do not exceed the recommended amount, as overdose can cause serious liver damage even before symptoms appear. Consult a doctor before use if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use, or an allergy to acetaminophen. Stop use and seek medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

title: Maxofen - MR Tablets (48x10x10's) Aceclofenac 100 mg, Paracetamol 325 mg, Chlorzoxazone 250 mg MR Tab by Abbott
name: Maxofen - MR Tablets (48x10x10's) Aceclofenac 100 mg, Paracetamol 325 mg, Chlorzoxazone 250 mg MR Tab by Abbott
searchText: Maxofen - MR Tablets (48x10x10's) Aceclofenac 100 mg, Paracetamol 325 mg, Chlorzoxazone 250 mg MR Tab by Abbott Abbott 2040013479
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful musculoskeletal conditions, such as muscle pain, joint pain, inflammation, stiffness and muscle spasms.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces inflammation and pain, while paracetamol helps relieve pain. Chlorzoxazone relaxes painful, tight muscles and helps reduce muscle spasm.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the modified-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Taking it after food may help reduce stomach discomfort. Do not take other medicines containing paracetamol or aceclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, drowsiness and headache may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery if dizzy or drowsy. Inform the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart problems, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, particularly during the last three months. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual severe weakness.

title: Maxofen New Tablets (20x40x15's) Aceclofenac 100 mg, Paracetamol 325 mg Tab by Abbott
name: Maxofen New Tablets (20x40x15's) Aceclofenac 100 mg, Paracetamol 325 mg Tab by Abbott
searchText: Maxofen New Tablets (20x40x15's) Aceclofenac 100 mg, Paracetamol 325 mg Tab by Abbott Abbott 2040013334
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions. It may also help reduce fever and general body pain.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid excessive alcohol. Do not use during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, facial swelling or breathing difficulty.

title: Maxofen-TH 4 Tablets (50x20x15's) Thiocolchicoside 4 mg, Aceclofenac 100 mg Tab by Abbott
name: Maxofen-TH 4 Tablets (50x20x15's) Thiocolchicoside 4 mg, Aceclofenac 100 mg Tab by Abbott
searchText: Maxofen-TH 4 Tablets (50x20x15's) Thiocolchicoside 4 mg, Aceclofenac 100 mg Tab by Abbott Abbott 2040013478
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful muscle spasms, stiffness and inflammation associated with musculoskeletal conditions such as back pain and other muscle or joint problems.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside helps relax tense skeletal muscles and relieve muscle spasm.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, drowsiness and headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, seizures, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid taking it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

title: Maxofen-TH 8 Tablets (50x20x15's) Thiocolchicoside 8 mg, Aceclofenac 100 mg Tab by Abbott
name: Maxofen-TH 8 Tablets (50x20x15's) Thiocolchicoside 8 mg, Aceclofenac 100 mg Tab by Abbott
searchText: Maxofen-TH 8 Tablets (50x20x15's) Thiocolchicoside 8 mg, Aceclofenac 100 mg Tab by Abbott Abbott 2040013477
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used for painful muscle spasms and pain caused by muscle, joint or other musculoskeletal conditions. It helps reduce pain, swelling and muscle stiffness.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside helps relax tight or spasming muscles.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid driving if it causes dizziness or drowsiness.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness may occur. Serious stomach bleeding, allergic reactions, liver or kidney problems and seizures are uncommon but require prompt medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, seizures, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially the later months, and while breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor. Do not combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or aspirin unless advised. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, swelling or a seizure.

title: MBKACIN 100 (16x10x8x2ml) Amikacin 100 mg/2 ml Inj by Abbott
name: MBKACIN 100 (16x10x8x2ml) Amikacin 100 mg/2 ml Inj by Abbott
searchText: MBKACIN 100 (16x10x8x2ml) Amikacin 100 mg/2 ml Inj by Abbott Abbott 2040000352
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amikacin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections caused by susceptible bacteria, including certain infections of the blood, lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, bones and joints. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amikacin kills bacteria by interfering with their ability to make essential proteins.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, body weight and kidney function. Do not self-inject or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea, vomiting and headache may occur. More serious effects can include hearing or balance problems and kidney problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and any muscle or nerve disorder. Kidney function and, when needed, hearing may be monitored during treatment. Seek medical help for reduced urine, swelling, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, severe dizziness or difficulty breathing. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that may affect the kidneys or hearing.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This topical gel is used for temporary relief of minor muscle and joint aches and pains, including discomfort related to strains, sprains or arthritis.

How does it work?
Menthol produces a cooling sensation that helps reduce the feeling of pain. Capsaicin acts on pain-sensing nerves and may reduce pain signals with repeated use.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a small amount to the affected area as directed on the product label. Wash hands after application, unless the hands are being treated. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Temporary burning, stinging, warmth, redness, itching or skin irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, nose and other sensitive areas. Do not cover tightly or apply with a heating pad. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe burning, swelling, blistering or an allergic reaction occurs.
