bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat scabies and lice infestations. It should be used only when recommended by a doctor or pharmacist.

How does it work?
Gamma benzene hexachloride kills scabies mites and lice by affecting their nervous system. Cetrimide acts as an antiseptic on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected skin exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Avoid the eyes, mouth, inside of the nose, and broken or inflamed skin. Wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated. Do not swallow or use more than recommended.

Common side effects
Temporary skin irritation, redness, burning, dryness, itching, or rash may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice in children, older adults, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or in people with a history of seizures. Avoid use on large areas, broken skin, or under airtight coverings unless specifically advised. Stop use and seek urgent medical help if severe dizziness, tremors, confusion, or seizures occur. Keep out of reach of children.

title: Alsera D 10'S (10'S) Diclofenac Sodium 50 Mg + Serratiopeptidase 10 Mg By Alkem

searchText: Alsera D 10'S (10'S) Diclofenac Sodium 50 Mg + Serratiopeptidase 10 Mg By Alkem Alkem ATAV02
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain, inflammation and swelling associated with muscle or joint injuries, arthritis, dental pain and inflammation after some procedures.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Serratiopeptidase is an enzyme that may help reduce inflammatory swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Take it with or after food and swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take it with other diclofenac or NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Serratiopeptidase may also cause stomach upset or skin rash.

Precautions
Avoid use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney or liver disease, serious heart disease, or allergy to diclofenac, aspirin or other NSAIDs. Use only on medical advice during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks and in the last 3 months. Inform the doctor about asthma triggered by painkillers, high blood pressure, bleeding problems, or use of blood thinners. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, chest pain or breathing difficulty.

title: Alsium Ccm Tablet (30'S) Calcium Citrate Malate 250Mg,Cholcecalciferal 100 Iu,Folic Acid 50Mg By Alkem

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This supplement provides calcium, vitamin D3 and folic acid. It helps support strong bones and teeth, calcium absorption, and normal red blood cell formation. It may be used when dietary intake of these nutrients is inadequate or when supplementation is recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Calcium helps maintain bones, teeth, muscles and nerves. Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium, while folic acid supports normal cell growth and red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, so ask a pharmacist about the appropriate time to take it with other medicines.

Common side effects
Constipation, gas, bloating, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, or high calcium levels. Seek advice before use with thyroid medicines, certain antibiotics, iron supplements or other calcium/vitamin D products. The listed folic acid strength is high; use this product under healthcare professional guidance, especially if there may be vitamin B12 deficiency.

title: Alsium K2 - 7 Softgel Capsules (15'S) Calcitriol 0.25 Mcg + Calcium Carbonate 625 Mg + Vitamin K2-7 45 Mcg By Alkem
name: Alsium K2 - 7 Softgel Capsules (15'S) Calcitriol 0.25 Mcg + Calcium Carbonate 625 Mg + Vitamin K2-7 45 Mcg By Alkem
searchText: Alsium K2 - 7 Softgel Capsules (15'S) Calcitriol 0.25 Mcg + Calcium Carbonate 625 Mg + Vitamin K2-7 45 Mcg By Alkem Alkem DC00000085
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used to support bone health and help manage conditions such as osteoporosis or low calcium levels, when prescribed by a doctor. It may help maintain bone strength and calcium balance.

How does it work?
Calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D, helps the body absorb calcium. Calcium supports bone strength, while vitamin K2-7 helps direct calcium toward bones and supports normal bone metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Calcium carbonate is generally better absorbed with food. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and do not use additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort or abdominal pain may occur. Excess calcium can cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness or vomiting.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or other vitamin D or calcium supplements. Use cautiously with medicines such as warfarin, thyroid medicines, iron supplements, and certain antibiotics; these may need dose separation or medical supervision. Seek medical advice if symptoms of high calcium develop.

title: Amorolkem (10G) (10 G) Amorolfine 0.25% By Alkem

searchText: Amorolkem (10G) (10 G) Amorolfine 0.25% By Alkem Alkem ASQD01
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amorolfine 0.25% is a topical antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected skin exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Keep the area clean and dry, and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or stinging at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to amorolfine or any of its ingredients. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs, or if the infection worsens or does not improve.

title: Amorolkem Cream (30 Gm ) (30 Gm) Amorolfine 0.25% By Alkem
name: Amorolkem Cream (30 Gm ) (30 Gm) Amorolfine 0.25% By Alkem
searchText: Amorolkem Cream (30 Gm ) (30 Gm) Amorolfine 0.25% By Alkem Alkem DS00000100
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amorolfine 0.25% is used on the skin to treat fungal infections such as athlete’s foot, ringworm, fungal infections of the groin or body, pityriasis versicolor and some yeast infections of the skin.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of substances that fungi need to build their cell membrane. This stops the growth and spread of the fungus.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to clean, dry, affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or the product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site. Stop use and seek medical advice if a severe rash or allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Do not apply to the eyes or swallow it. Avoid applying to severely damaged or irritated skin unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice if the infection does not improve, gets worse or keeps returning. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Keep the affected area clean and dry, and do not share towels or clothing.

title: Atrocub Injection (1 Ml) Atropine Sulphate 0.6Mg By Alkem

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Atropine sulphate is used by healthcare professionals to treat certain dangerously slow heartbeats. It may also be used in emergencies such as some types of poisoning and to reduce excessive body secretions before certain procedures.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of acetylcholine, a chemical messenger in the body. This can increase the heart rate and reduce certain secretions.

How to take/use it
This medicine should be given only by a healthcare professional. The route and dose depend on the medical condition being treated and the prescribed formulation.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, blurred vision, increased heart rate, constipation, difficulty passing urine, dizziness and reduced sweating may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about glaucoma, prostate or urinary problems, heart conditions, fever, or sensitivity to atropine. Reduced sweating can cause overheating. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, confusion, breathing difficulty, or inability to pass urine.

title: Calkem Soft (100Ml) (100 Ml) Calamine + Diphenhydramine By Alkem

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of itching and minor skin irritation, such as from insect bites, mild rashes, sunburn, or other minor skin reactions.

How does it work?
Calamine helps soothe and protect irritated skin. Diphenhydramine reduces itching by blocking the action of histamine in the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not apply to large areas, broken skin or infected skin unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Mild skin dryness, redness, burning, irritation or rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not swallow or use near the eyes. Stop use if irritation or an allergic reaction develops. Avoid covering the treated area tightly unless advised. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, widespread, worsening or do not improve.

title: Chinsunate Injection 120 Mg (10Ml Vail) (10 Ml Amp) Artesunate 120 Mg + Sodium Bicarbonate 5% W/V + Sodium Chloride 0.9% W/V By Alkem
name: Chinsunate Injection 120 Mg (10Ml Vail) (10 Ml Amp) Artesunate 120 Mg + Sodium Bicarbonate 5% W/V + Sodium Chloride 0.9% W/V By Alkem

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Artesunate injection is used under medical supervision to treat severe malaria, especially when rapid treatment is needed or oral medicines cannot be taken.

How does it work?
Artesunate rapidly kills malaria parasites in the blood, helping to reduce the severity of the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine must be reconstituted and given by a qualified healthcare professional by injection. The route, dose and treatment schedule depend on the severity of malaria and the treatment protocol. It should not be self-administered. A complete follow-on antimalarial treatment may be needed as prescribed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, fever, abdominal discomfort and injection-site discomfort may occur. Delayed loss of red blood cells (haemolytic anaemia) can occur after treatment and requires medical monitoring.

Precautions
Severe malaria is a medical emergency and requires hospital care. Tell the doctor about any previous reaction to artesunate or other antimalarial medicines. Medical follow-up may be needed for several weeks after treatment to check for delayed anaemia or other complications. Seek urgent medical attention for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe weakness, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or dark urine.

title: Chinsunate Injection (1Ml) (1 Ml Amp) Artesunate 60 Mg + Sodium Bicarbonate 5% W/V + Sodium Chloride 0.9% W/V By Alkem
name: Chinsunate Injection (1Ml) (1 Ml Amp) Artesunate 60 Mg + Sodium Bicarbonate 5% W/V + Sodium Chloride 0.9% W/V By Alkem
searchText: Chinsunate Injection (1Ml) (1 Ml Amp) Artesunate 60 Mg + Sodium Bicarbonate 5% W/V + Sodium Chloride 0.9% W/V By Alkem Alkem AIFV01
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Artesunate injection is used for the emergency treatment of severe malaria, including malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. It is usually given in a hospital or healthcare setting and followed by a suitable oral antimalarial treatment when the patient can take medicines by mouth.

How does it work?
Artesunate is rapidly converted into an active substance that kills malaria parasites in the blood, helping to reduce the severity of the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a trained healthcare professional. The supplied sodium bicarbonate and sodium chloride solutions are used to prepare the injection. The dose and treatment schedule must be decided by the treating doctor based on the severity of malaria and the patient’s condition.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, fever, chills, rash or itching, and injection-site reactions may occur. Delayed anaemia due to breakdown of red blood cells can occur after treatment.

Precautions
Severe malaria is a medical emergency and requires hospital care. Do not self-inject this medicine. Medical monitoring is needed during and after treatment, including monitoring for anaemia or other blood-related problems. Seek urgent medical attention for worsening weakness, pale skin, yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine, breathing difficulty, or signs of an allergic reaction.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cinnarizine is used to prevent and relieve motion sickness and to treat dizziness or vertigo, including symptoms such as spinning sensation, nausea and vomiting caused by inner-ear problems.

How does it work?
It reduces excessive stimulation of the balance centre in the inner ear and has an antihistamine effect, helping to control dizziness, nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than recommended. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dry mouth, indigestion, stomach discomfort and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and use caution with other medicines that cause drowsiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is Parkinson’s disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if dizziness is severe, new, persistent or associated with hearing loss, weakness or severe headache.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Clindamycin is used to treat certain bacterial infections, including serious infections caused by bacteria that are sensitive to it. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Clindamycin stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor or pharmacist. The dose, frequency, treatment duration and method of use depend on the infection and the product. Do not self-use or stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to clindamycin or similar antibiotics, or a history of colitis or severe diarrhoea after antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, even after treatment has ended. Use in newborns, premature babies, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or liver disease should be guided by a doctor.

title: Clindakem Acne Gel (20G) (20 Gm) Clindamycin Phosphate 1% W/W + Nicotinamide 4% W/W By Alkem

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat acne, including pimples and inflamed acne spots.

How does it work?
Clindamycin helps reduce acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Nicotinamide also helps reduce skin inflammation and supports acne control.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to clean, dry acne-affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips, inside of the nose, and broken or irritated skin. Wash hands after applying.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, burning, itching, irritation, or peeling at the application site.

Precautions
For external use only. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, persistent diarrhoea, or stomach cramps occur. Avoid applying other irritating skin products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Keep away from children.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to treat fungal skin infections that cause redness, itching, swelling or irritation. It should be used only when recommended by a healthcare professional, as the steroid component may mask or worsen some skin infections.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole stops the growth of fungi on the skin. Beclomethasone reduces inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not cover the area tightly unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, irritation, redness or itching at the application site. Prolonged or repeated use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Do not use on the face, skin folds, broken skin or near the eyes unless specifically advised. Do not use for an undiagnosed rash or for longer than recommended. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, spreads or does not improve. Consult a doctor before use in children, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat fungal infections that are also causing inflammation, redness, itching or irritation. It should be used only when recommended by a doctor or pharmacist, as the steroid component can mask or worsen some infections.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole stops the growth of fungi. Beclomethasone reduces inflammation, redness and itching in the affected skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not cover the area tightly unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, colour changes or stretch marks.

Precautions
Use only on the affected skin and do not use it for longer than recommended. Avoid self-treatment of undiagnosed rashes, and seek medical advice if the infection spreads, worsens or does not improve. Do not apply to broken skin, the face, groin or skin folds unless specifically advised. Stop use and seek medical help for severe irritation or an allergic reaction.

title: Clobikem Dusting Powder (100Gm) Clotrimazole 1% By Alkem
name: Clobikem Dusting Powder (100Gm) Clotrimazole 1% By Alkem

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Clotrimazole 1% is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as athlete’s foot, ringworm, jock itch and fungal skin rashes.

How does it work?
It is an antifungal medicine that damages the fungus and stops it from growing.

How to take/use it
Use on the affected skin only, following the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions. Keep the area clean and dry, and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, redness, itching, irritation or rash may occur where it is applied.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole or any ingredient in the product. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve with treatment. For external use only unless specifically directed otherwise.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Clotrimazole 1% is an antifungal medicine used on the skin to treat fungal infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch and fungal skin rashes.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents the infection from growing.

How to take/use it
Use on clean, dry skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Apply only to the affected area and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or rash at the application site.

Precautions
For external use unless specifically directed otherwise. Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole or any ingredient. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve with treatment.

title: Clobikem-S Ointment (20 Gm) Clobetasol Propionate 0.05% W/W + Salicylic Acid 3% W/W By Alkem

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used on the skin to reduce redness, swelling, itching and thick, scaly patches in inflammatory skin conditions such as psoriasis and eczema, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Clobetasol is a very potent corticosteroid that reduces skin inflammation and itching. Salicylic acid helps soften and remove thick, scaly skin so the medicine can work more effectively.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area exactly as prescribed. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not cover the treated area with a bandage or dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Burning or stinging, irritation, dryness, itching and redness may occur. Prolonged or excessive use can cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
This is a very potent steroid and should be used only on medical advice. Avoid use on the face, groin, underarms, broken skin or infected skin unless specifically directed. Do not use on large areas or for longer than prescribed. Seek medical advice if the condition worsens or shows signs of infection. Children, pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should use it only after medical advice.

title: Colikem-D Injection (2Ml) Ampoules (2Ml) Drotaverine Hydrochloride 40 Mg By Alkem
name: Colikem-D Injection (2Ml) Ampoules (2Ml) Drotaverine Hydrochloride 40 Mg By Alkem
searchText: Colikem-D Injection (2Ml) Ampoules (2Ml) Drotaverine Hydrochloride 40 Mg By Alkem Alkem AICY01
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Drotaverine is used to relieve painful cramps and spasms caused by tightening of smooth muscles. It may help with stomach and intestinal cramps, menstrual cramps, and spasms of the urinary or biliary tract.

How does it work?
It relaxes smooth muscles in the stomach, intestines, uterus, and urinary or biliary tract, helping to reduce cramping and pain.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, palpitations, and low blood pressure may occur. Allergic reactions such as rash or swelling are uncommon but require medical attention.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is low blood pressure or severe liver, kidney, or heart disease. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop using it and seek urgent help for severe dizziness, fainting, breathing difficulty, or swelling of the face or throat.

title: Colikem Spas Drops (10 Ml) Dicyclomine Hydrochloride 10 Mg + Activated Dimethicone 40 Mg By Alkem
name: Colikem Spas Drops (10 Ml) Dicyclomine Hydrochloride 10 Mg + Activated Dimethicone 40 Mg By Alkem
searchText: Colikem Spas Drops (10 Ml) Dicyclomine Hydrochloride 10 Mg + Activated Dimethicone 40 Mg By Alkem Alkem DL00000180
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve abdominal cramps or spasms, bloating and discomfort caused by excess gas, including symptoms associated with functional digestive problems such as irritable bowel syndrome.

How does it work?
Dicyclomine relaxes the muscles of the intestine to reduce painful spasms. Activated dimethicone helps combine and disperse gas bubbles, making gas easier to pass.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not take more than the recommended amount. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, nausea, constipation and drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate enlargement, intestinal blockage or severe bowel inflammation. Drowsiness or blurred vision may occur; avoid driving or operating machinery if affected. Avoid overheating because reduced sweating can occur. How does it work?
Dicyclomine relaxes spasms in the muscles of the intestine, helping reduce cramp-like pain. Simethicone helps gas bubbles combine and pass more easily, reducing bloating and fullness.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. If symptoms are severe, recurrent or do not improve, seek medical advice.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, constipation, nausea and stomach discomfort may occur. Simethicone is generally well tolerated.

Precautions
Dicyclomine may cause dizziness or blurred vision; avoid driving or operating machinery if affected. Seek medical advice before use if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate-related urinary problems, intestinal blockage or myasthenia gravis. What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid used under specialist supervision mainly for certain bone-loss conditions, including osteoporosis. It may also be used in selected blood disorders or other conditions when specifically prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It has androgen-like and anabolic effects that increase protein production and support bone and tissue formation. It may also stimulate red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the condition being treated and must be decided by the prescribing doctor. It should not be self-injected or used for bodybuilding.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in sexual desire, mood changes, injection-site discomfort, and changes in menstrual periods. Women may develop increased facial or body hair or a deeper voice.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about prostate or breast cancer, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high cholesterol, or a history of blood clots. Children require specialist monitoring because it can affect growth and puberty. Regular medical check-ups and blood tests may be needed. Seek medical advice promptly for yellowing of the skin, severe swelling, chest pain, or breathing difficulty.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as a deep injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and injection schedule depend on the condition being treated and must be decided by the prescriber.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in mood or sexual desire, injection-site discomfort, menstrual changes, increased facial or body hair, and deepening of the voice. It may also affect the liver, cholesterol levels, or prostate.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about prostate or breast cancer, liver or kidney disease, heart problems, high cholesterol, or a history of blood clots. How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by the doctor or product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not stop treatment early without medical advice.

Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation where it is applied.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not apply to broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice if the infection does not improve or keeps returning.

For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless treating the hands. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and do not cover the area unless advised.

Burning, stinging, itching, irritation, redness or dryness at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Diclofenac sodium is used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation in conditions affecting the muscles and joints, including arthritis and other painful musculoskeletal conditions.

It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use it exactly as prescribed or directed on the product label. Do not use more than recommended, and do not combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or naproxen unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Diclofenac can increase the risk of stomach bleeding, heart attack and stroke, especially with long-term or high-dose use. Avoid use during the last 3 months of pregnancy and seek medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe rash or swelling.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed or directed on the label. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. If taking it by mouth, taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not combine it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell a doctor before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAIDs. Esomeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It reduces the production of acid in the stomach, helping relieve symptoms and support healing of acid-related damage.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection or infusion into a vein by a doctor or nurse. It should not be self-administered. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and medical assessment.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain, gas and irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to esomeprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inform the doctor about all medicines being used, as esomeprazole can interact with some medicines. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash, swelling or breathing difficulty.

It helps strengthen small blood vessels and improves the ability of platelets to form a plug at the bleeding site.

How to take/use it
This injection should be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, route and duration depend on the cause and severity of bleeding.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, skin rash and discomfort at the injection site may occur. A temporary fall in blood pressure may occur, particularly if given rapidly.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to etamsylate or similar medicines, a history of blood clots, or other medical conditions. It should be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding only when prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing, facial swelling, severe rash or unusual worsening of symptoms.

Etamsylate is used to help reduce excessive bleeding, especially heavy menstrual bleeding. It may also be prescribed for certain small-vessel or capillary bleeding and to control bleeding around some medical or surgical procedures.

How does it work?
It helps improve the strength of small blood vessels and supports the early formation of a platelet plug, helping bleeding to stop. It does not replace treatment for the underlying cause of bleeding.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the prescribed dose and schedule, and do not take it for unexplained bleeding without medical advice. Seek medical attention if bleeding is heavy, persistent or keeps returning.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, headache and skin rash may occur. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction or unusual worsening of symptoms.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to etamsylate. Tell the doctor about porphyria, bleeding or clotting problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding before use. Unexplained bleeding should be medically evaluated rather than treated repeatedly with this medicine.

This medicine is used to reduce excessive bleeding, particularly heavy menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia), when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Tranexamic acid helps prevent the breakdown of blood clots, while etamsylate helps strengthen small blood vessels and support clot formation. Together, they help reduce bleeding.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the prescribed dose and duration, and do not take extra doses or continue treatment longer than advised. If heavy or unusual bleeding continues, seek medical evaluation.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of blood clots, stroke, kidney disease, or vision problems before use. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathlessness, sudden weakness, severe leg pain or swelling, or changes in vision. Do not use it to treat unexplained bleeding without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat anaemia caused by iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 deficiency, when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It provides iron needed to make haemoglobin and red blood cells. Folic acid and vitamin B12 support normal red blood cell formation.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed or directed on the label. Do not take more than recommended. Follow the advice of a healthcare professional about timing with food and other medicines.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Do not self-treat unexplained anaemia; the cause should be assessed. Tell the doctor if there is iron overload, another blood disorder, or an allergy to any ingredient. Iron-containing products can be harmful in overdose—keep out of reach of children. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, including antacids, calcium supplements and antibiotics.

Used to prevent or treat iron-deficiency anaemia and support red blood cell production when iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 supplementation is needed.

How does it work?
It provides iron needed to make haemoglobin, along with folic acid and vitamin B12, which support the formation of healthy red blood cells.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended. If it causes stomach upset, ask a healthcare professional whether it should be taken with food. Keep it out of the reach of children.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dark or black stools may occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if the cause of anaemia is unknown or if there is iron overload or a condition that causes excess iron. What is it used for?
Iron sucrose is used to treat iron-deficiency anaemia, especially when iron tablets are not effective, cannot be tolerated, or iron replacement is needed under medical supervision. It is commonly used in people with chronic kidney disease and in other situations decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
It supplies iron to the body, helping restore iron stores and support the production of haemoglobin and red blood cells.

How to take/use it
Iron sucrose is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and number of treatments depend on the severity of iron deficiency and the individual’s medical condition. It is not for self-injection or oral use.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It may also be used for hives (urticaria) and related itching when prescribed.

How does it work?
It is an antihistamine that blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the package instructions. Swallow the tablet with water. Avoid taking it with fruit juice, such as apple, orange or grapefruit juice. Headache, nausea, dizziness and tiredness may occur. Drowsiness is uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek medical advice if allergy symptoms are severe, unusual or do not improve.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It is also used to relieve itching and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce itching, sneezing, runny nose and other allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the label. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it with apple, orange or grapefruit juice, as these may reduce its effect. Headache, nausea, dizziness and mild drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek medical advice if symptoms do not improve or if an allergic reaction develops.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes caused by allergies.

How does it work?
Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can contribute to nasal swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed or directed on the label. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Avoid taking it with fruit juice unless advised by a healthcare professional. Do not use it to treat a sudden asthma attack.

It helps prevent blood clots from breaking down too quickly, which helps reduce bleeding.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more than the prescribed amount. The dose and treatment duration depend on the cause and severity of bleeding.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of blood clots, kidney disease, vision problems or an allergy to tranexamic acid. Used to help prevent or treat calcium and vitamin D deficiency and support healthy bones. It may be prescribed when the body needs active vitamin D along with calcium; use it only for the purpose advised by the doctor.

Calcitriol is an active form of vitamin D that helps the body absorb and use calcium. Calcium supports bone strength, while zinc contributes to normal tissue and immune function.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, preferably with food if advised, and swallow with water. Do not take extra calcium or vitamin D supplements unless recommended by a doctor. Do not exceed the prescribed amount.

Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort, or vomiting may occur. Excess calcium can cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness, or confusion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or other disorders affecting calcium or vitamin D. Avoid taking other calcium- or vitamin D-containing products without medical advice. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excess calcium occur. How does it work?
It relaxes the smooth muscles in the stomach, intestines and urinary tract, helping to reduce spasms and cramping.

How to take/use it
Use it only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. The dose, frequency and route of use depend on the formulation and medical condition. Do not use it for persistent or unexplained abdominal pain without medical advice.

Dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, fast heartbeat, dizziness and difficulty passing urine may occur.

Seek medical advice before use if there is glaucoma, prostate-related difficulty passing urine, suspected bowel blockage, severe constipation, myasthenia gravis or a fast heartbeat. What is it used for?
Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, especially when other suitable antibiotics cannot be used. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Use only when prescribed by a doctor. Take or use it exactly as directed on the prescription or product label, and complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise. Do not share it or use leftover medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, and skin rash may occur. Rarely, it can cause serious blood-related problems, including bone-marrow suppression.

Precautions
Chloramphenicol should be used under medical supervision because it can rarely cause serious or delayed blood disorders. Tell the doctor about any previous blood disorder, liver disease, medicine allergy, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical advice for unusual bruising or bleeding, persistent fever, sore throat, marked weakness, or pale skin. Keep it away from newborns and young infants unless specifically prescribed.

It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

Take it only on a doctor's prescription and follow the prescribed dose and duration. Swallow the tablet or capsule with water and complete the full course, unless the doctor tells otherwise. Do not self-medicate or share this medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and temporary changes in blood-cell counts may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, previous blood disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Medical monitoring, including blood tests, may be needed during treatment. Seek urgent medical advice for unusual bruising or bleeding, unusual tiredness, pale skin, fever, sore throat or severe diarrhoea. Do not use it for minor infections unless specifically prescribed.

Betamethasone sodium phosphate is a corticosteroid injection used under medical supervision to reduce inflammation and severe allergic or immune-related reactions. The exact condition and treatment plan depend on the doctor's diagnosis.

It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation, swelling and allergic reactions.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, injection site and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Pain or discomfort at the injection site, increased appetite, indigestion, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention and increased blood sugar may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems or any current infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infection and may mask infection symptoms. Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding and any medicines being taken. Do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

It adds beneficial bacteria to the intestine and helps support the normal balance of gut microorganisms.

Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If diarrhoea is severe, persistent, or associated with dehydration, seek medical advice.

Usually well tolerated. Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort, nausea, or temporary changes in bowel movements may occur.

Seek medical advice before use if immunocompromised, seriously ill, or using a central venous catheter, as rare bloodstream infections have been reported with probiotic products. It replaces B vitamins needed for nerve function, red blood cell formation and energy metabolism.

Inform the doctor about other medicines and medical conditions before use. Avoid prolonged use of high doses unless medically advised, as excess vitamin B6 may cause nerve damage. Seek medical advice if numbness, tingling or weakness persists or worsens.

Omeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be used for stomach or duodenal ulcers and other acid-related conditions when prescribed.

It reduces the production of acid in the stomach by blocking the stomach’s acid-producing pumps.

Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing and duration, even if symptoms improve.

Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, allergy to omeprazole or other medicines, or if it is being used for a long period. Omeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps stomach contents move forward and can help relieve nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the medicine with water and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Headache, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation, nausea, dry mouth or dizziness.

Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, or a history of electrolyte imbalance. It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them open and allowing air to move more easily into and out of the lungs.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the recommended times. Do not take extra doses or stop treatment without medical advice. Avoid taking other theophylline-containing medicines unless advised by a doctor. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the prescriber or pharmacist.

Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, shakiness and fast or pounding heartbeat.

Use only under medical supervision because theophylline levels can become too high. It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents the fungus from growing.

How to take/use it
Use the cream, shampoo or other formulation exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site.

For external use unless the product label or healthcare professional says otherwise. Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole or any ingredient. Avoid applying to the eyes or severely damaged skin. It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The route of use depends on the prescribed formulation; ketorolac 30 mg may be given by a healthcare professional. Do not self-inject or change the dose without medical advice.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by affecting the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, as this may trigger seizures. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, nausea, irritability, agitation, and mood or behaviour changes.

Precautions
Seek medical advice if there are severe mood changes, depression, aggression, confusion, or thoughts of self-harm. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the medicine label. It may generally be taken with or without food. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness or sleepiness, tiredness, headache, and dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
Drowsiness may affect driving or operating machinery; avoid alcohol if it increases sleepiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

The exact action depends on the Ayurvedic ingredients in the product. The ingredients were not provided, so a specific mechanism cannot be confirmed.

Use only as directed on the product label or by an Ayurvedic doctor or healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Specific common side effects cannot be confirmed without knowing the ingredients. Some people may experience digestive discomfort with herbal products.

It changes the composition of bile, helping bile flow more easily and reducing the amount of cholesterol in bile. This can help protect liver cells and gradually dissolve some cholesterol gallstones.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the medicine with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Treatment may require regular liver tests and follow-up.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, loose stools, stomach discomfort, abdominal pain, nausea or indigestion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about gallbladder inflammation, blocked bile ducts, frequent biliary pain or liver disease. It is not suitable for all types of gallstones. How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Use only the formulation intended for the affected area and follow the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions. Clean the area as directed and apply externally. Do not swallow it or use skin preparations in the eyes, mouth or other body areas unless the product is specifically made for that purpose.

Common side effects
Temporary skin irritation, redness, dryness or staining may occur. Rarely, an allergic reaction can occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to povidone iodine or any ingredient. Keep it away from the eyes and do not apply repeatedly over large areas, deep wounds or severe burns unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice for worsening redness, swelling, pain, pus or fever. People with thyroid problems, those taking lithium, pregnant or breastfeeding women, and infants should seek advice before repeated or extensive use.

How does it work?
Povidone iodine acts as an antiseptic against a wide range of germs. Ornidazole works against certain anaerobic bacteria and protozoa.

How to take/use it
Use only in the form, route and duration prescribed. Do not swallow or apply it to the eyes unless specifically instructed. Complete the prescribed treatment unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Application-site irritation, burning or itching; nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache or dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about thyroid problems, liver disease, iodine allergy, neurological disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid alcohol during treatment unless a doctor advises otherwise. Stop use and seek medical advice for severe irritation, rash, numbness, tingling, seizures or unusual confusion.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Povidone iodine is an antiseptic used to clean the skin and help prevent infection in minor cuts, grazes, and burns. Some products are also used to prepare the skin before medical procedures; use depends on the product formulation.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or inactivates many bacteria, viruses, fungi, and other germs on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only unless the product is specifically labelled for another use. Apply or use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not swallow it. Do not use on large areas, deep wounds, or severe burns without medical advice.

Common side effects
Temporary skin irritation, redness, itching, or dryness. Stop using it and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine or other ingredients. Ask a healthcare professional before repeated or prolonged use, use on large areas, or use in people with thyroid disease, kidney problems, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Keep away from children. Seek medical advice if a wound is deep, extensive, badly burned, or shows signs of infection.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Povidone iodine is an antiseptic used to clean minor cuts, scrapes and superficial wounds and to help prevent infection. Its use depends on the product formulation; some products may be intended for other areas of the body.

How does it work?
It slowly releases iodine, which kills or limits the growth of many bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. For products intended for skin, apply to the affected area as instructed. Do not swallow or use inside the body unless the product is specifically labelled for that purpose. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Temporary skin irritation, redness, dryness or stinging may occur. Rarely, an allergic reaction can develop.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to iodine or povidone iodine. Avoid prolonged use or applying to large areas unless advised by a healthcare professional. Ask a doctor before use if there is thyroid disease, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or in young children. Seek medical advice for deep, severe or heavily contaminated wounds, burns, or signs of infection.

title: Prednikem 125 (Vial) (Vial) Methylprednisolone 125 Mg By Alkem

searchText: Prednikem 125 (Vial) (Vial) Methylprednisolone 125 Mg By Alkem Alkem AIQJ11
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and calm an overactive immune response. It may be prescribed for inflammatory, allergic, respiratory, or autoimmune conditions; the exact use depends on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune activity.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. Depending on the product, it may be taken by mouth or administered by a healthcare professional. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice, especially after prolonged use.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention, increased blood sugar, and increased blood pressure. It may also increase the risk of infections.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions, liver or kidney problems, or any ongoing infection. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and ask the doctor before receiving vaccines. Seek medical advice for signs of infection, severe mood changes, vision problems, or severe stomach pain.

title: Prednikem 40 (Vial) (Vial) Methylprednisolone 40 Mg By Alkem

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune reactions. It may be prescribed for conditions such as severe allergies, asthma or other inflammatory, autoimmune, skin, joint and respiratory conditions, depending on medical advice.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of the immune system and decreases inflammation, swelling and allergic reactions.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. The dose, treatment length and method of use depend on the condition and the product form. Take oral medicine with food if advised. Do not stop treatment suddenly, especially after prolonged use, unless directed by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, facial puffiness, fluid retention, increased blood sugar and increased blood pressure. It may also increase the risk of infections.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, eye problems, mental health conditions or any current infection. Avoid close contact with people who have infections and ask a doctor before receiving vaccines. Seek medical advice for signs of infection or severe mood changes. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and suppress an overactive immune response. It may be prescribed for allergic, inflammatory, autoimmune, skin, joint, or respiratory conditions, depending on the doctor's assessment.

How does it work?
It acts like naturally occurring corticosteroid hormones and reduces inflammation, swelling, and immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, preferably with food or milk to reduce stomach upset. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially if it has been used for a longer period. Follow the prescribed schedule carefully.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, fluid retention, and increased blood sugar may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems, eye disease, or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce resistance to infection and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and ask the doctor before receiving vaccines. Seek medical advice for severe mood changes, vision problems, signs of infection, or unusual swelling.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune reactions in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma, arthritis, skin disorders and other inflammatory or autoimmune conditions. Its exact use depends on the condition being treated.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Take it with food or milk if it causes stomach upset. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice, especially after prolonged use.

Common side effects
Increased appetite, indigestion, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, fluid retention and increased blood sugar may occur. The risk of side effects increases with higher doses or longer treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health problems or an ongoing infection. This medicine can reduce resistance to infection and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically approved by a doctor. Long-term treatment may require medical monitoring.

title: Pyricool Injection (2Ml) Ampoule (2 Ml Amp) Paracetamol 150 Mg By Alkem

searchText: Pyricool Injection (2Ml) Ampoule (2 Ml Amp) Paracetamol 150 Mg By Alkem Alkem AIDH11
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Paracetamol 150 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache or pain associated with colds.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of chemicals in the body that cause pain and fever, helping lower temperature and relieve discomfort.

How to take/use it
Use only the dose and frequency stated on the product label or advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol. Do not use it for longer than recommended without medical advice.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used correctly. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not exceed the recommended dose, as too much paracetamol can cause serious liver damage. Seek medical advice before use if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use, or use of other paracetamol-containing medicines. Stop use and seek urgent medical help for a severe rash, breathing difficulty, or symptoms of overdose, even if feeling well.

title: Qmax Iv Injection (100Ml) (100 Ml) Ofloxacin 200 Mg By Alkem
name: Qmax Iv Injection (100Ml) (100 Ml) Ofloxacin 200 Mg By Alkem
searchText: Qmax Iv Injection (100Ml) (100 Ml) Ofloxacin 200 Mg By Alkem Alkem AIDD01
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Ofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the urinary tract, lungs, skin, and other parts of the body. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking enzymes needed for bacterial DNA replication and growth.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor and complete the prescribed course. Swallow with water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium, or zinc; follow the advised time gap. Do not share this medicine or use leftover tablets.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, and difficulty sleeping may occur. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, or a serious allergic reaction.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, tendon problems, seizures, heart-rhythm problems, myasthenia gravis, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Avoid unnecessary sun exposure. Stop the medicine and seek medical advice if tendon pain or swelling develops. Use only under medical supervision, especially in children and older adults.

title: Rabalkem Injection (20Mg) Vial (Vial) Rabeprazole Sodium 20 Mg By Alkem
name: Rabalkem Injection (20Mg) Vial (Vial) Rabeprazole Sodium 20 Mg By Alkem
searchText: Rabalkem Injection (20Mg) Vial (Vial) Rabeprazole Sodium 20 Mg By Alkem Alkem AIFS01
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Rabeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid, helping treat acidity, heartburn and acid reflux (GERD). It is also used for stomach or duodenal ulcers and may be combined with antibiotics to treat Helicobacter pylori infection, as prescribed.

How does it work?
It blocks a stomach enzyme called the proton pump, reducing the production of stomach acid.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed or directed on the label. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing and duration, even if symptoms improve.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to rabeprazole or other acid-reducing medicines, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and liver disease. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms. Long-term use may require medical monitoring, especially for low magnesium or vitamin B12. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, particularly warfarin, digoxin, high-dose methotrexate and some HIV medicines.

title: Rg-Kem Sachet (6.5G) L-Arginine 3 G + Proanthocyanidin 75 Mg By Alkem

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This is a nutritional supplement used to support nitric oxide production, healthy blood circulation and antioxidant protection. It is not a substitute for treatment of any diagnosed medical condition.

How does it work?
L-arginine is an amino acid used by the body to produce nitric oxide, which helps relax blood vessels. Proanthocyanidins are antioxidant plant compounds that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Take with water, and follow any food-related instructions on the label.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating, diarrhoea, headache or dizziness may occur. It may lower blood pressure in some people.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is low blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, liver disease or a history of herpes. Seek advice before use with blood-pressure medicines, nitrates, erectile-dysfunction medicines or blood thinners. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe dizziness, allergic symptoms or other serious reactions occur.

title: Rifaxitab - 200 Tablets (10'S) (10'S) Rifaximin 200 Mg By Alkem

searchText: Rifaxitab - 200 Tablets (10'S) (10'S) Rifaximin 200 Mg By Alkem Alkem DT00000247
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Rifaximin is an intestinal antibiotic used mainly to treat certain bacterial causes of diarrhoea, including travellers’ diarrhoea. It may also be prescribed for other bowel conditions when specifically advised by a doctor.

How does it work?
It acts mainly inside the intestine and stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins needed for their growth.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not self-medicate for diarrhoea without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach or abdominal pain, headache, dizziness and gas may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics. Seek medical advice before use if there is severe liver disease. It may not be suitable for diarrhoea with fever or blood in the stool. Contact a doctor if diarrhoea worsens, persists or returns after treatment, as antibiotic-associated diarrhoea can occur.

title: Rifaxitab - 400 Tablets (10'S) (10'S) Rifaximin 400 Mg By Alkem

searchText: Rifaxitab - 400 Tablets (10'S) (10'S) Rifaximin 400 Mg By Alkem Alkem DT00000251
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Rifaximin is an intestinal antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections of the digestive tract, including some types of bacterial diarrhoea. It may also be prescribed in some people with liver disease to help reduce episodes of confusion caused by hepatic encephalopathy.

How does it work?
It works mainly inside the intestines by stopping susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins needed for their growth. Very little of the medicine is absorbed into the bloodstream.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional tells otherwise. Do not use it for self-treatment of diarrhoea without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, abdominal pain or discomfort, bloating, flatulence, headache, dizziness and constipation may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics. Seek medical advice promptly for diarrhoea with blood, high fever, severe abdominal pain, dehydration, or diarrhoea that worsens or continues after treatment. Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Use only under medical supervision, especially for prolonged or repeated courses.

title: Rifaxitab - 550 Tablets (10'S) (10'S) Rifaximin 550 Mg By Alkem
name: Rifaxitab - 550 Tablets (10'S) (10'S) Rifaximin 550 Mg By Alkem
searchText: Rifaxitab - 550 Tablets (10'S) (10'S) Rifaximin 550 Mg By Alkem Alkem DT00000246
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Rifaximin 550 mg is mainly used to reduce the risk of repeated episodes of hepatic encephalopathy, a brain-related complication of severe liver disease. It may also be prescribed for irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhoea (IBS-D) in selected patients.

How does it work?
It is an antibiotic that works mainly inside the intestine. It reduces certain harmful bacteria and the toxins they produce, while very little of the medicine is absorbed into the bloodstream.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course. Swallow the tablet with water; it may generally be taken with or without food unless advised otherwise. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, dizziness, stomach or abdominal pain, constipation, tiredness and swelling of the hands or feet may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, allergies to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, fever, blood in the stool, worsening abdominal pain, or signs of an allergic reaction. Use only under medical supervision, especially in severe liver disease.

title: Ronflox-Lb Tablets (10'S) (10S) Ofloxacin 200 Mg + Lactic Acid Bacillus 60 Million Spores By Alkem
name: Ronflox-Lb Tablets (10'S) (10S) Ofloxacin 200 Mg + Lactic Acid Bacillus 60 Million Spores By Alkem
searchText: Ronflox-Lb Tablets (10'S) (10S) Ofloxacin 200 Mg + Lactic Acid Bacillus 60 Million Spores By Alkem Alkem ATOC01
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat bacterial infections caused by bacteria that are sensitive to ofloxacin. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Lactic acid bacillus helps support healthy intestinal bacteria during antibiotic treatment.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin kills bacteria by blocking enzymes needed for bacterial growth and reproduction. Lactic acid bacillus is a probiotic that helps maintain the normal balance of bacteria in the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not take it together with antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron or calcium unless advised by a doctor or pharmacist, as they may reduce absorption.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, indigestion, headache, dizziness and sleep disturbance may occur. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, allergic reactions, tendon pain or swelling, numbness, tingling or unusual weakness.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney disease, seizure disorders, heart rhythm problems, diabetes, tendon problems or previous reaction to quinolone antibiotics. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizzy. Avoid unnecessary sun exposure and use sun protection. Use in children and older adults only when specifically prescribed.

title: Ronflox-Mz Suspension (30Ml) (30 Ml) Ofloxacin 50 Mg + Metronidazole 120 Mg + Simethicone 10 Mg By Alkem
name: Ronflox-Mz Suspension (30Ml) (30 Ml) Ofloxacin 50 Mg + Metronidazole 120 Mg + Simethicone 10 Mg By Alkem
searchText: Ronflox-Mz Suspension (30Ml) (30 Ml) Ofloxacin 50 Mg + Metronidazole 120 Mg + Simethicone 10 Mg By Alkem Alkem ALOC01
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to treat certain bacterial and protozoal infections of the digestive tract that may cause diarrhoea, loose motions, dysentery and abdominal gas. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin and metronidazole work against different bacteria and parasites that can cause intestinal infections. Simethicone helps break up gas bubbles and may relieve bloating and abdominal discomfort.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron or calcium; follow the prescriber’s instructions for spacing them. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, metallic taste and loss of appetite.

Precautions
Do not self-medicate or use it for every episode of diarrhoea. Tell the healthcare professional about pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver disease, seizures, heart-rhythm problems, tendon disorders or previous reactions to antibiotics. Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe rash, breathing difficulty or unusual palpitations.

title: Sengvital - 9G 10'S (Soft Gel Capsules) (10'S) Antioxidants With Multivitamin & Multimineral By Alkem
name: Sengvital - 9G 10'S (Soft Gel Capsules) (10'S) Antioxidants With Multivitamin & Multimineral By Alkem
