bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide a combination of vitamins, minerals and antioxidant nutrients, helping support normal nutritional needs and prevent deficiencies when dietary intake is inadequate.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamins and minerals required for normal body functions. Antioxidant nutrients help protect cells from oxidative damage.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount or take it with other multivitamin products unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea may occur, depending on the ingredients.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list for allergies and avoid duplicate vitamin or mineral supplements. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is kidney or liver disease or regular medicine use. Keep out of reach of children; products containing iron can be dangerous if accidentally taken in excess.

title: Sofrakem (15G) (15 G) Fradiomycin Sulphate 5 Mg By Alkem
name: Sofrakem (15G) (15 G) Fradiomycin Sulphate 5 Mg By Alkem
searchText: Sofrakem (15G) (15 G) Fradiomycin Sulphate 5 Mg By Alkem Alkem ASHC02
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Fradiomycin is an antibacterial antibiotic used to treat susceptible bacterial infections. The exact use depends on the product formulation and the area being treated. It does not treat viral or fungal infections.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
Use only by the route and in the amount stated on the product label or prescribed by a doctor. The supplied information does not specify the formulation, dose, frequency or treatment duration. Do not use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Depending on the formulation, local irritation, redness, itching or skin rash may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if signs of a serious allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to fradiomycin, neomycin or related aminoglycoside antibiotics. Use only as directed, particularly on large, broken or damaged areas of skin, or near the eyes and ears. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve.

title: Sulbakem-C 1.5 G Injection (Vial) (20 Ml Vial) Cefoperazone 1 G + Sulbactam 500 Mg By Alkem
name: Sulbakem-C 1.5 G Injection (Vial) (20 Ml Vial) Cefoperazone 1 G + Sulbactam 500 Mg By Alkem
searchText: Sulbakem-C 1.5 G Injection (Vial) (20 Ml Vial) Cefoperazone 1 G + Sulbactam 500 Mg By Alkem Alkem AIRH11
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cefoperazone with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin and soft tissues, blood, and bile passages. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefoperazone kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps cefoperazone work against bacteria that produce enzymes capable of reducing the effect of some antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney or liver function. Complete the prescribed course and do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash, and pain or redness at the injection site may occur. Changes in liver test results or blood counts can also occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefoperazone, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or related antibiotics. Inform the doctor about liver or kidney disease, bleeding problems, or use of blood-thinning medicines. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for a few days after the last dose. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

title: Thrombostrong Ointment (20 Gm) Heparin Sodium + Benzyl Nicotinate By Alkem
name: Thrombostrong Ointment (20 Gm) Heparin Sodium + Benzyl Nicotinate By Alkem
searchText: Thrombostrong Ointment (20 Gm) Heparin Sodium + Benzyl Nicotinate By Alkem Alkem DS00000073
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used on the skin to help reduce superficial vein inflammation, swelling, bruising and blood collections under the skin, such as haematomas after minor injury.

How does it work?
Heparin helps limit local clot formation and supports the body’s removal of blood collected under the skin. Benzyl nicotinate increases local blood flow, which may help reduce swelling and discomfort.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area and gently spread it as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not apply to open, infected or damaged skin, and wash hands after use.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or a burning sensation at the application site. Unusual bruising or bleeding can rarely occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to heparin or any ingredient. Do not apply to wounds, mucous membranes or near the eyes. Use medical advice if there is a bleeding disorder, low platelet count, or use of blood-thinning medicines. Seek urgent medical care for sudden severe leg swelling or pain, chest pain or breathing difficulty.

title: Zincopunch Syrup (60 Ml) Zinc Gluconate 20 Mg (Elemental Zinc) By Alkem
name: Zincopunch Syrup (60 Ml) Zinc Gluconate 20 Mg (Elemental Zinc) By Alkem
searchText: Zincopunch Syrup (60 Ml) Zinc Gluconate 20 Mg (Elemental Zinc) By Alkem Alkem DL00000181
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Zinc gluconate is used to prevent or treat zinc deficiency. Zinc deficiency may affect immunity, growth, wound healing and general health. Use it for a diagnosed or suspected deficiency as advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It supplies elemental zinc, an essential mineral needed for normal immune function, cell growth, enzyme activity and wound healing.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. This product provides 20 mg of elemental zinc per stated dose. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. If it causes stomach upset, taking it with food may help.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, abdominal cramps, diarrhoea and a metallic taste may occur, especially with higher amounts.

Precautions
Do not exceed the recommended amount. Long-term or excessive zinc use can cause copper deficiency and other health problems. Zinc can reduce the absorption of some antibiotics and penicillamine; separate doses as advised by a healthcare professional. Tell a healthcare professional about all medicines and supplements being used, particularly during pregnancy, breastfeeding or if there is a medical condition.

Clobetasol reduces skin inflammation and itching. Ketoconazole and iodochlorhydroxyquinoline act against fungi, while gentamicin acts against certain bacteria.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and fever.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably after food, with water. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking it with other painkillers or anti-inflammatory medicines unless a doctor recommends this.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if there is liver disease or a previous serious reaction to nimesulide. Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid excessive alcohol. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, unusual tiredness, severe stomach pain, black stools, breathing difficulty or swelling.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Measure the syrup with an accurate measuring device. Do not take more than recommended or combine it with other cough, cold, antihistamine or decongestant medicines.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, headache, nervousness, increased blood pressure or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery because drowsiness or dizziness may occur. Precautions

What is it used for?
Metformin is mainly used to control high blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes. It may be used alone or with other diabetes medicines, along with a suitable diet and exercise plan.

How does it work?
It lowers the amount of glucose made by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively. This helps reduce blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or after food, to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain or discomfort, gas, indigestion and reduced appetite. These often improve as the body adjusts.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heart failure, heavy alcohol use, or any serious infection or dehydration. Kidney function should be checked during treatment. Metformin may need to be stopped temporarily before some scans using injected contrast dye or during major surgery, as advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for severe weakness, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting or unusual drowsiness.

How to take/use it

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heavy alcohol use, severe infection, dehydration, or heart failure. Kidney function should be checked during treatment. It reduces the liver's production of cholesterol and helps the liver remove more LDL cholesterol from the blood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Continue it regularly and do not stop without medical advice. Follow the recommended diet and exercise plan.

Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems, or a history of muscle problems. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cilnidipine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It may help reduce the risk of complications related to uncontrolled blood pressure.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens the blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily and lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, with or without food. Take it at the same time each day and do not stop it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, palpitations, and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur.

Precautions
It may cause dizziness, especially when starting treatment; rise slowly from sitting or lying down. Inform the doctor if there is very low blood pressure, heart disease, or liver or kidney problems. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Regular blood pressure monitoring is recommended.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other complications.

How does it work?
Cilnidipine relaxes and widens blood vessels, while nebivolol slows the heart rate and reduces the heart’s workload. Together, they help lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow it with water and do not stop it suddenly without medical advice. Do not take an extra dose if one is missed; follow the prescriber’s instructions.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, low blood pressure, slow heartbeat, ankle swelling, nausea or constipation may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about asthma or breathing problems, a slow heartbeat, heart block, heart failure, diabetes, liver or kidney disease, or circulation problems. It may mask some warning signs of low blood sugar. Avoid driving if dizzy, and inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding or other medicines being used.

What is it used for?
Used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering blood pressure helps reduce the risk of complications such as heart attack and stroke.

How does it work?
Cilnidipine relaxes and widens blood vessels, while telmisartan blocks the action of a hormone that causes blood vessels to tighten. Together, they help blood flow more easily and lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop taking it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the doctor’s or pharmacist’s advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, ankle or leg swelling, weakness, and low blood pressure may occur. Contact a doctor if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, or high potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor. Dizziness may occur, especially when starting treatment; rise slowly and avoid driving if affected. Regular blood pressure, kidney function, and potassium monitoring may be recommended.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat bacterial infections of the eye or ear when inflammation is also present. The exact use depends on whether the product is intended for the eye or ear, as stated on the label or prescription.

How does it work?
Ciprofloxacin kills or stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation, redness and swelling.

How to take/use it
Use only in the eye or ear and by the route stated on the label or prescribed by the doctor. Follow the prescribed instructions; do not use more often or for longer than advised. Wash hands before use and do not touch the dropper tip to the eye, ear or any surface. Do not use it for another condition without medical advice.

Common side effects
Temporary burning, stinging, itching, irritation or redness at the application site may occur. Eye use may briefly cause blurred vision. Ear use may cause temporary discomfort.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ciprofloxacin, dexamethasone or similar medicines. Corticosteroids may worsen or mask some viral or fungal infections and prolonged eye use may increase eye pressure or delay healing. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, do not improve, or if severe pain, swelling, rash or vision changes occur.

What is it used for?
This medicine is prescribed to support memory, thinking and recovery in certain neurological conditions, including cognitive problems after stroke or brain injury. It should be used only under medical supervision.

Citicoline supports the formation and maintenance of nerve-cell membranes and may support brain function. Piracetam affects nerve-cell communication and membrane function.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, nervousness, difficulty sleeping, nausea and stomach upset may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, a history of bleeding or seizures, or if taking blood thinners. Medical advice is important during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek advice if unusual bleeding, severe dizziness or worsening symptoms occur.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Dapagliflozin is used with diet and exercise to help control blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may also be prescribed to reduce the risk of worsening heart failure and progression of certain types of chronic kidney disease.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove excess glucose and sodium from the body through urine. This lowers blood sugar and can reduce extra fluid and pressure on the heart and kidneys.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Drink adequate fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, thirst, dehydration, dizziness, urinary tract infections, and fungal infections around the genitals. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, low blood pressure, dehydration, or recurrent urinary or genital infections. Seek urgent medical help for severe nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, breathing difficulty, or confusion, as these may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis. It may need to be stopped temporarily during serious illness, prolonged fasting, or before surgery—follow medical advice. It is not generally used for type 1 diabetes. Discuss use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Febuxostat is used to lower high uric acid levels in adults with gout. It helps prevent gout attacks and complications caused by uric acid crystals, but it does not provide immediate relief during an acute gout attack.

How does it work?
It blocks xanthine oxidase, an enzyme involved in producing uric acid. This lowers uric acid levels in the blood and helps prevent crystal build-up in the joints.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Continue taking it regularly even if feeling well. Do not stop it without medical advice. Gout attacks can occur when treatment is first started; follow the prescribed treatment for such attacks.

Common side effects
Nausea, joint pain or a gout flare, rash, and changes in liver function tests may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about heart disease, stroke, liver disease, or kidney problems. Febuxostat may increase cardiovascular risk in some people. It should not be taken with azathioprine or mercaptopurine unless specifically directed by a specialist. Seek urgent medical help for severe rash, facial swelling, breathing difficulty, chest pain, or sudden weakness.

Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as this may worsen seizures. If a dose is missed or vomiting occurs after taking it, follow the prescriber's instructions.

What is it used for?
Metoprolol tartrate is used to treat high blood pressure and certain heart conditions, such as angina (heart-related chest pain), fast or irregular heartbeat, and after a heart attack. It may also be prescribed for other heart-related conditions by a doctor.

How does it work?
It is a beta-blocker that slows the heartbeat and reduces the force with which the heart pumps. This lowers blood pressure and reduces the heart’s workload.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or immediately after food, and at the same time each day. Swallow with water. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice, as this may worsen heart problems.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, slow heartbeat, headache, cold hands or feet, nausea, and stomach upset.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is asthma or other breathing disease, a very slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart failure, circulation problems, or diabetes. It may hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Avoid driving if dizzy, and seek medical advice for fainting, severe breathing difficulty, or an unusually slow heartbeat.

This medicine helps remove excess salt and water from the body and is used to reduce swelling or fluid retention related to conditions such as heart failure, liver disease or kidney problems. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Torsemide increases urine production, helping the body remove excess fluid. Spironolactone also removes fluid while helping the body retain potassium.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may increase urination, so avoid taking it close to bedtime unless directed otherwise. Do not change the dose or stop it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist and do not double the next dose.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, low blood pressure, dehydration, weakness, nausea and changes in blood potassium or sodium levels. Spironolactone may also cause breast tenderness or enlargement.

Precautions
Regular blood tests may be needed to check kidney function and electrolytes, especially potassium. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, high potassium or Addison’s disease. Avoid potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Inform the doctor about use of blood-pressure medicines, other diuretics, painkillers such as ibuprofen, or lithium. Seek medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, very low urine output, confusion, or an irregular heartbeat.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used for certain liver and bile-flow conditions, including primary biliary cholangitis. It may also be prescribed to dissolve selected cholesterol gallstones when suitable.

How does it work?
It changes the composition of bile, helping reduce cholesterol build-up and improve bile flow. It may also help protect liver cells from the effects of harmful bile acids.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water. Follow the prescribed timing and treatment duration, and do not stop it without medical advice. The medicine may need to be taken for a long period and works only for suitable types of gallstones.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea or loose stools, abdominal discomfort, nausea, and itching may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is blockage of the bile ducts, acute gallbladder inflammation, or significant liver disease. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines being taken. Antacids containing aluminium and some cholesterol-lowering bile acid medicines may reduce its absorption and may need to be taken separately.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to treat certain liver and bile-flow disorders, including primary biliary cholangitis. It may also be prescribed to dissolve selected cholesterol gallstones when the gallbladder is functioning properly.

How does it work?
It improves the flow and composition of bile, making bile less likely to damage liver cells and less likely to form cholesterol deposits. This can help dissolve some cholesterol gallstones over time.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Take it regularly and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular liver tests or scans may be needed during treatment.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, loose stools, abdominal discomfort, nausea, or indigestion. Contact a doctor if diarrhoea is severe or persistent.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is liver disease, gallbladder inflammation, or suspected blockage of the bile ducts. It may not be suitable for all types of gallstones. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines, particularly antacids containing aluminium or medicines that bind bile acids, as these may reduce its absorption.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Vildagliptin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may be used alone or together with other diabetes medicines.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called DPP-4, helping the body release insulin after meals and reduce the release of excess glucose from the liver. This helps lower blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It may be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If used with other diabetes medicines, follow the prescribed schedule carefully.

Common side effects
Nausea, dizziness, headache, constipation and shaking or tremor may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when it is taken with insulin or sulfonylurea medicines.

Precautions
It is intended for type 2 diabetes and should not be used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems; dose adjustment or monitoring may be needed. Seek medical help for severe, persistent abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, swelling of the face or throat, or a serious skin reaction. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Vildagliptin is used to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes, usually along with diet and exercise. It may be used alone or with other diabetes medicines when needed.

How does it work?
It helps the body release more insulin after meals and reduces the amount of sugar made by the liver. This helps lower blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it regularly and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Continue the recommended diet, exercise and blood sugar monitoring.

Common side effects
Nausea, dizziness, headache, shaking or low blood sugar (especially when taken with insulin or sulfonylureas), constipation, and joint pain may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, heart failure, or a history of pancreatitis before use. Seek medical help for severe, persistent abdominal pain, especially if it spreads to the back, as this may indicate pancreatitis. Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness, which may indicate liver problems. The risk of low blood sugar is higher when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used to help control blood glucose in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus when prescribed by a doctor, alongside diet and exercise.
How does it work?
Vildagliptin inhibits the DPP-4 enzyme, helping regulate incretin hormones and glucose-dependent insulin release. Dapagliflozin blocks the SGLT2 protein in the kidneys, increasing urinary glucose excretion.
How to take/use it
Take orally as prescribed. Follow the product-specific instructions for the sustained-release formulation. Swallow the tablet as directed and do not crush or chew it unless the leaflet permits it.
Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, genital fungal infections, urinary tract infections, and dehydration may occur.
Precautions
Monitor blood glucose and kidney function as advised. Maintain adequate hydration according to your doctor's instructions. Seek urgent medical attention for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, or difficulty breathing, which may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis even if blood glucose is not very high. Inform your doctor about liver disease, kidney problems, or planned surgery.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Vildagliptin 50 mg + metformin 1000 mg is used with diet and exercise to control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Vildagliptin helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces the release of glucagon. Metformin lowers glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or after food, to reduce stomach upset. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain or discomfort, vomiting, gas, headache and dizziness may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, liver disease, heart failure, pancreatitis, heavy alcohol use, or any planned surgery or contrast-dye scan. Kidney and liver function may need monitoring. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, unusual weakness, difficulty breathing, or signs of a serious allergic reaction. Avoid excessive alcohol. Take medical advice during severe vomiting, diarrhoea or dehydration.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Vildagliptin 50 mg + metformin 500 mg is used with diet and exercise to control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It helps improve blood glucose control when one medicine alone is not enough.

How does it work?
Vildagliptin helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces excess glucose production. Metformin mainly reduces glucose production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with or after food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole and do not stop treatment without medical advice. Do not take extra doses if a dose is missed; follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain or discomfort, vomiting, reduced appetite, headache, dizziness and a metallic taste. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with insulin or sulfonylure medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, heart failure, heavy alcohol use, or a history of pancreatitis. Kidney function should be checked during treatment. Seek medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, unusual weakness, breathing difficulty or severe drowsiness. This medicine is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis. Inform the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding, and before surgery or procedures involving contrast dye.

What is it used for?
Voglibose is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes, especially the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How does it work?
It slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates in the intestine. This helps reduce the increase in blood sugar after eating.

How to take/use it
Take it just before meals, exactly as prescribed. Follow the recommended diet and blood sugar monitoring plan. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort or pain, diarrhoea, and constipation.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney or liver disease, digestive or intestinal disease, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Low blood sugar may occur when used with insulin or other diabetes medicines; seek medical advice if symptoms such as sweating, shakiness, dizziness, or confusion occur. Report severe abdominal pain or persistent diarrhoea.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Pancreatin is used as pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy when the pancreas does not produce enough digestive enzymes. It helps the body digest fats, proteins and carbohydrates, such as in pancreatic insufficiency.

How does it work?
It supplies enzymes similar to those normally made by the pancreas. These enzymes help break down food so nutrients can be absorbed.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed or as stated on the product label, usually with meals or snacks. If the product is enteric-coated, swallow it whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Stomach pain, bloating, constipation, diarrhoea, nausea or vomiting may occur. Mouth irritation can occur if the medicine is chewed.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to pancreatin or pork-derived products. Seek medical advice if severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting or constipation occurs. People with gout, high uric acid, cystic fibrosis, or a history of bowel narrowing should use it only under medical supervision.

title: Aplipase 25000 Cap (10x1x10) Pancreatin 300 mg Cap by Aristo

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Pancreatin is used as digestive enzyme replacement when the pancreas does not produce enough enzymes. It helps improve the digestion and absorption of fats, proteins and carbohydrates, including in conditions such as chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis or after pancreatic surgery.

How does it work?
It supplies pancreatic enzymes, including lipase, amylase and protease, to help break down food in the intestine.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed or directed on the product label. It is generally taken with meals and snacks. Swallow the medicine as directed; do not crush or chew enteric-coated preparations unless specifically advised.

Common side effects
Abdominal pain, bloating, nausea, constipation or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about an allergy to pancreatin or pork proteins, cystic fibrosis, gout or high uric acid levels. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, constipation or vomiting. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

title: Arginorm Sachet (6.5 gm) L-Arginine, Proanthocyanidin Granules by Aristo

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This product provides L-arginine and proanthocyanidins as a nutritional supplement. Its specific medical use depends on the product formulation and the advice of a healthcare professional; it should not be used to self-treat a particular condition.

How does it work?
L-arginine is used by the body to make nitric oxide, which helps support normal blood vessel function. Proanthocyanidins are plant compounds with antioxidant activity.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or prescribed by a healthcare professional. Follow the instructions for preparing the granules and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is low blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, liver disease, asthma, or recurrent herpes infection. Discuss its use with a healthcare professional if taking blood-pressure medicines, nitrates, medicines for erectile dysfunction, or blood thinners. Stop use and seek advice if troublesome effects occur.

title: Arinandrol 25mg Injection (Pack) Nandrolone Decanoate 25 mg Inj by Aristo
name: Arinandrol 25mg Injection (Pack) Nandrolone Decanoate 25 mg Inj by Aristo
searchText: Arinandrol 25mg Injection (Pack) Nandrolone Decanoate 25 mg Inj by Aristo Aristo 48000333
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is an anabolic steroid prescribed mainly to help manage osteoporosis and bone loss. In some cases, a specialist may use it for certain types of anemia or severe loss of body tissue.

How does it work?
It acts like a modified male hormone and promotes protein production and tissue building. It may also support bone formation and the production of red blood cells.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. It is generally administered by a healthcare professional; do not self-inject or use it for bodybuilding or performance enhancement. The dose and treatment duration depend on the medical condition and response to treatment.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in cholesterol, mood changes, menstrual irregularities, increased body or facial hair, and changes in sexual function. Long-term use may affect the liver, fertility, or natural hormone production.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about liver, kidney, heart, prostate, or breast problems, diabetes, high cholesterol, or use of blood thinners. It may cause masculinising effects in women and may affect growth in children. Regular medical monitoring is important.

title: Arinandrol 50mg Injection (Pack) Nandrolone Decanoate 50 mg Inj by Aristo
name: Arinandrol 50mg Injection (Pack) Nandrolone Decanoate 50 mg Inj by Aristo
searchText: Arinandrol 50mg Injection (Pack) Nandrolone Decanoate 50 mg Inj by Aristo Aristo 48000334
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid that may be used under specialist supervision for certain types of osteoporosis (bone thinning) and some anaemias, particularly when other treatments are unsuitable. Its exact use depends on the doctor’s assessment.

How does it work?
It acts like an androgen hormone and increases protein production. This can support bone and muscle tissue and may stimulate red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
It is given as a deep intramuscular injection by a healthcare professional. The dose and injection schedule depend on the condition being treated and must be decided by the prescriber. It should not be used for bodybuilding or without medical supervision.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in sexual desire, mood changes, injection-site pain, menstrual changes, increased facial or body hair, and voice deepening in women. It may also affect liver function, cholesterol levels, or blood cell counts.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Inform the doctor about prostate or breast cancer, liver, kidney or heart disease, high cholesterol, or sleep apnoea. Women should report voice deepening, increased hair growth, or menstrual changes promptly; some effects may be irreversible. Regular medical monitoring may be needed, including blood counts, liver function, cholesterol, and prostate checks where appropriate.

title: Aristatin 10 Tab (10x10) Atorvastatin 10 mg Tab by Aristo
name: Aristatin 10 Tab (10x10) Atorvastatin 10 mg Tab by Aristo
searchText: Aristatin 10 Tab (10x10) Atorvastatin 10 mg Tab by Aristo Aristo 48000188
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high levels of cholesterol and other fats in the blood. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme involved in making cholesterol in the liver. This lowers LDL (bad) cholesterol and helps reduce fatty build-up in the arteries.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water, with or without food. Continue taking it regularly and do not stop without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, indigestion, diarrhoea and muscle pain may occur. Contact a doctor if muscle pain or weakness is severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems or a history of muscle problems. Seek medical advice promptly for unexplained muscle pain, weakness, dark urine or yellowing of the skin or eyes. It is generally not used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, including antibiotics and antifungal medicines, before starting treatment.

title: Aristatin 20 Tab (10x10) Atorvastatin 20 mg Tab by Aristo

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and triglycerides. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It reduces cholesterol production in the liver and helps the liver remove more LDL cholesterol from the blood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually once daily, with or without food. Take it at the same time each day and do not stop it without medical advice. Continue diet and lifestyle measures recommended by the prescriber.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, indigestion and muscle aches may occur. Contact a doctor promptly for unexplained or severe muscle pain, weakness or dark urine.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems or a history of muscle problems. Seek medical advice before using it with other medicines, as some medicines can increase the risk of muscle problems. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor. Liver tests may be needed during treatment.

Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and triglycerides. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. It may be taken with or without food, preferably at the same time each day. Do not stop or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, indigestion, and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney problems, thyroid problems, heavy alcohol use, or any unexplained muscle pain or weakness. What is it used for?
This medicine is used to help prevent heart attacks and strokes in people at increased cardiovascular risk, especially those with established heart disease. It helps lower cholesterol and reduce the formation of harmful blood clots.

How does it work?
Atorvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol production in the liver. Aspirin reduces the ability of platelets to stick together, helping prevent blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, easy bruising or bleeding, headache, and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, liver disease, kidney disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, or bleeding disorders. Seek medical advice for unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe muscle pain or weakness, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially blood thinners, other painkillers, and medicines that may affect the liver. This medicine is generally not used during pregnancy; ask a doctor before use while breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This combination is prescribed to reduce the risk of blood clots, heart attack and certain types of stroke in people with coronary artery disease or after certain heart-related events or procedures.

How does it work?
Atorvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol and helps protect blood vessels. Aspirin and clopidogrel reduce platelet clumping, helping prevent blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Do not stop this medicine or skip doses without medical advice, as this may increase the risk of a blood clot. Follow the prescribed instructions regarding food and other medicines.

Common side effects
Easy bruising or bleeding, nosebleeds, indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, and muscle aches may occur. Mild changes in liver tests can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of bleeding, stomach ulcers, liver disease, kidney disease, or muscle problems. Inform the doctor and dentist before surgery or dental procedures. Seek urgent medical care for uncontrolled bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe headache, or sudden weakness. Report severe muscle pain or weakness, especially with dark urine. Avoid pregnancy and breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor, and check before using painkillers or other medicines that may increase bleeding.

This combination is used to help prevent harmful blood clots and reduce the risk of heart attack or stroke in people with coronary artery disease, including after certain heart-related events or procedures. The exact reason for prescribing it depends on the patient's condition.

How does it work?
Atorvastatin lowers LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and helps stabilise fatty deposits in blood vessels. Aspirin and clopidogrel reduce platelet clotting, helping prevent blood clots from forming.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the same time each day. Do not stop it without medical advice, especially after a heart procedure. If a dose is missed, follow the prescribed instructions and do not take an extra dose unless advised.

Common side effects
Easy bruising or bleeding, nosebleeds, indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, headache, and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe weakness, or unexplained severe muscle pain. Tell the doctor about ulcers, bleeding disorders, liver disease, kidney disease, or any planned surgery or dental procedure. Avoid starting painkillers such as ibuprofen or other medicines, including blood thinners, without medical advice. Avoid alcohol or limit it, as it may increase bleeding or liver-related risks. This medicine is generally not used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a doctor.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Bilastine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It is also used to relieve itching and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce itching, sneezing, redness and other allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It is generally taken with water on an empty stomach—1 hour before or 2 hours after food or fruit juice. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Headache, sleepiness, dizziness and tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Use only as advised if there is kidney disease or if taking other medicines. Avoid driving or operating machinery if sleepy or dizzy. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis (hay fever), such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Bilastine blocks histamine, a chemical that causes allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, substances involved in allergic inflammation and swelling of the airways.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the instructions on the label, and do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Do not stop or change treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, sleepiness or tiredness, stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, disturbed sleep, nightmares, irritability, anxiety, depression, or suicidal thoughts. Seek medical advice promptly if these occur. It is not intended to treat a sudden asthma or breathing attack. Drowsiness may occur; take care when driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Tell the doctor about other medicines and any liver or kidney problems.

Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow it with water. Follow the product label or doctor's instructions about timing with food or fruit juice, as these may affect bilastine absorption. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Kaolin clay absorbs oil and impurities from the skin. Aloe vera may help soothe and moisturise irritated or dry-feeling skin.

For external use only. Use exactly as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not apply to broken or infected skin unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Skin dryness, tightness, redness, itching or irritation may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon.

Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Keep away from the eyes and mouth. Seek medical advice if irritation persists or the skin condition worsens.

This supplement provides calcium and active vitamin D (calcitriol) to support calcium absorption and maintain strong bones and teeth. It may also help provide omega-3 fatty acids, vitamin B12 and folic acid when supplementation is needed.

Calcium provides minerals needed for bones and teeth, while calcitriol helps the body absorb calcium. Vitamin B12 and folic acid support normal blood-cell and nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or as stated on the product label. Swallow the softgel whole with water, preferably with food. Do not take additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Constipation, stomach upset, nausea, bloating or diarrhoea may occur. Excess calcium may cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness or confusion and requires medical attention.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high blood calcium, or a disorder that increases calcium levels. Calcitriol may require blood-calcium monitoring. Inform the doctor about anticoagulants and other medicines, especially thyroid medicines, iron supplements or certain antibiotics. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excess calcium occur.

Calcium provides the mineral needed for bones, while calcitriol helps the body absorb calcium. Vitamin K, magnesium, zinc, vitamin B12 and L-methylfolate support normal bone and body functions.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Swallow the capsule whole with water, preferably with food unless otherwise advised. Do not take additional calcium or vitamin D supplements without medical advice.

Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating or diarrhoea may occur. Excess calcium may cause increased thirst or urination, weakness, or confusion and requires medical attention.

Luliconazole 1% cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch. It helps clear the infection and relieve related itching, redness and scaling.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents their growth and helps eliminate the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the clean, dry affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or on the product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not cover the area tightly unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild application-site irritation, redness, itching, burning or stinging may occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not use if allergic to luliconazole or any ingredient. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, causes severe irritation, or does not improve as expected. Use on the scalp or nails only if specifically advised by a doctor.

For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not stop treatment early without medical advice.

Mild irritation, redness, itching, burning or stinging at the application site.

Traditionally used in babies to help relieve colic, gas and mild digestive discomfort. Evidence for gripe water is limited, and benefits may vary by formulation.

Its ingredients are intended to soothe the digestive tract and reduce gas-related discomfort. The exact action depends on the Ayurvedic formulation.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount or give it to a baby unless the label permits it. Consult a paediatrician before use, especially in newborns or young infants.

Side effects depend on the ingredients and may include digestive upset or an allergic reaction.

Precautions
Check the ingredients and age recommendation before use. Stop use and seek medical advice if rash, vomiting, diarrhoea or breathing difficulty occurs. Persistent crying, fever, poor feeding, a swollen abdomen or blood in the stool requires prompt medical attention.

Metronidazole 400 mg is used to treat infections caused by certain bacteria and parasites, including some infections of the stomach and intestines, teeth and gums, vagina, skin and other parts of the body. It may also be used for amoebiasis, giardiasis and trichomoniasis when prescribed.

How does it work?
It enters susceptible bacteria and parasites and damages their genetic material, stopping them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not drink alcohol while taking it and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, metallic taste, dry mouth and dark-coloured urine.

Precautions
Inform the doctor if there is liver disease, a nervous-system disorder, a blood disorder, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Dextromethorphan helps reduce coughing, phenylephrine relieves nasal blockage, and chlorpheniramine helps reduce allergy-like symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take or use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount, and avoid taking other cough, cold or decongestant medicines at the same time unless advised.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, restlessness, palpitations or a temporary increase in blood pressure may occur.

Precautions

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold or allergy-related symptoms such as a blocked or runny nose, sneezing and nasal congestion.

How does it work?

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the package or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than recommended or combine with other cold medicines containing similar ingredients.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Omega-3 fatty acid capsules are used as a dietary supplement to provide omega-3 fats, which may be helpful when dietary intake is low. Some higher-strength omega-3 products are also used under medical supervision to help lower high triglyceride levels.

How does it work?
Omega-3 fatty acids such as EPA and DHA are important fats used by the body. They help support normal fat metabolism and other body functions.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach discomfort.

Common side effects
Fishy taste or burping, indigestion, nausea, loose stools or diarrhoea, and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to fish or other ingredients in the product. Consult a healthcare professional before use if taking blood thinners, having a bleeding disorder, or before surgery. Seek medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if using it to manage high triglyceride levels.

title: Aristomet G1 Tab (10x15) Glimepiride 1 mg, Metformin 500 mg PR Tab by Aristo

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when one medicine alone is not enough.

How does it work?
Glimepiride helps the pancreas release more insulin, while metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin. Together, they help lower blood sugar.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with a meal to reduce stomach upset and the risk of low blood sugar. Swallow the prolonged-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, vomiting, loss of appetite and a metallic taste may occur. Metformin may rarely cause vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use.

Precautions
Monitor blood sugar as advised. Do not skip meals, as this may increase the risk of low blood sugar. Avoid excessive alcohol. Tell the doctor about kidney, liver or heart problems, severe infection, dehydration, or upcoming surgery or contrast-dye scans. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent weakness, breathing difficulty, unusual sleepiness, or confusion. This medicine is not used for type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

title: Aristomet G2 Tab (10x15) Glimepiride 2 mg, Metformin 500 mg PR Tab by Aristo
name: Aristomet G2 Tab (10x15) Glimepiride 2 mg, Metformin 500 mg PR Tab by Aristo
searchText: Aristomet G2 Tab (10x15) Glimepiride 2 mg, Metformin 500 mg PR Tab by Aristo Aristo 48000032
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when these measures alone are not enough. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Metformin reduces the amount of glucose made by the liver and helps the body use insulin better. Glimepiride helps the pancreas release more insulin to lower blood sugar.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and with food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the prolonged-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Monitor blood sugar as recommended.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, and headache. Low blood sugar may cause sweating, shaking, dizziness, hunger, or confusion.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is kidney or liver disease, heart failure, heavy alcohol use, or irregular meals. Avoid skipping meals and limit alcohol, as these may increase the risk of low blood sugar. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent weakness, breathing difficulty, unusual sleepiness, or severe vomiting. Kidney function may need monitoring during treatment.

How does it work?
Amoxicillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps prevent some bacteria from breaking down amoxicillin, making it effective against a wider range of bacteria.

Take exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Take doses at evenly spaced times and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Taking it with a meal may reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial and protozoal infections that may cause diarrhoea or dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Norfloxacin stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Tinidazole damages certain bacteria and parasites, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with a full glass of water, and complete the prescribed course. Do not self-medicate or stop early. Avoid taking it with milk or dairy products, and separate antacids or mineral supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc as advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 72 hours after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and a metallic taste in the mouth may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney disease, seizures, nerve problems, tendon disorders or myasthenia gravis. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe rash, breathing difficulty, or unusual confusion. Avoid driving if dizziness or blurred vision occurs. Keep hydrated unless fluid restriction has been advised.

What is it used for?
Sodium chloride infusion is given through a vein in hospitals or clinics to replace lost fluids and sodium (salt), such as during dehydration or certain conditions causing fluid or salt loss. Its exact use depends on the solution strength and the patient's medical needs.

How does it work?
It supplies water, sodium and chloride to the bloodstream, helping restore fluid and electrolyte balance.

How to take/use it
This infusion must be given into a vein by a healthcare professional. The amount and speed are decided by the doctor based on the patient's condition and monitoring results. It must not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Fluid retention, swelling, irritation or pain at the injection site, and changes in blood sodium levels may occur.

Precautions
Use cautiously in people with heart failure, kidney problems, high blood pressure or a tendency to retain fluid. Medical monitoring may be needed to check fluid balance and electrolyte levels. Tell the healthcare professional about existing heart or kidney disease before treatment.

What is it used for?
Oral rehydration solution (ORS) helps prevent and treat dehydration caused by diarrhoea, vomiting, excessive sweating or other fluid loss. It replaces lost water and essential salts.

How does it work?
ORS contains glucose and salts that help the intestine absorb water more effectively, restoring the body's fluid and electrolyte balance.

How to take/use it
Dissolve the entire sachet in the exact amount of clean water stated on the package. Stir well and drink in frequent small sips. Do not take the powder directly or prepare it with less or more water than recommended. Use the prepared solution only as directed on the label.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, bloating or mild stomach discomfort may occur, especially if taken too quickly.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical care for severe dehydration, persistent vomiting, blood in the stool, high fever, confusion, very little urination or inability to drink. Use only with medical advice in severe kidney disease, heart failure or other conditions requiring fluid or salt restriction. ORS does not replace medical treatment for the cause of diarrhoea.

Local irritation, redness, itching or an allergic skin reaction may occur. Stop use if symptoms worsen or a severe reaction develops.

Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. It is generally absorbed better when taken with food. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it long term without medical advice.

Sodium hyaluronate forms a moisture-retaining lubricating layer over the eye surface, helping reduce friction and discomfort. Stabilized oxychloro complex helps maintain the sterility of the eye drops.

How to take/use it
Use in the eyes exactly as directed on the label or by an eye-care professional. Wash hands before use and do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or other surfaces. If contact lenses are worn, follow the product instructions regarding removal and reinsertion.

Common side effects
Mild, temporary stinging, burning, irritation, redness or blurred vision may occur after application.

Precautions
For ophthalmic use only. Do not use if the solution is discoloured or the container is damaged. Stop use and seek medical advice if eye pain, marked redness, vision changes or persistent irritation occurs. Do not share the bottle.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cinnarizine is used to prevent and relieve vertigo (a spinning or dizzy sensation) and related nausea. It is also used to help prevent motion sickness.

How does it work?
It reduces the sensitivity of the balance centre in the inner ear and blocks certain signals that can cause dizziness and nausea.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food if it causes stomach upset. Do not drive or operate machinery until its effect on alertness is known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dry mouth, indigestion, nausea and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness; avoid alcohol and take care when driving. Inform the doctor if there is Parkinson’s disease, as cinnarizine may worsen its symptoms. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if side effects are severe or persistent.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Metronidazole is used to treat certain infections caused by anaerobic bacteria and parasites such as amoebiasis and giardiasis. It may also be prescribed for conditions such as bacterial vaginosis and some dental or abdominal infections, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It enters susceptible bacteria and parasites and damages their genetic material, stopping them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Follow the product label for measuring and taking the medicine; do not take extra doses for a missed dose. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, metallic taste and dizziness.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to metronidazole or similar medicines. Tell the doctor about pregnancy or breastfeeding, liver disease, nervous system disorders, or medicines such as warfarin, lithium, disulfiram or seizure medicines. Seek medical help for numbness, tingling, seizures, severe rash or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cilnidipine 10 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It helps lower blood pressure and reduces the risk of complications related to uncontrolled hypertension.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens the blood vessels by reducing calcium entry into the muscle cells of the vessel walls. This allows blood to flow more easily and lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the same time each day. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; do not take two doses together.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, palpitations and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur.

Precautions
Rise slowly if dizziness occurs, especially when starting treatment. Inform the doctor about low blood pressure, liver or kidney problems, or swelling of the legs. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if swelling is severe, fainting occurs or blood pressure remains uncontrolled.

title: Cilniristo 20 Tab (10x15) Cilnidipine 20 mg Tab by Aristo
