bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Azithromycin 250 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, ears, chest, sinuses, skin and some sexually transmitted infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share it or use leftover antibiotics. Follow the product instructions about taking it with food, and separate it from aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids if advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, vomiting and headache.

Precautions
Tell the prescriber about allergies to azithromycin or other macrolide antibiotics, liver problems, heart rhythm problems or a history of severe diarrhoea after antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, severe or persistent diarrhoea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, fainting, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.

searchText: Beclotas-N 15 Gm ( Combo ) (Beclomethasone Dipropionate 0.025%, Neomycin Sulphate 0.50% Cream) By Intas Intas 400027234
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is generally used on the skin for inflamed skin conditions that are complicated by a bacterial infection, such as infected dermatitis or eczema. Use it only for the condition prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Beclomethasone reduces skin inflammation, redness and itching. Neomycin helps control susceptible bacterial infections.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. If supplied as a skin preparation, apply only to the affected area and avoid using it more often or for longer than advised. Wash hands before and after use unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, irritation, itching or redness may occur. Prolonged or repeated use may cause skin thinning, colour changes or other skin changes.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas unless specifically advised. Do not use on untreated fungal or viral skin infections, large areas, broken skin or under airtight dressings unless prescribed. Stop use and seek medical advice if the rash worsens or signs of an allergic reaction occur. Avoid prolonged use, especially in children, unless supervised by a doctor.

title: Becocap 10 Cap (Vitamin B Complex, Copper 25 Mcg, Zinc 600 Mcg Cap) By Intas

searchText: Becocap 10 Cap (Vitamin B Complex, Copper 25 Mcg, Zinc 600 Mcg Cap) By Intas Intas 9O900033374
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
It is used as a nutritional supplement to provide B vitamins, copper and zinc, and may help prevent or correct deficiencies when dietary intake is inadequate. The exact use depends on the product label and individual nutritional needs.

How does it work?
B vitamins support energy metabolism and normal function of the nervous system and blood cells. Copper and zinc support normal immune function, tissue maintenance and other essential body processes.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount or take additional supplements containing the same nutrients without advice.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Nausea, stomach upset or other digestive discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional about any other vitamins, supplements or medicines being taken. Zinc and mineral supplements may affect the absorption of some medicines, including certain antibiotics and thyroid medicines; separate them as advised. Seek advice before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in people with a medical condition.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat deficiency of B vitamins and to provide nutritional supplementation when dietary intake is inadequate or additional B vitamins are needed.

How does it work?
It supplies B vitamins that help the body release energy from food and support normal nerve function, blood cell formation and other body processes.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water, exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Nausea, stomach discomfort or headache may occur. Urine may become bright yellow due to vitamin B2 and this is generally harmless.

Precautions
Check with a doctor before use if there is a known allergy to any ingredient, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or an ongoing medical condition. Seek medical advice if unusual or severe symptoms occur.

title: Betni Inj. 1Ml (Betamethasone 4 Mg/Ml Inj) By Intas

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Betamethasone sodium phosphate injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and control allergic or immune-related reactions in conditions requiring steroid treatment. The exact use depends on the patient's condition and the healthcare professional's assessment.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of the immune system and blocks the release of substances that cause inflammation, swelling and allergic symptoms.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a healthcare professional, usually by injection. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, mood or sleep changes, increased blood sugar, increased blood pressure, fluid retention and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically advised. Do not stop repeated or prolonged treatment suddenly without medical advice.

title: Bilintas 20 (Bilastine 20 Mg) By Intas
name: Bilintas 20 (Bilastine 20 Mg) By Intas
searchText: Bilintas 20 (Bilastine 20 Mg) By Intas Intas 400028251
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Bilastine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably on an empty stomach. Avoid taking it with food or fruit juice, as these may reduce its effect.

Common side effects
Headache, drowsiness, dizziness, tiredness and nausea may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease or if other medicines are being taken. Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsiness or dizziness occurs.

title: Bilintas-M (Bilastine 20 Mg, Montelukast 10 Mg) By Intas
name: Bilintas-M (Bilastine 20 Mg, Montelukast 10 Mg) By Intas
searchText: Bilintas-M (Bilastine 20 Mg, Montelukast 10 Mg) By Intas Intas 400028250
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis (hay fever), such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Bilastine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can contribute to inflammation and nasal allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow with water. Bilastine is usually taken on an empty stomach—about 1 hour before or 2 hours after food or fruit juice—unless the prescriber gives different instructions. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Headache, drowsiness, tiredness, stomach pain, nausea, or sleep disturbances may occur.

Precautions
Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, disturbing dreams, depression, or suicidal thoughts. Stop the medicine and seek medical advice promptly if these occur. Avoid driving or using machinery if drowsiness occurs. If prescribed for asthma, this medicine does not replace a rescue inhaler for a sudden asthma attack. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in case of liver or kidney problems.

title: Biscotas 1Ml Inj. (Hyoscine Butylbromide 20 Mg/Ml Inj) By Intas

searchText: Biscotas 1Ml Inj. (Hyoscine Butylbromide 20 Mg/Ml Inj) By Intas Intas 400023733
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Hyoscine butylbromide injection is used for short-term relief of painful muscle spasms or cramps in the stomach and intestines. It may also be used for spasms affecting the bile ducts or urinary tract.

How does it work?
It relaxes the smooth muscles of the digestive, biliary and urinary tracts by blocking certain nerve signals that cause muscle spasms.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection, usually by a doctor or other healthcare professional. It should not be self-injected. The dose and frequency depend on the condition and response to treatment.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, fast heartbeat, dizziness and difficulty passing urine may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, an enlarged prostate, bowel blockage, severe constipation, myasthenia gravis or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Seek urgent medical help for severe or worsening abdominal pain, fainting, breathing difficulty, swelling, or painful red eyes with blurred vision.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve itching and soothe minor skin irritation, such as that caused by insect bites, mild rashes or sunburn.

How does it work?
Calamine helps soothe and protect irritated skin. Diphenhydramine helps reduce itching, while camphor provides a cooling sensation.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, dryness, redness or a burning sensation may occur. Stop use if a rash or allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Do not apply to broken, infected or severely irritated skin, or over large areas unless advised by a healthcare professional. Do not swallow. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent or worsening.

What is it used for?
This lotion is used to relieve itching and soothe minor skin irritation, including itching from insect bites, rashes and mild sunburn.

How does it work?
Calamine forms a soothing, protective layer on the skin. Diphenhydramine helps reduce histamine-related itching, while camphor provides a cooling sensation.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid applying it to the eyes, mouth, broken skin or large areas of the body. Wash hands after use.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, dryness or a burning or stinging sensation may occur. Stop use if a rash or other signs of an allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Do not swallow. Avoid contact with the eyes and mucous membranes. Do not use on broken or infected skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Avoid prolonged or repeated use over large areas, and keep out of reach of children. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

title: Calcitas-D (200 Ml) (Calcium Carbonate 250 Mg/5 Ml, Cholecalciferol 125 Iu/5 Ml) By Intas

searchText: Calcitas-D (200 Ml) (Calcium Carbonate 250 Mg/5 Ml, Cholecalciferol 125 Iu/5 Ml) By Intas Intas 400027633
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat calcium and vitamin D deficiency and to support strong bones and teeth. It may be recommended when dietary calcium or vitamin D intake is insufficient.

How does it work?
Calcium provides a mineral needed for bones, teeth, muscles and nerves. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and supports healthy bone maintenance.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Measure the liquid with a proper measuring device; do not use a household spoon. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Constipation, stomach discomfort, bloating, nausea or vomiting. Excessive calcium intake may cause increased thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, or high calcium or vitamin D levels. Calcium can affect the absorption of some medicines, including iron, thyroid medicines and certain antibiotics; separate doses as advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Seek medical advice if severe vomiting, confusion, marked weakness or unusual thirst occurs.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) is used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency and to support healthy bones, teeth and muscles.

How does it work?
It helps the body absorb calcium and phosphate from food. These minerals are needed for normal bone strength and muscle function.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth and swallow the softgel whole with water, exactly as prescribed. Do not take it more often or for longer than recommended, as this is a high-strength vitamin D product.

Common side effects
Usually none when used as directed. Excess vitamin D may cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach discomfort, unusual thirst, frequent urination or weakness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, parathyroid disease or sarcoidosis. Seek medical advice before using it with calcium or other vitamin D supplements. Do not take extra doses without medical advice.

Vitamin D3 is converted into an active form in the body. It helps the intestines absorb calcium and phosphate, which are needed for normal bone health.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. This is a high-strength vitamin D product, so do not take it more often or for longer than advised. Follow the recommended schedule and do not take additional vitamin D supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated when used as directed. Excessive intake may cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach discomfort, increased thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or a condition such as sarcoidosis. Use cautiously with calcium supplements or other vitamin D products. It is converted in the body into an active form of vitamin D. This helps improve calcium and phosphate absorption and supports bone mineralisation.

Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the capsule whole, preferably with a meal. Do not take it more often or for longer than advised, and do not combine it with other vitamin D or calcium supplements unless recommended.

Usually well tolerated when used as directed. Nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach discomfort, thirst or increased urination may occur, especially with excessive use.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is high calcium, kidney disease, kidney stones, or a condition that increases calcium levels. Tell the doctor about other medicines, especially digoxin, thiazide diuretics, or calcium and vitamin D supplements.

Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. It may be taken with food.

Usually, vitamin D3 causes no side effects when taken as recommended. Excessive intake may cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, weakness, excessive thirst or frequent urination.

Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels, or a condition that increases calcium levels. Avoid taking additional vitamin D or calcium supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Used to supplement calcium and support calcium absorption and bone health, especially when calcium or active vitamin D supplementation is needed.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat certain fungal infections, especially when there is significant inflammation or a suspected bacterial infection alongside it.

Clotrimazole damages the fungal cell membrane. Beclomethasone reduces redness, swelling and itching, while neomycin acts against susceptible bacteria.

Burning, stinging, itching, irritation, redness, dryness or skin peeling at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning or colour changes.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Clotrimazole 1% is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch and fungal skin infections caused by Candida.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For use on the skin only. Apply to clean, dry affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, burning, stinging or itching may occur at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use on the eyes or swallow it. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, an allergic reaction or worsening symptoms occur. Seek medical advice if the infection does not improve or keeps returning.

title: Canditas – V Gel 30Gm (Clotrimazole 2% W/W Gel) By Intas

searchText: Canditas – V Gel 30Gm (Clotrimazole 2% W/W Gel) By Intas Intas 400011224
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Clotrimazole vaginal cream is used to treat vaginal fungal infections, commonly known as vaginal thrush or yeast infection. It can help relieve symptoms such as itching, soreness and abnormal discharge caused by the infection.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole is an antifungal medicine. It damages the fungal cell membrane, which stops the fungus from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For vaginal use only. Wash hands before and after use. Use the applicator to insert the cream into the vagina exactly as directed on the pack or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not swallow it. Avoid getting it in the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild burning, irritation, itching or discomfort in the vagina may occur after application.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole or any ingredient. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially before using the applicator. Seek medical advice if symptoms do not improve, keep returning, or occur with fever, lower abdominal pain, foul-smelling discharge, sores or unusual bleeding. The cream may reduce the effectiveness of latex condoms or diaphragms during treatment and for a short time afterwards; check the product instructions.

title: Cardipin Retard 10 Tab (Nifedipine 20 Mg Er Tab) By Intas

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Nifedipine extended-release is mainly used to lower high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to help prevent chest pain caused by angina.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily and reducing the workload on the heart.

How to take/use it

This combination is used to treat certain bacterial infections when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

Cefixime stops bacteria from forming their protective cell wall. Ofloxacin stops bacteria from multiplying by interfering with their DNA. Together, they help control susceptible bacterial infections.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not self-medicate or share this medicine. Precautions
Inform the doctor about allergies to cephalosporins, penicillins or quinolone antibiotics, kidney disease, seizures, heart rhythm problems, tendon problems or myasthenia gravis. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, swelling or breathing difficulty, tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, or an irregular heartbeat. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

It acts like an anabolic androgen hormone, helping increase protein production and support muscle and bone tissue. It can also stimulate red blood cell production.

This medicine is given as a deep injection into a muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and injection schedule depend on the condition being treated and must be decided by the prescriber. Do not self-inject or use it for bodybuilding.

Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Dry mouth, dizziness, drowsiness, blurred vision, nausea and constipation.

Precautions

Drotaverine is used to relieve painful spasms or cramps in smooth muscles, especially in the stomach and intestines. It may also be used for spasms of the bile ducts, urinary tract or uterus when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It relaxes smooth muscles, helping reduce spasms and cramp-like pain.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or healthcare professional. If this is an injectable medicine, it should be administered by a trained healthcare professional. Do not self-administer unless specifically instructed.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, constipation, palpitations and low blood pressure may occur. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to drotaverine, low blood pressure, or severe liver, kidney or heart disease. Seek medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, breathing difficulty or swelling of the face or throat. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Drotaverine injection is used to relieve painful cramps caused by spasms of smooth muscles, such as stomach or intestinal cramps, biliary or urinary tract spasms, and menstrual cramps.

It relaxes the smooth muscles in internal organs, helping reduce spasms and cramping pain.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or nurse. The dose, route and frequency depend on the condition and should be decided by a healthcare professional. Do not self-inject.

Dizziness, headache, nausea, palpitations, low blood pressure and injection-site discomfort may occur. Allergic reactions are possible.

Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is low blood pressure or severe liver, kidney or heart disease. Tell the doctor about any medicine allergies and if pregnant or breastfeeding. Used as a dietary protein supplement to help increase daily protein intake and support muscle maintenance, growth and recovery when combined with a balanced diet.

How does it work?
It provides protein and amino acids that the body uses to build and repair muscles and other tissues.

How to take/use it
Mix and consume as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended serving. Use with a balanced diet and adequate fluids.

Common side effects
Some people may experience bloating, gas, nausea or stomach discomfort, depending on the ingredients and individual tolerance.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list for allergens, including milk, soy, nuts or other ingredients. Avoid it if allergic to any ingredient. People with kidney disease or other medical conditions should seek medical advice before using a high-protein supplement. Sugar-free products may contain sweeteners that can cause digestive discomfort in some people.

title: Dydrovista 10Tab (Dydrogesterone 10 Mg Tab) By Intas

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Dydrogesterone is a progesterone-like medicine used for conditions related to low progesterone, such as irregular or painful periods, endometriosis, abnormal uterine bleeding, and some fertility or pregnancy-support treatments. It may also be used with oestrogen in hormone replacement therapy, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It acts similarly to the natural hormone progesterone. This helps regulate the lining of the uterus and support the menstrual cycle or pregnancy when progesterone support is needed.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache or migraine, nausea, breast tenderness, stomach discomfort, and changes in menstrual bleeding or spotting.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, unexplained vaginal bleeding, or a history of hormone-sensitive cancers. Seek medical advice for heavy or unusual bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe headache, or allergic symptoms. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

title: Emenorm 10 Tab (Metoclopramide 10 Mg Tab) By Intas

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Metoclopramide is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for slow stomach emptying and related digestive movement problems.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals involved in nausea and vomiting. It also helps the stomach empty more quickly by increasing movement in the upper digestive tract.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. Avoid driving or operating machinery if it causes drowsiness or restlessness.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, restlessness, headache, diarrhoea and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, depression, a history of involuntary muscle movements, stomach or intestinal blockage or bleeding, or kidney or liver problems. Avoid alcohol and check before using it with sedatives, antipsychotics or other medicines that affect movement. Seek urgent medical help for unusual muscle movements, severe restlessness, facial or neck spasms, confusion or seizures. Prolonged use can cause serious movement disorders and should be avoided unless specifically advised.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals in the brain that can trigger nausea and vomiting. It also increases movement of the upper digestive tract, helping the stomach empty more quickly.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. The dose and duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not take it for longer than recommended, and avoid driving or operating machinery if it causes drowsiness or restlessness.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, dizziness, restlessness, headache and diarrhoea. Unusual muscle spasms, stiffness, shaking or uncontrolled movements can occur and require prompt medical attention.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is stomach or intestinal blockage, bleeding or perforation, epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, or a history of involuntary muscle movements caused by medicines. What is it used for?
Metoclopramide is used to prevent or treat nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for slow stomach emptying and related digestive symptoms.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals in the vomiting centre of the brain, helping control nausea and vomiting. It also increases movement of the upper digestive tract and helps the stomach empty more quickly.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually before meals if directed. Swallow with water and do not take it for longer than recommended. Do not drive or operate machinery if it causes drowsiness or dizziness.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, dizziness, restlessness, headache and diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice, especially in children, older adults, or people with Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, depression, kidney problems or a history of involuntary movements. Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor or pharmacist before combining it with medicines that cause drowsiness. Stop using it and seek urgent medical help for uncontrolled movements, muscle stiffness, severe restlessness or unusual facial or tongue movements. It should not be used if there is suspected stomach or intestinal blockage, bleeding or perforation.

Prochlorperazine is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for dizziness or vertigo and nausea associated with migraine.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals in the brain that can trigger nausea and vomiting. It also reduces abnormal signals involved in dizziness and vertigo.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. Place the mouth-dissolving tablet on the tongue and allow it to dissolve. Do not take more than prescribed. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision and restlessness may occur. Some people may develop muscle stiffness, tremors or other abnormal movements.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol, as it can increase drowsiness. Seek medical help for severe muscle stiffness, uncontrolled movements, high fever, confusion, fainting or an irregular heartbeat. Ethamsylate is used to help control or prevent certain types of bleeding, including heavy menstrual bleeding and bleeding from small blood vessels, as prescribed by a doctor.

It helps strengthen small blood vessels and supports the formation of an initial platelet plug, which can reduce bleeding.

How to take/use it
This 125 mg/ml injection should be given only by a healthcare professional, exactly as prescribed. Do not self-inject or change the treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, skin rash or other allergic reactions.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ethamsylate or previous medicine reactions. Seek medical advice for unexplained, persistent or severe bleeding. The cause of abnormal bleeding should be assessed rather than treated without medical supervision. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction.

title: Emsyl-500 10 Tab (Ethamsylate 500 Mg Tab) By Intas

What is it used for?
Ethamsylate is used to help reduce excessive bleeding, especially heavy menstrual bleeding and bleeding from small blood vessels, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps strengthen small blood vessels and improves the ability of platelets to form a plug at the site of bleeding, which can help reduce blood loss.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice. Do not take extra doses to control sudden or heavy bleeding.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical care for very heavy, prolonged or unexplained bleeding, or if bleeding is accompanied by dizziness, weakness or fainting. Tell the doctor about any allergy to ethamsylate, porphyria, pregnancy or breastfeeding before use. Stop the medicine and seek urgent help for facial swelling, breathing difficulty or a severe skin rash.

Esomeprazole reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acidity, heartburn and acid reflux, and may also be used to help treat or prevent stomach and intestinal ulcers when prescribed.

It blocks the stomach’s acid-producing proton pumps, reducing the amount of acid made in the stomach.

Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before food. Swallow the gastro-resistant tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about other medicines being taken, especially blood thinners, some HIV medicines, methotrexate or medicines affected by stomach acid. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor.

Esomeprazole reduces the production of stomach acid. Domperidone helps food move through the stomach and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably before a meal. Swallow the capsule whole with water. Do not crush, chew or open it unless advised by a doctor. Do not take it for longer than prescribed.

Headache, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, dry mouth and dizziness.

Tell the doctor about heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, liver problems, electrolyte imbalance or any history of prolonged QT interval. bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Artesunate injection is used for the urgent treatment of severe malaria, including malaria caused by Plasmodium parasites. It is usually given in a hospital or medical facility.

How does it work?
Artesunate rapidly kills malaria parasites in the blood, helping to control the infection. Sodium bicarbonate and sodium chloride are used to prepare and dilute the injection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a trained healthcare professional. It must be prepared using the supplied diluents and used only according to the prescribed treatment plan. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, fever, weakness, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur. Changes in blood counts or liver tests can also occur.

Precautions
Severe malaria requires urgent medical care and monitoring. Inform the healthcare professional about any previous reaction to artesunate or other antimalarial medicines. Delayed breakdown of red blood cells can rarely occur days or weeks after treatment; follow-up blood tests may be needed. Seek immediate medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, unusual tiredness, pale skin, or yellowing of the eyes or skin.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Artesunate injection is used for the emergency treatment of severe malaria, including malaria caused by Plasmodium parasites. It is given in a hospital or healthcare setting and is usually followed by a complete course of an oral antimalarial medicine as prescribed.

How does it work?
Artesunate is converted in the body to an active substance that damages and kills malaria parasites in the blood, helping to reduce the parasite load quickly.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. It must be prepared and administered according to the product instructions. Do not self-inject. Complete the follow-up antimalarial treatment prescribed by the doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, fever, injection-site discomfort and changes in liver blood tests may occur. Delayed breakdown of red blood cells can rarely occur after treatment.

Precautions
It should be used under medical supervision for severe malaria. Tell the doctor about any previous reaction to artesunate or other antimalarial medicines. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, unusual tiredness, fainting or worsening fever after treatment. Medical follow-up and blood tests may be needed after treatment to check for delayed anaemia or other complications.

Alpha Beta Arteether is used to treat severe malaria, especially malaria caused by the Plasmodium falciparum parasite. Severe malaria is a medical emergency and usually requires hospital care.

It damages the malaria parasites in the blood, helping to reduce the parasite load and control the infection.

Use only under medical supervision. It is generally administered by a healthcare professional, and the exact dose, schedule and duration depend on the severity of malaria and the treatment plan. Do not self-administer or stop treatment without medical advice.

Nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, headache, dizziness, fever and pain at the injection site may occur.

Precautions

It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents the fungus from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
This preparation is generally given as a slow intravenous infusion by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the infection and kidney function; use it only as prescribed.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, vomiting and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, an irregular heartbeat, or an allergy to fluconazole or other azole antifungals. bodyHtml:

Take it exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Follow any instructions about taking it with food and spacing it from other medicines.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Iron sucrose is used to treat iron deficiency and iron deficiency anaemia, especially when iron tablets are not suitable, do not work well, or iron needs to be replaced under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It supplies iron to the body so it can produce haemoglobin and healthy red blood cells. This helps replenish the body's iron stores.

How to take/use it
Iron sucrose is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and number of treatments depend on the severity of iron deficiency and the medical condition. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, dizziness, low blood pressure, flushing, muscle cramps, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous reaction to iron injections or medicines, iron overload, or liver problems. Medical monitoring is needed during and after administration because serious allergic reactions, although uncommon, can occur. bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron and folic acid deficiency, including iron-deficiency anaemia. It may be prescribed when the body needs extra iron and folate to make healthy red blood cells.

How does it work?
Iron helps the body make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood. Folic acid supports the formation of healthy red blood cells, while ascorbate (vitamin C) helps improve iron absorption.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. If it causes stomach upset, it may be taken with or after food. Tea, coffee, milk, calcium supplements and antacids may reduce iron absorption; ask a doctor or pharmacist how to space them.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea. Dark or black stools are common with iron supplements.

Precautions
Use only after the cause of anaemia or deficiency has been assessed, as not all anaemia is caused by iron deficiency. Tell the doctor about iron-overload disorders, vitamin B12 deficiency, or other medicines and supplements being used. Keep out of reach of children, as an iron overdose can be dangerous. Seek medical help for severe allergic reactions, persistent vomiting or severe stomach pain.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron and folic acid deficiency, which may lead to nutritional anaemia. It also provides zinc supplementation when needed.

How does it work?
Iron helps the body make haemoglobin for carrying oxygen in the blood. Folic acid supports the formation of healthy red blood cells, while zinc supports normal growth, immunity and body functions.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow with water. If it causes stomach upset, taking it after food may help. Avoid taking it at the same time as tea, coffee, milk, calcium supplements or antacids; ask a pharmacist about the appropriate time gap.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, diarrhoea, metallic taste and dark-coloured stools.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Hydrocortisone sodium succinate injection is used for short-term treatment of severe inflammation or allergic reactions and for replacing the hormone cortisol when the body does not produce enough, such as in adrenal insufficiency. It may be used in hospital or emergency care when a rapid effect is needed.

How does it work?
It is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation and overactivity of the immune system. It also acts like the natural hormone cortisol in the body.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and response to treatment. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Injection-site discomfort, increased blood sugar or blood pressure, indigestion, mood or sleep changes, increased appetite and fluid retention may occur. The risk of side effects increases with higher doses or longer treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems or any infection. This medicine can reduce the body's ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Do not stop prolonged corticosteroid treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for severe infection symptoms, breathing difficulty or swelling of the face or throat.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Etoricoxib is used to reduce pain, swelling and stiffness in osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis. It may also be prescribed for short-term treatment of acute gout pain and certain other acute pain conditions.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called COX-2, which helps reduce the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water, with or without food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other painkillers or anti-inflammatory medicines with it unless a doctor advises this.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, swelling of the legs or feet, and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, high blood pressure, heart disease, stroke, kidney or liver problems, or allergy to painkillers such as aspirin or other NSAIDs. It may increase the risk of heart attack or stroke, especially with higher doses or prolonged use. Avoid during pregnancy, particularly after 20 weeks and in the last trimester, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, black stools, severe skin reactions or facial swelling.

It may not be suitable during pregnancy, especially in the later months. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, facial swelling, black stools or unusual bleeding.

Used on the skin for certain mixed skin infections involving fungi and bacteria, along with redness, itching or inflammation. It should be used only when prescribed, as the clobetasol component is a strong steroid.

Ofloxacin and ornidazole act against certain bacteria and other microorganisms, while itraconazole acts against fungi. Clobetasol reduces inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Wash and dry the area before use and wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Do not use more often or for longer than directed.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not apply to the face, groin, broken skin or under bandages unless specifically advised by a doctor. searchText: Intadol- Sp 10 Tab (Combo) (Aceclofenac 100 Mg, Paracetamol 325 Mg, Serratiopeptidase 10 Mg Tab) By Intas Intas 400026358
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling, especially in muscle, joint and other painful inflammatory conditions.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor, preferably with or after food, and swallow with water. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or NSAIDs unless advised.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, indigestion, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or if taking blood thinners. Avoid excessive alcohol. Avoid use during pregnancy, particularly in the last three months, unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash.

Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a healthcare professional, preferably with or after food. Swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take additional medicines containing paracetamol or other painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Use with caution or seek medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid alcohol. Do not use during the last 3 months of pregnancy, and seek medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, or swelling of the face or throat.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful muscle and joint conditions associated with muscle stiffness or spasms, such as back pain and other musculoskeletal pain.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside acts as a muscle relaxant to help reduce painful muscle spasms.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Take it with or after food and swallow it with water if it is supplied as an oral medicine. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness. Serious stomach irritation or bleeding can rarely occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or a history of seizures. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially the later months, and during breastfeeding unless specifically prescribed. Avoid taking it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe rash, breathing difficulty or swelling.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used as an oral rinse to help reduce dental plaque and bacteria, support gum health, and help prevent tooth decay.

How does it work?
Chlorhexidine reduces harmful bacteria in the mouth. Sodium fluoride strengthens tooth enamel, while zinc chloride may help reduce plaque and mouth odour.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a dentist. Rinse around the mouth and spit out; do not swallow. Do not dilute unless directed. Avoid eating or drinking immediately after use if advised on the label.

Common side effects
Temporary staining of the teeth or tongue, altered taste, mouth irritation, or a mild burning sensation may occur. Long-term use may increase tartar buildup.

Precautions
Do not swallow. Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient. Chlorhexidine-containing rinses can interact with some toothpastes, so follow the product instructions on timing. Stop use and seek dental or medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash, or breathing difficulty occurs.

searchText: Intagenta Inj. 20Ml (Gentamicin 40 Mg/Ml Inj) By Intas Intas 400000850
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Gentamicin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including certain infections of the blood, lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, bones and joints. It is usually used when prescribed and administered by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from multiplying.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type of infection and kidney function. Do not self-inject or change the treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain or irritation, nausea and headache may occur. More serious effects include kidney problems, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, dizziness or problems with balance.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, or muscle-nerve disorders. Kidney function and, when needed, blood levels and hearing may be monitored during treatment. Inform the doctor about all other medicines, especially those that can affect the kidneys or hearing. Seek medical help for reduced urination, unusual thirst, ringing in the ears, hearing changes, severe dizziness or difficulty breathing.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Diclofenac injection is used for short-term relief of moderate to severe pain and inflammation, including pain affecting the muscles, joints and bones.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a healthcare professional, usually as an injection. It should not be self-injected. The dose and duration depend on the condition and should be decided by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and pain at the injection site.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma or allergy after taking painkillers, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems. It may increase the risk of stomach bleeding, heart problems and kidney problems, especially with prolonged use. It should generally be avoided during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Diclofenac is used for short-term relief of pain and inflammation, such as muscle, joint, back or other painful inflammatory conditions. The exact use depends on the prescribed formulation and medical condition.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. The dose, route and frequency depend on the formulation and condition being treated. Do not use more than recommended or for longer than advised. If it is an injectable formulation, it should be given by a qualified healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and skin rash.

Precautions
Avoid diclofenac if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney or liver disease, serious heart disease, or an allergic reaction to aspirin or other NSAIDs, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or use of blood thinners or other painkillers. It should generally be avoided during the last 3 months of pregnancy and used in pregnancy only on medical advice. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic symptoms, chest pain or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of muscle and joint pain, including pain from sprains, strains and mild sports injuries.

How does it work?
Diclofenac and methyl salicylate help reduce pain and inflammation. Menthol provides a cooling sensation that may help soothe the painful area.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the painful area as directed on the product label and wash hands after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not swallow.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, broken or infected skin. Do not cover the treated area with a tight bandage or apply heat over it. Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other painkillers or any ingredient in the product. Stop use and seek medical help if severe skin reactions, swelling or breathing difficulty occur. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last three months, or if applying to large areas or for a prolonged period.

searchText: Intagra-100 4 Tab ( Combo ) (Sildenafil 100 Mg) By Intas Intas 400027233
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Sildenafil 100 mg is used to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sexual activity).

How does it work?
It increases blood flow to the penis during sexual stimulation, helping produce an erection. It does not increase sexual desire and will not work without sexual stimulation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, usually before planned sexual activity. Swallow with water and do not take more than prescribed. Follow the product label or medical advice for timing and use.

Common side effects
Headache, flushing, indigestion, blocked or stuffy nose, dizziness and temporary visual changes.

Precautions
Do not use with nitrate medicines for chest pain or with riociguat, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Seek medical advice before use if there is serious heart disease, low blood pressure, recent stroke or heart attack, or if taking alpha-blockers or other medicines for erectile dysfunction. Get urgent medical help for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, sudden loss of vision or hearing, or chest pain during sexual activity.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Sildenafil is mainly used to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sexual activity).

How does it work?
It increases blood flow to the penis by relaxing blood vessels. It works only with sexual stimulation and does not increase sexual desire.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Swallow with water. Do not take more than prescribed or use it with other medicines for erectile dysfunction.

Common side effects
Headache, flushing, indigestion, blocked or runny nose, dizziness, and changes in vision.

Precautions
Do not use sildenafil with nitrate medicines for chest pain or with riociguat, as this can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Seek medical help for chest pain, sudden loss of vision or hearing, or an erection lasting more than 4 hours. Tell a doctor about heart problems, low blood pressure, or use of alpha-blockers before taking it.

title: Intagra Force (4 T) (Combo) (Sildenafil 50 Mg, Dapoxetine 30 Mg) By Intas
name: Intagra Force (4 T) (Combo) (Sildenafil 50 Mg, Dapoxetine 30 Mg) By Intas
searchText: Intagra Force (4 T) (Combo) (Sildenafil 50 Mg, Dapoxetine 30 Mg) By Intas Intas 400027772
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This combination is used in adult men to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection) and premature ejaculation.

How does it work?
Sildenafil improves blood flow to the penis when there is sexual stimulation, helping achieve and maintain an erection. Dapoxetine affects serotonin activity and can help delay ejaculation.

How to take/use it
Take only in the dose and at the time prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take it more often than prescribed. It does not increase sexual desire and works only with sexual stimulation. Avoid excessive alcohol.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, flushing, indigestion, blocked nose, nausea, diarrhoea, dry mouth and visual changes may occur.

Precautions
Do not use with nitrate medicines for chest pain or riociguat, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Tell the doctor about heart disease, low blood pressure, fainting, liver problems, or medicines for blood pressure, depression or other mental health conditions. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, fainting, sudden loss of vision or hearing, or an erection lasting more than 4 hours.

title: Intagyl 100 Ml (Metronidazole 500 Mg) By Intas
name: Intagyl 100 Ml (Metronidazole 500 Mg) By Intas
searchText: Intagyl 100 Ml (Metronidazole 500 Mg) By Intas Intas 400022389
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Metronidazole is used to treat certain bacterial infections, especially infections caused by bacteria that grow without oxygen. It is also used for some parasitic infections, including amoebiasis, giardiasis and trichomoniasis, and for conditions such as bacterial vaginosis and some dental infections.

How does it work?
It damages the DNA of susceptible bacteria and parasites, stopping them from growing and surviving. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Do not use leftover medicine or share it with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, and a metallic taste in the mouth. Urine may become darker temporarily.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol while taking metronidazole and for at least 48 hours after the last dose. Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, a history of nerve problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if medicines such as warfarin are being used. Seek medical help for severe rash, numbness or tingling, seizures, confusion, or severe diarrhoea.

title: Intalka Liquid (Disodium Hydrogen Citrate 1.4 G/5 Ml Liquid) By Intas
name: Intalka Liquid (Disodium Hydrogen Citrate 1.4 G/5 Ml Liquid) By Intas
searchText: Intalka Liquid (Disodium Hydrogen Citrate 1.4 G/5 Ml Liquid) By Intas Intas KB155071314
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to make urine less acidic and relieve burning or discomfort during urination. It may also be used as supportive treatment in some kidney stone conditions. It does not treat a bacterial urinary infection by itself.

How does it work?
Disodium hydrogen citrate is converted into bicarbonate in the body, which helps reduce acidity and makes the urine more alkaline.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Measure the liquid carefully using a proper measuring device. Do not use more or for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, bloating or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Use only with medical advice if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, swelling, or a sodium-restricted diet, as this medicine contains sodium. Seek medical advice for fever, back or side pain, blood in the urine, or urinary symptoms that do not improve, as these may require treatment for an underlying infection or other condition.

title: Intalon 1000 Ml (Chlorhexidine Gluconate 0.3%, Cetrimide 0.6% Antiseptic Liquid) By Intas

searchText: Intalon 1000 Ml (Chlorhexidine Gluconate 0.3%, Cetrimide 0.6% Antiseptic Liquid) By Intas Intas 1Q900151354
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used as a topical antiseptic to cleanse minor cuts, grazes and wounds and help reduce the risk of infection.

How does it work?
Chlorhexidine and cetrimide kill or reduce the growth of many bacteria and other microorganisms on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply or use it on the affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, ears and mouth, and do not swallow it.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, burning or itching. Allergic reactions may rarely occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to chlorhexidine, cetrimide or any of its ingredients. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or other signs of a serious allergic reaction occur. Seek medical advice for deep, heavily bleeding or seriously infected wounds.

title: Intalon 100 Ml (Chlorhexidine Gluconate 0.3%, Cetrimide 0.6% Liquid) By Intas

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used as an antiseptic to clean and disinfect the skin, including minor cuts, wounds and superficial skin injuries. It helps reduce germs on the skin.

How does it work?
Chlorhexidine and cetrimide kill or reduce many bacteria and other germs by damaging their outer membranes.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use on the affected skin exactly as directed on the product label. Avoid swallowing and wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, burning, redness, irritation or dryness of the skin may occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the ears. Do not use if allergic to chlorhexidine, cetrimide or similar antiseptics. Do not apply to deep or extensive wounds, serious burns or large areas unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs.

title: Intamether-L 6 Tab (Arteether 80 Mg, Lumefantrine 480 Mg Uncoated Tab) By Intas

searchText: Intamether-L 6 Tab (Arteether 80 Mg, Lumefantrine 480 Mg Uncoated Tab) By Intas Intas 400008137
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to treat uncomplicated malaria, especially malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. It is not suitable for severe malaria, which requires urgent hospital treatment.

How does it work?
Arteether and lumefantrine act together to kill malaria parasites in the blood. They reduce the parasites responsible for causing malaria symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor and complete the full treatment course. Taking it with food or milk may improve absorption. Do not use it to prevent malaria or take extra doses if a dose is missed without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, loss of appetite and palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart problems, fainting, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or medicines such as rifampicin, carbamazepine or phenytoin. Seek urgent medical help for severe vomiting, fainting, an unusually fast or irregular heartbeat, seizures, confusion or worsening malaria symptoms.

Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Use the measuring device provided and do not exceed the recommended amount.

May cause mild stomach discomfort, nausea or loose stools. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent or associated with vomiting, severe abdominal pain or blood in the stool. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in young children.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to help reduce inflammation and swelling associated with soft-tissue injuries, inflammation and recovery after some procedures. Its exact use depends on the prescriber's advice.

How does it work?
Papain and alpha amylase are enzymes that help break down proteins and other substances involved in inflammatory swelling, which may help the body clear swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed by the doctor or as stated on the product label. Measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device and do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea. Allergic reactions such as rash or itching may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to papain, alpha amylase or any ingredient in the product. Tell the doctor if there is a bleeding disorder or if blood-thinning medicines are being used. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

searchText: Intaphylline 10 Tab (Etophylline 77 Mg, Theophylline 23 Mg Tab) By Intas Intas 400004281
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to help relieve breathing difficulty and wheezing caused by asthma and other obstructive airway conditions, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps open the airways and improve airflow.

How does it work?
Etophylline and theophylline relax the muscles around the airways, helping them widen. This makes breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the medicine with water and do not take more or more often than advised. Avoid changing the dose or stopping treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, trembling and fast or irregular heartbeat.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially with heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, thyroid problems, liver disease or stomach ulcers. Avoid excessive caffeine, as it may worsen side effects. Seek medical help for severe vomiting, marked palpitations, seizures or worsening breathing difficulty.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relax narrowed airways and relieve breathing difficulty caused by bronchospasm, such as in asthma and other obstructive airway conditions.

How does it work?
It contains theophylline, a bronchodilator that relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them open and making breathing easier.

How to take/use it
This is an injectable medicine and should be given only by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. Do not inject it yourself. Use it only in the dose and manner prescribed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, tremors and fast or irregular heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, irregular heartbeat, high blood pressure, seizures, liver disease or fever. Theophylline can interact with several medicines, so provide a complete list of medicines being used. Seek urgent medical help for severe vomiting, marked restlessness, seizures, or a very fast or irregular heartbeat.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat deficiencies of B-group vitamins and to support nutritional needs when dietary intake is inadequate. It may also support normal energy metabolism, nerve function and red blood cell formation.

How does it work?
The B vitamins help the body release energy from food and support the nervous system and blood cell production. Lysine is an essential amino acid needed for protein synthesis.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Shake the bottle well before use and measure the syrup with a proper measuring device. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort or diarrhoea may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Check the ingredients before use if there is a history of allergy to any component. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or use of other vitamin supplements. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction.

title: Intapod 200 10 Tab (Oval) (Cefpodoxime Proxetil 200 Mg Dt Tab) By Intas

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, ears, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
It is a cephalosporin antibiotic that stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall, causing the bacteria to die.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Disperse the tablet in water as directed on the product label and drink it immediately. Do not share leftover antibiotics with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and headache. Mild rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics, unless advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or any medicine being taken. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe skin reactions, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime proxetil is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ear, throat, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Shake the suspension well before each use and measure it with an oral syringe or measuring spoon. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not use leftover medicine or share it with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and headache may occur. Skin rash can also occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Use in children only under medical supervision.

title: Intapred-16 10 Tab (Methylprednisolone 16 Mg Tab) By Intas
name: Intapred-16 10 Tab (Methylprednisolone 16 Mg Tab) By Intas
searchText: Intapred-16 10 Tab (Methylprednisolone 16 Mg Tab) By Intas Intas 400020721
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and suppress an overactive immune response in conditions such as autoimmune disorders, severe allergies, and other inflammatory illnesses. The exact use depends on the condition being treated.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and allergic or immune reactions.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food or milk to reduce stomach irritation. Do not stop it suddenly, especially after prolonged treatment; the dose may need to be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, fluid retention, and increases in blood sugar or blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions, or any infection. Corticosteroids can weaken the immune system and may hide signs of infection. Avoid live vaccines unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for severe infection symptoms, vision changes, severe mood changes, black stools, or unusual swelling.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactivity of the immune system in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma, arthritis and other inflammatory or immune-related disorders. Its exact use depends on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow with water. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially if it has been used for a prolonged period.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, fluid retention and increased blood sugar may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions or any infection. This medicine can increase the risk of infections or hide their symptoms. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and check with the doctor before receiving vaccines. Seek medical help for signs of a serious infection, severe allergic reaction or major mood changes.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune reactions in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma, arthritis, and other inflammatory or autoimmune disorders. It should be used only for the condition prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of the immune system and lowers the release of substances that cause inflammation, swelling, redness and allergic symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food to reduce stomach upset. Do not stop it suddenly, especially after prolonged use; the dose may need to be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, increased blood sugar and increased blood pressure may occur. The risk of side effects increases with higher doses or longer treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions or any infection. Seek medical help for signs of serious infection, severe mood changes, vision problems or black stools.

title: Intarax (100Ml) (Hydroxyzine 10 Mg) By Intas

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Hydroxyzine is used to relieve itching and other symptoms caused by allergies or skin conditions. It may also be prescribed for short-term relief of anxiety and tension.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergic symptoms such as itching. It can also have a calming and sedating effect.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, headache, blurred vision and tiredness.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor before using it with sleeping tablets, sedatives or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice before use if there is heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic reaction or breathing difficulty.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Hydroxyzine is an antihistamine used to relieve itching caused by allergies and skin conditions. It may also be prescribed for short-term relief of anxiety.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions and itching. It can also reduce activity in the brain, which may cause a calming and drowsy effect.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, headache and constipation.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor before using it with sleeping tablets, sedatives or other medicines that cause drowsiness. For external use only. Apply or use it only as directed on the product label. Do not apply near the eyes, inside the nose or mouth, or on broken or irritated skin.

Skin irritation, redness, burning or an allergic skin reaction may occur.

Avoid contact with the eyes and mucous membranes, and do not swallow. Stop use if irritation or rash develops. Seek medical advice if cough or cold symptoms are severe, persistent, or associated with breathing difficulty.

Used for temporary relief of cough and cold symptoms through topical application.

Its topical ingredients may provide a soothing or warming sensation that helps relieve cough and cold discomfort. The exact action depends on the ingredients in the product.

For external use only. Apply to the recommended area exactly as directed on the product label. Do not swallow, and avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Skin irritation, redness, itching or an allergic rash may occur.

Do not apply to broken, irritated or sensitive skin. Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Keep out of reach of children and seek medical advice if swallowed. Check the label for age-specific warnings before use in children.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of indigestion, acidity, stomach discomfort and gas-related bloating. It may also help relieve mild digestive discomfort caused by trapped gas.

How does it work?
Sarjikakshara helps neutralise excess stomach acid. Dill, anise and peppermint oils have carminative properties that may help ease intestinal spasms and the feeling of gas.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount or use it for a prolonged period without medical advice.

Common side effects
Mild nausea, belching, stomach discomfort or bloating may occur. Stop use if an allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Check with a healthcare professional before use in children, especially infants, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding.
