bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Doripenem is an antibiotic used in hospitals to treat serious bacterial infections, especially complicated urinary tract and abdominal infections. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming the protective cell wall they need to survive.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function; follow the prescribed hospital treatment exactly.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, headache, rash, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to doripenem, other carbapenem antibiotics, penicillins or cephalosporins. Extra caution is needed in people with kidney problems or a history of seizures. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, seizures, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Doripenem can interact with some medicines, including valproic acid or sodium valproate.

title: Doxylink (10 Ml) Doxofylline By Protech

What is it used for?
Doxofylline is a bronchodilator used to help relieve breathing difficulty, wheezing and chest tightness in asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps keep the airways open.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them widen and making breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more or more often than directed. Do not stop regular asthma or COPD treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, tremors, fast heartbeat and palpitations.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart problems, high blood pressure, seizures, liver or kidney disease, or pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe or worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain or a persistent fast heartbeat. Inform the doctor about all other medicines being taken, as some medicines may interact with doxofylline.

title: Doxytech 100 (10 Ml) Doxycycline 100 Mg By Protech
name: Doxytech 100 (10 Ml) Doxycycline 100 Mg By Protech
searchText: Doxytech 100 (10 Ml) Doxycycline 100 Mg By Protech Protech DOXYTECH100
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Doxycycline is an antibiotic used to treat a range of bacterial infections, including certain infections of the skin, lungs, urinary tract and other body areas. It should be used only for infections confirmed or considered likely to be bacterial.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth and survival, helping control the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course. Swallow with a full glass of water while sitting or standing, and avoid lying down immediately afterwards. Antacids and supplements containing iron, calcium or magnesium can reduce its absorption; ask a doctor or pharmacist how to space them apart.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, indigestion and increased sensitivity to sunlight.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in children, especially those under 8 years. Use sun protection and avoid excessive sunlight. Tell the doctor about allergies and any liver problems. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, difficulty swallowing, severe headache or vision changes, or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Drotaverine injection is used to relieve painful spasms or cramps of smooth muscles, especially in the stomach and intestines. It may also be prescribed for spasms of the bile ducts or urinary tract.

How does it work?
It relaxes the smooth muscles in internal organs, helping reduce spasms and cramp-like pain.

How to take/use it
This injection should be given only by a doctor or other trained healthcare professional. The dose, route and frequency depend on the condition being treated; do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, palpitations, flushing or a fall in blood pressure may occur. Injection-site discomfort or allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about low blood pressure, severe liver, kidney or heart problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and any medicine allergies. Avoid driving if dizziness occurs. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, severe weakness, difficulty breathing, facial swelling or other signs of a serious allergic reaction.

title: Edarapro 20 (20 Ml) Edaravone By Protech
name: Edarapro 20 (20 Ml) Edaravone By Protech
searchText: Edarapro 20 (20 Ml) Edaravone By Protech Protech EDARAPRO20
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Edaravone is mainly used to help slow the loss of physical function in adults with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a progressive disease affecting nerve cells that control muscles. In some countries and formulations, it is also used for acute ischemic stroke; the approved use depends on the product and local medical guidance.

How does it work?
Edaravone helps remove harmful free radicals and may reduce oxidative damage to nerve cells. This may help slow disease-related nerve and muscle deterioration in ALS.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a specialist. The route and schedule depend on the formulation; some forms are given by intravenous infusion by a healthcare professional, while others are taken by mouth. Follow the product-specific instructions and do not change or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Bruising, headache, difficulty walking, skin irritation or rash, and tiredness may occur. Side effects can vary with the formulation.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to edaravone or other ingredients, and about asthma or previous reactions to medicines or infusions. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, dizziness, or fainting, as these may indicate a serious allergic reaction. Medical supervision is required during treatment.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Enoxaparin is an anticoagulant used to prevent and treat blood clots in the veins. It is commonly used after surgery, during hospital stays or periods of reduced movement, and in some heart-related conditions as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the blood’s ability to form clots by blocking clotting factor Xa. This helps prevent existing clots from getting larger and reduces the risk of new clots forming.

How to take/use it
This medicine is usually injected under the skin, often by a healthcare professional or after proper instruction. Use it exactly as prescribed. Do not inject it into a muscle, and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Bruising, pain or redness at the injection site, bleeding, and anaemia may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any bleeding disorder, low platelet count, kidney disease, stomach ulcer, recent surgery, or allergy to heparin. Inform the doctor before spinal or epidural procedures. Do not take aspirin, ibuprofen or other blood-thinning medicines unless advised. Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe headache, sudden weakness, or difficulty breathing.

title: Enoxatech 60 Pfs (Pfs) Enoxaparin 60 Mg Inj By Protech
name: Enoxatech 60 Pfs (Pfs) Enoxaparin 60 Mg Inj By Protech
searchText: Enoxatech 60 Pfs (Pfs) Enoxaparin 60 Mg Inj By Protech Protech ENOXATECH60PFS
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Enoxaparin is an anticoagulant used to prevent and treat blood clots in the veins, such as deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). It is also used to reduce the risk of clots during hospitalisation or around certain surgeries.

How does it work?
It reduces the blood’s ability to form harmful clots by increasing the action of antithrombin, mainly against clotting factor Xa.

How to take/use it
This medicine is usually given as an injection under the skin, as prescribed. It should not be injected into a muscle. Follow the prescribed dose and schedule, do not stop it or change the dose without medical advice, and do not rub the injection site after use.

Common side effects
Bruising, pain or redness at the injection site, bleeding, and anaemia may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any bleeding disorder, stomach ulcer, kidney disease, liver disease, recent surgery, or planned surgery or dental procedure. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially other blood thinners, aspirin, ibuprofen, or similar painkillers. Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe headache, sudden weakness, or breathing difficulty.

title: Esomtech 40 (10 Ml) Esomeprazole 40 Mg By Protech
name: Esomtech 40 (10 Ml) Esomeprazole 40 Mg By Protech
searchText: Esomtech 40 (10 Ml) Esomeprazole 40 Mg By Protech Protech ESOMTECH40
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Esomeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD) and related irritation of the food pipe. It may also be used for certain stomach ulcers and other acid-related conditions when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that blocks the release of acid in the stomach. This helps relieve acid-related symptoms and allows irritation or ulcers to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before food. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies and all other medicines being taken, especially clopidogrel, warfarin, digoxin or medicines for HIV. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, persistent vomiting or symptoms that do not improve. Long-term use should be taken only under medical supervision.

title: Feripenam 500Mg (10 Ml) Ferric Carboxymaltose 500 Mg/10 Ml By Protech

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to treat iron deficiency, including iron deficiency anaemia, when oral iron is not suitable, does not work well, or iron needs to be replaced quickly.

How does it work?
Ferric carboxymaltose supplies iron that the body uses to make haemoglobin and red blood cells. It also helps replenish the body's stored iron.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given only by a healthcare professional through a vein (intravenous injection or infusion). The dose and number of treatments depend on the severity of iron deficiency and the individual's iron needs. It must not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, dizziness, flushing, high blood pressure, and reactions at the injection site. Low phosphate levels may occur, especially with repeated treatment.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any previous allergy to intravenous iron, iron overload, liver disease, or other medical conditions. The patient should be monitored during and shortly after administration because serious allergic reactions can rarely occur. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, fainting, or chest tightness.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Fosfomycin is an antibacterial medicine used to treat certain bacterial infections. The exact infection it treats depends on the prescribed formulation and the doctor’s assessment. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking an early step needed to build their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. The route of use depends on the formulation; injectable fosfomycin must be given by a healthcare professional. Do not change the dose or stop treatment early unless advised by the doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach upset, headache, and injection-site discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to fosfomycin or other antibiotics, kidney problems, or a history of severe diarrhoea after antibiotic use. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, or other signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by susceptible bacteria, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, abdomen, bones or joints, and blood. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection, kidney function and other medical factors. Complete the prescribed course unless the healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain or irritation at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash and temporary changes in liver blood tests may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there has been an allergy to cefuroxime, cephalosporins, penicillins or other antibiotics, or if there is kidney disease. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty or a severe skin reaction. Contact a doctor for severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, as this may occur during or after antibiotic treatment.

Cefuroxime injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, bones and joints, abdomen, or blood. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Do not self-inject, and use it only as prescribed.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea or vomiting; and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics, or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related severe diarrhoea, or any medicine being used. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
This antibiotic injection is used to treat certain bacterial infections. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor and is not effective against viral infections such as colds or flu.

Cefuroxime stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps cefuroxime work against some bacteria that can resist certain antibiotics.

This medicine is given as an injection by a doctor or nurse. The dose and duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and medical advice. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Pain or redness at the injection site, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefuroxime, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, kidney problems, or a previous episode of severe antibiotic-associated diarrhoea. bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Furosemide injection is used to remove excess fluid from the body (oedema), including fluid buildup related to heart failure, kidney disease or liver disease. It may also be used for urgent fluid buildup in the lungs and, in some cases, to help control high blood pressure.

How does it work?
It is a loop diuretic, or “water tablet” medicine. It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water through the urine, reducing fluid buildup and sometimes lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein or muscle by a doctor or other trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the medical condition and response to treatment. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, low blood pressure, dehydration, weakness, nausea and changes in blood salts such as low potassium or sodium.

Precautions
Medical monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function, hydration and blood salts may be needed. Tell the healthcare professional about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, gout, diabetes, difficulty passing urine or hearing problems. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, severe weakness, confusion, very little urine or new hearing or ringing problems.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Ganciclovir is an antiviral medicine used to treat serious cytomegalovirus (CMV) infections, especially in people with weakened immunity. It may also be used for CMV retinitis and, in some cases, to prevent CMV infection after an organ transplant.

How does it work?
It blocks the ability of CMV to make new copies of itself, helping control the infection.

How to take/use it
This 500 mg medicine is usually given by a healthcare professional, often into a vein. The exact dose and treatment duration depend on the infection, kidney function and blood test results. Do not self-administer or change the treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Low white blood cell, red blood cell or platelet counts; nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, headache and tiredness.

Precautions
Regular blood and kidney-function tests are usually needed. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, low blood counts, pregnancy, plans for pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for unusual bleeding, severe weakness, fever, signs of infection or a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Gentamicin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, particularly those caused by certain Gram-negative bacteria. It is usually used in hospitals or under close medical supervision.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from multiplying.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a muscle or vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the infection, kidney function and other factors. Do not self-inject or use it without medical supervision.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain, nausea, headache and dizziness may occur. Serious effects can include kidney problems, ringing in the ears, hearing loss or balance problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, hearing or balance disorders, pregnancy, or dehydration. Kidney function and, when needed, blood levels and hearing may be monitored during treatment. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that can affect the kidneys, hearing or muscles. Seek medical help for reduced urination, severe dizziness, ringing in the ears, hearing changes, breathing difficulty or unusual muscle weakness.

What is it used for?
Glutathione 1200 mg is used as a dietary supplement to provide glutathione, a naturally occurring antioxidant in the body. It is not a substitute for treatment of a medical condition unless advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Glutathione helps neutralise reactive molecules and supports the body's normal antioxidant defences.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Some people may experience nausea, bloating, abdominal discomfort or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Check with a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking regular medicines. Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe or persistent side effects occur.

Glutathione is used as an antioxidant supplement to support the body's natural antioxidant and cellular protection systems. It is not a replacement for treatment of any medical condition.

Glutathione is a naturally occurring antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative damage and supports normal detoxification processes in the body.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. The dosage form and route are not specified here; if it is an injectable product, it should be administered only by a qualified healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Side effects depend on the dosage form. Oral products may cause stomach upset, bloating, abdominal cramps or loose stools. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or allergy. Do not self-administer an injectable form. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or severe rash.

What is it used for?
L-Ornithine L-Aspartate injection is used to help lower high ammonia levels in the blood, especially in people with liver disease and hepatic encephalopathy. It may help improve symptoms such as confusion caused by this condition.

How does it work?
It helps the body convert ammonia into less harmful substances that can be removed through the urea cycle or used to make glutamine.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse, usually into a vein. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and medical advice. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects

How does it work?
It increases the action of antithrombin, a natural substance that slows the blood-clotting process. This helps prevent existing clots from getting larger and reduces the formation of new clots.

Use only as prescribed by a doctor or healthcare professional. The dose, route and duration depend on the condition and blood-clotting test results. Do not self-administer or change the dose. This medicine may require regular monitoring.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any bleeding disorder, low platelet count, stomach ulcer, recent surgery, uncontrolled high blood pressure, liver or kidney problems, or previous reaction to heparin. Hydroxyprogesterone injection is a prescription hormonal medicine used by specialist doctors for progesterone support during pregnancy, including in selected cases to help reduce the risk of preterm birth. How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone. Progesterone helps support the lining of the uterus and maintain hormonal support during pregnancy.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection by a healthcare professional. The dose and injection schedule depend on the reason for treatment, so it should be used only as prescribed. Do not self-inject or change the schedule without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain, swelling or itching at the injection site, headache, dizziness, nausea, tiredness, breast tenderness and changes in vaginal bleeding or menstrual pattern.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of blood clots, liver disease, hormone-sensitive cancer, unexplained vaginal bleeding, depression or allergies to hormonal medicines. Citicoline is used as part of treatment and recovery support after stroke or head injury. It may also be prescribed for certain problems involving memory, thinking or other brain functions, depending on the doctor's assessment.

How does it work?
Citicoline helps provide building blocks for nerve-cell membranes and supports brain-cell function. It may also influence certain chemical messengers involved in brain activity.

How to take/use it
This 2 mL injection should be given only by a healthcare professional, by the prescribed route and schedule. Do not self-inject or change the dose without medical advice.

Headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach upset and difficulty sleeping may occur. Tell a healthcare professional if these effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to citicoline, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all medicines being used. Extra care may be needed with medicines used for Parkinson’s disease. Seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction or any sudden worsening of neurological symptoms.

How does it work?
Citicoline helps support the structure of nerve-cell membranes and the production of certain brain chemicals involved in nerve signalling.

How to take/use it
This 4 mL injection should be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, route and duration depend on the condition being treated and the prescribed medical advice. Do not self-inject.

Headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach discomfort, restlessness or difficulty sleeping may occur. Most side effects are mild, but medical advice should be sought if they are severe or persistent.

Metoclopramide injection is used to prevent or treat nausea and vomiting. It may also be used to help the stomach empty more quickly in certain digestive conditions.

It blocks dopamine signals in the vomiting centre of the brain and helps movement of food through the upper digestive system.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection, usually by a doctor or nurse. Use it only as prescribed and do not self-inject. The dose and treatment duration depend on the medical condition and response to treatment.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, restlessness, headache, dizziness, diarrhoea and weakness.

Tell the doctor if there is bowel blockage or bleeding, epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, kidney or liver problems, or a history of involuntary movements. Promethazine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as itching, rashes and runny nose. It may also be used to prevent or treat nausea and vomiting, including motion sickness, when prescribed.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions. It also acts on areas of the brain that trigger nausea and vomiting, and can cause drowsiness.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The dose, route and duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject; if this is an injectable product, it should be administered by a trained healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision and constipation may occur.

Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or less alert. How does it work?
It damages the outer membrane of susceptible bacteria, causing the bacteria to die.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The dose, treatment duration and method of administration depend on the infection and formulation. Injectable forms must be given by a healthcare professional; do not self-administer.

Common side effects
Kidney problems, tingling or numbness, dizziness, muscle weakness, and allergic reactions may occur. Side effects can be serious, particularly with injectable treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, neuromuscular disorders, or any previous allergy to polymyxins. Kidney function may need monitoring during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for reduced urination, severe weakness, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a widespread rash.

Propofol is an intravenous medicine used by healthcare professionals to start and maintain general anaesthesia during surgery. It may also be used to provide sedation for certain medical procedures and, in specialist settings, for patients receiving intensive care.

How does it work?
Propofol slows activity in the brain by enhancing the effect of a natural calming chemical called GABA. This produces sleep and loss of awareness; it does not provide pain relief on its own.

How to take/use it
Propofol is given into a vein by an anaesthetist or other trained healthcare professional in a hospital or clinical setting. Breathing, blood pressure, heart rate and oxygen levels must be closely monitored during use.

Common side effects
Pain or discomfort at the injection site, low blood pressure, slow or shallow breathing, temporary pauses in breathing, nausea, vomiting, dizziness and drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
It must only be administered where equipment and trained staff are available to support breathing and circulation. Tell the doctor about allergies, breathing problems, heart or blood-pressure problems, liver or kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all medicines being used. Do not drive, drink alcohol or make important decisions until the effects have fully worn off and medical advice permits it.

Propofol is an intravenous anaesthetic used in hospitals to induce and maintain general anaesthesia during surgery. It may also be used to provide sedation for certain medical procedures or for patients receiving intensive care.

How does it work?
It acts on the brain to reduce activity and produce sleep-like unconsciousness and sedation. It also reduces awareness of pain and other sensations during anaesthesia.

How to take/use it
Propofol is given into a vein by a trained anaesthetist or other qualified healthcare professional. The dose is individually adjusted, and breathing, blood pressure, heart rate and oxygen levels must be closely monitored. It must not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Pain or burning at the injection site, low blood pressure, slowed or stopped breathing, slow heartbeat, nausea, vomiting, dizziness and confusion on waking.

Precautions
It should only be used where airway and breathing support equipment and trained medical staff are available. Extra care is needed in people with breathing or heart problems, low blood pressure, or allergies to propofol or its ingredients. Seek urgent medical attention for severe breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, or loss of consciousness that does not improve after the procedure.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, age and other medical factors. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, rash and changes in liver test results may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it without medical supervision. Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefotaxime, cephalosporins, penicillins or other antibiotics, and about kidney disease. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor if severe or persistent diarrhoea develops during or after treatment.

Cefotaxime kills bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps cefotaxime work against bacteria that can resist some antibiotics.

It acts like the natural hormone somatostatin and reduces the release of several hormones and other substances in the body, including growth hormone and substances that increase intestinal secretions.

Iohexol is a contrast medium used during certain X-rays, CT scans, angiograms and other imaging tests. It helps blood vessels, organs or body tissues show up more clearly on the images. It is used for diagnosis, not to treat a disease.

How does it work?
Iohexol contains iodine, which absorbs X-rays. This creates greater contrast between different tissues and makes the area being examined easier to see.

How to take/use it
Iohexol is given by injection or through another route by a trained healthcare professional before or during the imaging test. It must not be self-administered. Follow the instructions provided by the radiology team, including any advice about fluids or eating and drinking.

Common side effects
A temporary warm or flushed feeling, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, or pain and discomfort at the injection site may occur. Most reactions are mild and short-lasting.

Precautions
Tell the doctor or radiology team about any previous reaction to contrast media, kidney problems, thyroid disease, asthma, allergies, pregnancy or breastfeeding. How does it work?
It blocks acid-producing pumps in the stomach lining, reducing the amount of acid released into the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is commonly taken before food, but follow the instructions on the prescription or package.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to rabeprazole or similar medicines, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and other medicines being used. Long-term use may require medical monitoring. How to take/use it
This injection must be given into a vein or muscle by a healthcare professional. The dose and duration depend on the condition and should be decided by the doctor. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or constipation may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, previous allergy to ranitidine, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, confusion or an irregular heartbeat.

Use in the eyes exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before use and do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. Do not use if the solution is cloudy or the seal is damaged.

Temporary blurred vision, mild stinging, burning or eye irritation may occur after use.

Seek medical advice if eye pain, marked redness, discharge or vision changes occur, or if symptoms do not improve. People who wear contact lenses should check the product instructions before use. Stop using it and seek advice if irritation is severe or persistent.

Teicoplanin is given as an injection or infusion by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or clinic. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, and response to treatment. Complete the prescribed course and do not self-administer it.

It prevents susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall, which stops them from growing and helps clear the infection.

Terlipressin is used in hospitals to treat serious complications of advanced liver disease, especially hepatorenal syndrome, a condition in which kidney function worsens. It may also be used to help control bleeding from enlarged veins in the food pipe (oesophageal varices).

How does it work?
It acts like vasopressin and narrows certain blood vessels, especially those supplying the digestive organs. This can increase blood pressure and improve blood flow to the kidneys, while also helping reduce bleeding from varices.

How to take/use it
Terlipressin is given by injection or infusion by a doctor or trained healthcare professional, usually in a hospital. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and response to treatment. It requires close monitoring.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, headache, pale skin, increased blood pressure, slow or irregular heartbeat, low sodium levels, and breathing difficulty due to fluid in the lungs may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart or blood-vessel disease, high blood pressure, irregular heartbeat, breathing problems, kidney problems, or pregnancy. How does it work?
Thiamine is converted into an active form that helps the body produce energy from carbohydrates and supports normal nerve and heart function.

How to take/use it
This injection should be given by a healthcare professional. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the severity of deficiency and the individual's medical condition.

Pain, redness or discomfort at the injection site; nausea or sweating may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon but can be serious.

Tell the healthcare professional about any previous allergy to thiamine or this medicine. It should be administered under medical supervision because serious allergic reactions can rarely occur. Thiopentone injection is mainly used in hospitals to induce general anaesthesia before surgery or other procedures. It may also be used by specialists to control certain severe seizures.

How does it work?

title: 1000 Paraultra Iv (100Ml) Paracetamol Infusion 1.0% W/V by RPG
name: 1000 Paraultra Iv (100Ml) Paracetamol Infusion 1.0% W/V by RPG
searchText: 1000 Paraultra Iv (100Ml) Paracetamol Infusion 1.0% W/V by RPG RPG 1000PARAULTRAIV
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Paracetamol Infusion is used for short-term relief of moderate pain and reduction of fever, especially when medicine cannot be taken by mouth or when an intravenous medicine is needed.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that contribute to pain and fever. It mainly acts in the brain and does not significantly reduce inflammation.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a healthcare professional. The prescribed amount and treatment duration depend on the patient's condition. Do not use other medicines containing paracetamol unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, and discomfort at the infusion site may occur. Serious allergic reactions and liver problems are uncommon but require urgent medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about liver disease, kidney problems, dehydration, poor nutrition, regular alcohol use, or allergy to paracetamol. Do not exceed the prescribed amount, as overdose can cause serious liver damage. Seek urgent help for a rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, severe weakness, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

title: Acloultra Mr (20X10'S) Aceclofenac 100 Mg Paracetamol 325 Mg Chlorzoxazone 250 Mg by RPG
name: Acloultra Mr (20X10'S) Aceclofenac 100 Mg Paracetamol 325 Mg Chlorzoxazone 250 Mg by RPG
searchText: Acloultra Mr (20X10'S) Aceclofenac 100 Mg Paracetamol 325 Mg Chlorzoxazone 250 Mg by RPG RPG ACLOULTRAMR
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of painful muscle and joint conditions associated with inflammation and muscle spasms.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac and paracetamol help reduce pain and inflammation. Chlorzoxazone acts on the central nervous system to help relax painful muscle spasms.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount, or combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or aceclofenac unless advised by a doctor. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving if affected.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness and the risk of liver damage. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

title: Acyultra 10 Gm Oint (10 Gm (14)) Acyclovir 5% W/W by RPG
name: Acyultra 10 Gm Oint (10 Gm (14)) Acyclovir 5% W/W by RPG
searchText: Acyultra 10 Gm Oint (10 Gm (14)) Acyclovir 5% W/W by RPG RPG ACYULTRA10GMOINT
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Acyclovir 5% ointment is used to treat herpes simplex infections of the skin, including cold sores and genital herpes sores.

How does it work?
It is an antiviral medicine that blocks the ability of the herpes virus to multiply, helping the sores heal.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin as directed by a doctor or the product label. Wash hands before and after use. Avoid applying it to the eyes, inside the mouth, or other areas unless specifically advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes. Do not pick or touch the sores unnecessarily, and wash hands regularly to reduce spreading the infection. Acyclovir does not remove the virus from the body or reliably prevent transmission. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, does not improve, or if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

title: Ampoclav 250 Cap (G/Y) (30X10'S) Amoxycillin 250Mg by RPG
name: Ampoclav 250 Cap (G/Y) (30X10'S) Amoxycillin 250Mg by RPG
searchText: Ampoclav 250 Cap (G/Y) (30X10'S) Amoxycillin 250Mg by RPG RPG AMPOCLAV250CAPGY
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amoxycillin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from making a protective cell wall, which stops the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at evenly spaced times, with water. Complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not take leftover antibiotics or share this medicine with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to amoxycillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, a severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

title: Ampoclav 250 Rw (30X10'S) Amoxycillin 250Mg by RPG
name: Ampoclav 250 Rw (30X10'S) Amoxycillin 250Mg by RPG
searchText: Ampoclav 250 Rw (30X10'S) Amoxycillin 250Mg by RPG RPG AMPOCLAV250RW
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amoxycillin is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by susceptible bacteria, such as certain infections of the ear, throat, chest, urinary tract and skin. It does not work for viral infections such as common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with the formation of their protective cell wall, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Do not share antibiotics or use leftover medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a previous serious allergy to amoxycillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or a history of antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, a severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

title: Ampoclav 625 Tab (20X1X10'S) Amoxycillin 500 Mg. Potassium Clavulanate 125Mg. by RPG
name: Ampoclav 625 Tab (20X1X10'S) Amoxycillin 500 Mg. Potassium Clavulanate 125Mg. by RPG
searchText: Ampoclav 625 Tab (20X1X10'S) Amoxycillin 500 Mg. Potassium Clavulanate 125Mg. by RPG RPG AMPOCLAV625TAB
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amoxicillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, sinuses, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxicillin kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps prevent certain bacteria from breaking down amoxicillin, making the antibiotic effective against some resistant bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Swallow with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share antibiotics or use leftover medicine.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take this medicine if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin, clavulanic acid or related antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver disease and any previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

title: Ampoclav-Safe Syp (30Ml) Amoxycillin Trihydrate 200Mg Potassium Clavulanate 28.5Mg by RPG
name: Ampoclav-Safe Syp (30Ml) Amoxycillin Trihydrate 200Mg Potassium Clavulanate 28.5Mg by RPG
searchText: Ampoclav-Safe Syp (30Ml) Amoxycillin Trihydrate 200Mg Potassium Clavulanate 28.5Mg by RPG RPG AMPOCLAVSAFESYP
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, sinuses, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps amoxycillin remain effective against bacteria that can otherwise break it down.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Take each dose at the recommended time and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Taking it at the start of a meal may help reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics or any of its ingredients. Tell the doctor about previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, kidney disease, glandular fever, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe skin rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Antibiotics should be used only when prescribed.

title: Arpicef 100Mg D.S 30Ml (30Ml) Cefixime 100Mg. by RPG
name: Arpicef 100Mg D.S 30Ml (30Ml) Cefixime 100Mg. by RPG
searchText: Arpicef 100Mg D.S 30Ml (30Ml) Cefixime 100Mg. by RPG RPG ARPICEFDS
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, airways, urinary tract and other areas, when caused by bacteria sensitive to it. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not share this medicine or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, vomiting and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor if there is an allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or penicillin-type antibiotics, or if there is kidney disease. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, bloody stools, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

title: Arpicef 200 Tab (20X10'S) Cefixime Dispersible 200Mg by RPG
name: Arpicef 200 Tab (20X10'S) Cefixime Dispersible 200Mg by RPG
searchText: Arpicef 200 Tab (20X10'S) Cefixime Dispersible 200Mg by RPG RPG ARPICEF200TAB
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, airways, urinary tract and other areas, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Disperse the tablet in water as directed on the pack or by the pharmacist, and take it immediately after it has dispersed. Do not share or reuse leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and vomiting may occur. Mild rash or headache can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or penicillin, or if there is kidney disease. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially if it contains blood. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can lead to resistance.

title: Arpicef 50Mg D.S 30Ml (30Ml) Cefixime 50Mg. by RPG
name: Arpicef 50Mg D.S 30Ml (30Ml) Cefixime 50Mg. by RPG
searchText: Arpicef 50Mg D.S 30Ml (30Ml) Cefixime 50Mg. by RPG RPG ARPICEF50MGDS
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, ears, airways and urinary tract. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and headache. Mild skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to cefixime, penicillin or other cephalosporin antibiotics, kidney problems, or a history of severe diarrhoea after antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

title: Arpicef Cv Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefixime 200Mg, Potassium Clavulanate 125Mg. by RPG
name: Arpicef Cv Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefixime 200Mg, Potassium Clavulanate 125Mg. by RPG
searchText: Arpicef Cv Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefixime 200Mg, Potassium Clavulanate 125Mg. by RPG RPG ARPICEFCVTAB
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to treat bacterial infections caused by bacteria susceptible to cefixime and clavulanate. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime stops bacteria from building their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate blocks certain enzymes made by bacteria that can make them resistant to cefixime.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Follow the product label or prescriber's instructions, and do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion and headache. Skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the prescriber about any allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporins or penicillin-type antibiotics, and about kidney or liver problems. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, a severe rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

title: Arpicef O Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefixime 200Mg, Ofloxacin 200Mg by RPG
name: Arpicef O Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefixime 200Mg, Ofloxacin 200Mg by RPG
searchText: Arpicef O Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefixime 200Mg, Ofloxacin 200Mg by RPG RPG ARPICEFOTAB
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat certain bacterial infections when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime damages the bacterial cell wall. Ofloxacin stops bacteria from copying their genetic material, helping to kill the bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not take antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc at the same time; follow the prescribed time gap. Do not share or reuse leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion, headache, dizziness and skin rash.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to penicillin, cephalosporins or quinolone antibiotics, kidney disease, seizures, tendon problems, heart rhythm problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for breathing difficulty, severe or persistent diarrhoea, tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe rash, or unusual palpitations. Use in children and older adults only when specifically prescribed.

title: Arpigyl 500 Mg Iv (100Ml) Metronidazole 500Mg by RPG
name: Arpigyl 500 Mg Iv (100Ml) Metronidazole 500Mg by RPG
searchText: Arpigyl 500 Mg Iv (100Ml) Metronidazole 500Mg by RPG RPG ARPIGYL500MGIV
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Metronidazole injection is used to treat serious infections caused by certain anaerobic bacteria and some parasites, including certain intestinal and genital infections. It may also be used to prevent certain infections around surgery when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It enters susceptible bacteria and parasites and damages their genetic material, stopping them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection and should be decided by the treating doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, metallic taste and pain or irritation at the injection site.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose. Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, a history of seizures or nerve problems, or an allergy to metronidazole. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially warfarin. Seek medical help for severe rash, numbness or tingling, seizures, confusion, or severe diarrhoea.

title: Arpiroxx 250 Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefuroxime 250 Mg by RPG
name: Arpiroxx 250 Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefuroxime 250 Mg by RPG
searchText: Arpiroxx 250 Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefuroxime 250 Mg by RPG RPG ARPIROXX250TAB
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cefuroxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, chest, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not skip doses or stop treatment early unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, cephalosporins or other penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

title: Arpiroxx 500 Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefuroxime Axetil 500Mg by RPG
name: Arpiroxx 500 Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefuroxime Axetil 500Mg by RPG
searchText: Arpiroxx 500 Tab (10X1X10'S) Cefuroxime Axetil 500Mg by RPG RPG ARPIROXX500TAB
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cefuroxime axetil is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, sinuses, ears, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it

It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

Take by mouth only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not chew or crush it. Do not use it for longer than recommended. Avoid taking it at the same time as milk or antacids.

What is it used for?
Clobetasol propionate cream is a very strong steroid used for short-term treatment of severe, inflamed and itchy skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis and psoriasis, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces inflammation, redness, swelling and itching by suppressing overactive immune reactions in the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Use it only on the skin, wash hands after applying, and avoid contact with the eyes. Do not use it for longer or on larger areas than advised. Do not cover the treated area with a tight dressing unless instructed.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, itching, dryness or irritation at the application site. Prolonged or excessive use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks, changes in skin colour, or small visible blood vessels.

Precautions
Do not use on the face, groin, underarms, broken skin or infected skin unless specifically advised. Avoid use in children unless prescribed. Seek medical advice if the condition worsens, shows signs of infection, or does not improve. Stop and seek urgent help for severe irritation or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Deflazacort is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactivity of the immune system. It may be prescribed for certain inflammatory, allergic or autoimmune conditions, depending on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Take it with food if it causes stomach discomfort. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially after prolonged use, unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Increased appetite, indigestion, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, fluid retention and increased blood sugar may occur. The risk of side effects is higher with larger doses or longer treatment.

Precautions

It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and allergic or immune reactions.

How to take/use it

Increased blood sugar, indigestion, mood or sleep changes, increased appetite, fluid retention and pain at the injection site may occur. It can also increase the risk of infections.

Precautions

How does it work?
It acts similarly to the natural hormone progesterone. This helps regulate the menstrual cycle and supports the lining of the uterus.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, breast tenderness, abdominal discomfort, spotting or changes in menstrual bleeding, and mood changes may occur.

Precautions

How to take/use it
Amikacin injection is given into a vein or muscle by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration are decided by the doctor based on the infection, kidney function and body weight. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea and vomiting may occur. This medicine can also cause kidney problems, hearing loss, ringing in the ears or balance problems.

Precautions

It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Shake the suspension well before each use and measure it with a suitable measuring device. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not use leftover medicine or share it with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and headache. Skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics, unless advised by a doctor. Inform the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, facial swelling, breathing difficulty or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from growing.

Use only as prescribed. If it is a dry syrup, prepare and measure it exactly as directed on the label, and shake the suspension well before each use. Complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not share or save leftover antibiotic.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Cefpodoxime kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps cefpodoxime work against some bacteria that can otherwise resist it.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not skip doses or share this medicine with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain and headache may occur. Mild rash can also occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporins, penicillins or related antibiotics unless specifically advised by a doctor. Inform the doctor about kidney disease or a history of severe antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotics can contribute to resistance.

searchText: Seretan Cream (30Gm (20)) Sertaconazole 2% W/W by RPG RPG SERETANCREAM
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Sertaconazole cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch and certain yeast infections of the skin.

How does it work?
It prevents fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which stops their growth and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected, clean and dry skin as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use. For external use only; avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to sertaconazole or similar antifungal medicines. Avoid applying to the eyes or inside the mouth. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs, or if the infection worsens or does not improve with treatment.

searchText: Topheal Cream (30Gm (20)) Ketoconazole 2% W/W by RPG RPG TOPHEALCREAM
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% cream is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch, pityriasis versicolor and some yeast infections of the skin.

How does it work?
It is an antifungal medicine that stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane. This helps stop the fungal infection from growing and clears the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use in the eyes or on broken skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Consult a healthcare professional if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain, inflammation and muscle spasm in musculoskeletal conditions such as back pain, sprains and strains.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain, while chlorzoxazone acts as a muscle relaxant to reduce muscle spasm.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, preferably with or after food and with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking other medicines containing diclofenac, paracetamol or similar painkillers unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if dizzy or drowsy. Use only under medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or during pregnancy. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe skin rash.

title: Amentone Tablets (10X1X10 T) Tranexamic Acid 500 Mg, Mefenamic Acid 250 Mg Tab By Zuventus
name: Amentone Tablets (10X1X10 T) Tranexamic Acid 500 Mg, Mefenamic Acid 250 Mg Tab By Zuventus
searchText: Amentone Tablets (10X1X10 T) Tranexamic Acid 500 Mg, Mefenamic Acid 250 Mg Tab By Zuventus Zuventus 423330471
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used to reduce heavy menstrual bleeding and relieve period pain or cramps.

How does it work?
Tranexamic acid helps prevent the breakdown of blood clots, reducing menstrual blood loss. Mefenamic acid reduces substances that cause pain, inflammation and menstrual cramps.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, usually during the menstrual period. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain or indigestion, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of blood clots, kidney disease, stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAID painkillers. Avoid taking it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathlessness, sudden leg swelling or pain, unusual vision changes, vomiting blood, or black stools.

title: Azilac-500 Tablets (20X1X3 T) Azithromycin 500 Mg Tab By Zuventus
name: Azilac-500 Tablets (20X1X3 T) Azithromycin 500 Mg Tab By Zuventus
searchText: Azilac-500 Tablets (20X1X3 T) Azithromycin 500 Mg Tab By Zuventus Zuventus 423331013
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Azithromycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the chest, throat, skin, ears and genital tract. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth and survival.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not skip doses or stop treatment early, even if symptoms improve. Do not share antibiotics or use leftover medicine. The dose and treatment duration depend on the infection and should be decided by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, vomiting and headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to azithromycin or other macrolide antibiotics, liver disease, heart rhythm problems or low levels of potassium or magnesium. Inform the doctor about all other medicines being taken. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, fainting, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.

title: Calobuild Tablets (20X1X15 T) Calcium 500 Mg, Cholecalciferol 250 Iu Tab By Zuventus
name: Calobuild Tablets (20X1X15 T) Calcium 500 Mg, Cholecalciferol 250 Iu Tab By Zuventus
searchText: Calobuild Tablets (20X1X15 T) Calcium 500 Mg, Cholecalciferol 250 Iu Tab By Zuventus Zuventus 423330447
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat calcium and vitamin D deficiency and to support healthy bones and teeth. It may also be used as part of bone-health treatment when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Calcium provides the mineral needed for bones, teeth, muscles and nerves. Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) helps the body absorb calcium and supports bone mineralisation.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. If taking other medicines or supplements, check with a pharmacist about the appropriate timing.

Common side effects
Constipation, stomach discomfort, bloating, nausea or vomiting may occur. Excessive calcium intake can cause increased thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or vitamin D excess. Seek medical advice if severe stomach pain, persistent vomiting, confusion or unusual weakness occurs. Calcium can affect the absorption of some medicines, including certain antibiotics, thyroid medicines and iron supplements; ask a pharmacist about spacing doses.

title: Cetlergy - 10 Tablets (40X1X10 T) Cetirizine 10 Mg Tab By Zuventus
name: Cetlergy - 10 Tablets (40X1X10 T) Cetirizine 10 Mg Tab By Zuventus
searchText: Cetlergy - 10 Tablets (40X1X10 T) Cetirizine 10 Mg Tab By Zuventus Zuventus 423331570
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin allergies such as hives and itching.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water, exactly as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. It may cause drowsiness in some people; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea, or dizziness.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful with other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Get urgent medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, or a severe allergic reaction.

title: Cetlergy Syrup 60 Ml (20X1X60 Ml) Cetirizine 5 Mg/5 Ml Syr By Zuventus
name: Cetlergy Syrup 60 Ml (20X1X60 Ml) Cetirizine 5 Mg/5 Ml Syr By Zuventus
searchText: Cetlergy Syrup 60 Ml (20X1X60 Ml) Cetirizine 5 Mg/5 Ml Syr By Zuventus Zuventus 423331066
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Cetirizine syrup is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than the recommended amount. It may cause drowsiness in some people.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and nausea may occur.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness. Consult a doctor before use in kidney disease, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction such as facial swelling, breathing difficulty, or severe rash.

title: Chyventhral Forte Tablet (10X1X20 T) Trypsin, Chymotrypsin 100,000 Armour Units (6:1) Gastro-Resistant Tab By Zuventus
name: Chyventhral Forte Tablet (10X1X20 T) Trypsin, Chymotrypsin 100,000 Armour Units (6:1) Gastro-Resistant Tab By Zuventus
searchText: Chyventhral Forte Tablet (10X1X20 T) Trypsin, Chymotrypsin 100,000 Armour Units (6:1) Gastro-Resistant Tab By Zuventus Zuventus 423331146
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Trypsin and chymotrypsin tablets are used as prescribed to help reduce swelling and inflammation associated with injuries, surgery, or other soft-tissue conditions.

How does it work?
These are proteolytic enzymes that help break down proteins involved in inflammation and swelling, which may support recovery of injured tissues.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by the doctor or product label. Swallow the gastro-resistant tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, diarrhoea, or abdominal discomfort may occur. Skin rash or other allergic reactions can occur rarely.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a bleeding or clotting disorder, an active ulcer, an allergy to these enzymes, or if blood-thinning medicines are being used. Medical advice is recommended before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding and before planned surgery. Seek urgent medical help for unusual bleeding, severe rash, swelling, or breathing difficulty.

title: Covafem Tablets (30X1X10 T) Norethisterone 5 Mg Tab By Zuventus
name: Covafem Tablets (30X1X10 T) Norethisterone 5 Mg Tab By Zuventus
searchText: Covafem Tablets (30X1X10 T) Norethisterone 5 Mg Tab By Zuventus Zuventus 423331746
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Norethisterone is used to manage heavy, painful or irregular periods and other menstrual problems. It may also be prescribed for endometriosis or to delay a period.

How does it work?
It is a synthetic form of the hormone progesterone. It helps control changes in the womb lining and regulate menstrual bleeding.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. This medicine is not a contraceptive.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, breast tenderness, bloating, mood changes, and spotting or irregular bleeding may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if pregnant unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver disease, a history of blood clots, migraine, or hormone-sensitive cancer. Seek urgent medical help for sudden chest pain, breathlessness, painful leg swelling, severe headache, vision changes, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

It kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably after food. Swallow the tablet whole with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not skip doses or share this medicine with others.

It is a synthetic substance related to testosterone. It can increase protein production in the body and may help support bone and muscle tissue.

This medicine is given as an injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject or use it without medical supervision.

Acne, oily skin, swelling or fluid retention, changes in sexual desire, mood changes, and pain at the injection site. Women may develop increased facial hair, menstrual changes, or a deeper voice.

Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about liver, kidney, heart, prostate, or breast problems, diabetes, or high cholesterol. Mifepristone blocks progesterone, a hormone needed to maintain pregnancy. Misoprostol softens the cervix and causes uterine contractions, leading to expulsion of the pregnancy.

Use only as prescribed by a qualified healthcare professional. The two medicines must be taken in the specific sequence and at the time advised. Do not use this pack without medical assessment and access to follow-up care.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if an ectopic pregnancy is suspected, if there is an intrauterine device, severe anaemia, a bleeding disorder, use of blood thinners, long-term steroid treatment or allergy to either medicine. What is it used for?
Amikacin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including certain infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, blood, bones and joints. It is usually used when other antibiotics may not be suitable. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from making proteins needed for their growth and survival.

How to take/use it
Amikacin 100 mg is usually given as an injection or infusion by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment length depend on the type and severity of infection, body weight and kidney function. Do not self-inject or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain or redness at the injection site, nausea and vomiting may occur. Serious effects can include reduced urine output, hearing changes, ringing in the ears, dizziness or problems with balance.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Kidney function and, when needed, hearing should be monitored during treatment. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that may affect the kidneys or hearing. Seek medical help promptly for hearing loss, severe dizziness, unusual weakness or reduced urination.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This combination is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections when considered appropriate by a doctor. It does not work for viral infections such as common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime damages the bacterial cell wall, while ofloxacin blocks enzymes needed for bacterial growth and reproduction. Together, they help kill susceptible bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor and complete the prescribed course. It may be taken with or without food, but follow the product label or medical advice. Do not self-medicate or share this medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and indigestion. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash, breathing difficulty, tendon pain or numbness/tingling.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to cephalosporins, penicillins or quinolone antibiotics, kidney disease, seizures, heart rhythm problems, tendon problems, or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice. Antacids and supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or aluminium may interfere with ofloxacin; ask a doctor or pharmacist about timing. Avoid unnecessary sun exposure and stop strenuous exercise if tendon pain occurs.
