What is it used for?
Bacillus clausii is a probiotic used to help restore the balance of beneficial bacteria in the intestine and support the management of diarrhoea, including diarrhoea associated with antibiotic use. It should be used along with adequate fluids and oral rehydration when needed.

How does it work?
It contains live Bacillus clausii spores that reach the intestine and help support a healthier balance of gut bacteria. This may help reduce the growth of harmful microorganisms.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not mix it with hot liquids. If taking antibiotics, follow the product or healthcare professional’s instructions on timing.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Mild gas, bloating, nausea or abdominal discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice if diarrhoea is severe, bloody, associated with dehydration, or does not improve. People with severely weakened immunity, serious illness, or a central venous catheter should consult a doctor before using it. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

Amoxicillin kills susceptible bacteria by damaging their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid blocks enzymes that can make some bacteria resistant to amoxicillin, helping the antibiotic work effectively.

Use only as prescribed and follow the instructions for the specific product and route of administration. Take doses at evenly spaced times and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them for future illnesses.

What is it used for?
Hydroxyzine is mainly used to relieve itching caused by allergies or certain skin conditions. It may also be prescribed to reduce anxiety and tension or to cause short-term calming or drowsiness.

It blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergic symptoms and itching. It also acts on the brain to produce a calming and sedating effect.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed or directed on the product label. Do not take more than recommended. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and take care with other medicines that cause drowsiness, including sleeping tablets, sedatives and some pain medicines. Orlistat is used with a reduced-calorie diet and physical activity to help manage obesity and support weight loss in suitable adults.

How does it work?
It blocks enzymes that digest dietary fat in the intestine. This reduces the amount of fat absorbed by the body, so some undigested fat leaves the body in the stools.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, usually with meals as directed. Follow a reduced-calorie, lower-fat diet to reduce stomach and bowel-related side effects. Do not take more than prescribed. A doctor may recommend a multivitamin because orlistat can reduce absorption of vitamins A, D, E and K.

Common side effects
Oily or fatty stools, increased bowel movements, sudden urge to pass stools, loose stools, gas with discharge, and stomach discomfort or cramps.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor if there is chronic malabsorption, reduced bile flow, liver or kidney disease, or if taking medicines such as warfarin, ciclosporin, thyroid medicines or medicines for seizures. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or allergic symptoms.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and suppress overactive immune reactions. It may be prescribed for severe allergies, inflammatory or autoimmune conditions, and other medical conditions; the exact use depends on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It acts like natural corticosteroid hormones and reduces inflammation and immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially after prolonged use. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention, and increased blood sugar may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental-health conditions, or any infection. Dexamethasone can reduce resistance to infection and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically advised. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune reactions. It may be prescribed for severe allergies, asthma flare-ups, autoimmune or other inflammatory conditions, and certain serious medical conditions under specialist supervision.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune activity.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed. If taken by mouth, take it with food to reduce stomach upset. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially after prolonged use, unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, facial swelling, fluid retention, increased blood sugar and increased susceptibility to infections may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Inform the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions or an ongoing infection. Dexamethasone can mask infection symptoms and may interact with other medicines. Seek medical advice for signs of infection, severe mood changes, vision problems or unusual swelling.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and control overactive immune reactions. It may be prescribed for severe allergies, swelling, autoimmune conditions and other inflammatory illnesses, depending on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and suppresses an overactive immune response.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed, following the recommended route and schedule. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially after prolonged use, unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention and increased blood sugar may occur. Longer use can increase the risk of infections, weight gain and bone thinning.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions or any infection. Avoid contact with people who have infections and check before receiving vaccines, especially live vaccines. Seek medical advice for signs of infection or severe mood changes.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Diclofenac 75 mg is used to relieve pain and reduce inflammation in conditions such as arthritis, muscle pain, joint pain, sprains and other painful inflammatory conditions.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. If it is an oral medicine, take it with or after food and swallow it with water. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid diclofenac if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney or liver disease, severe heart disease, or an allergy to NSAIDs such as ibuprofen or aspirin, unless specifically advised by a doctor. It may increase the risk of stomach bleeding, heart problems and kidney problems, especially with prolonged use. Avoid combining it with other NSAIDs or blood thinners unless advised. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy, particularly after 20 weeks or in the last 3 months, and if there is asthma, high blood pressure or heart disease.

title: Zydiclo Inj. (3ml)Diclofenac 25 Mg by Zydus
name: Zydiclo Inj. (3ml)Diclofenac 25 Mg by Zydus
searchText: Zydiclo Inj. (3ml)Diclofenac 25 Mg by Zydus Zydus 5000876
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Diclofenac is used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use diclofenac exactly as prescribed or directed on the product label. If it is an oral medicine, taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Avoid diclofenac if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, serious kidney, liver or heart disease, or an allergy to diclofenac, aspirin or other NSAIDs, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty or facial swelling. Do not combine it with other NSAID painkillers without medical advice. Tell the doctor if pregnant, especially after 20 weeks or during the last 3 months, or if taking blood thinners, steroids or medicines for blood pressure or kidney problems.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve occasional constipation and make stools softer and easier to pass.

How does it work?
Liquid paraffin lubricates the stool, while magnesium hydroxide draws water into the bowel to soften it. Sodium picosulfate stimulates bowel movement.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Measure the liquid accurately and do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Drink adequate fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, loose stools or diarrhoea, nausea, bloating and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is severe or unexplained abdominal pain, vomiting, bowel blockage or rectal bleeding. Seek medical advice if constipation persists or keeps returning. Use cautiously in kidney disease or dehydration. Prolonged or excessive use may cause fluid or electrolyte imbalance and should be avoided. Keep out of reach of children; liquid paraffin can be harmful if accidentally inhaled.

title: Zydopenam SB (1.5GM)Meropenem 1000 Mg + Sulbactam 500 Mg by Zydus
name: Zydopenam SB (1.5GM)Meropenem 1000 Mg + Sulbactam 500 Mg by Zydus
searchText: Zydopenam SB (1.5GM)Meropenem 1000 Mg + Sulbactam 500 Mg by Zydus Zydus 5044407
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Meropenem with sulbactam is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, particularly infections caused by bacteria that may resist some other antibiotics. It is generally used in hospitals or under close medical supervision.

How does it work?
Meropenem kills bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Sulbactam blocks enzymes made by some bacteria that can otherwise reduce the effect of antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection or infusion by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and medical advice. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, skin rash and pain, redness or swelling at the injection site may occur. Changes in liver or blood test results are also possible.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to meropenem, sulbactam, penicillins, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney disease. Tell the doctor about a history of seizures or brain disorders, and about use of valproate medicines. Seek medical attention for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can cause resistance.

title: ZYDOPENEM INJECTION 1GM (1G.Vial)Meropenem 1000 Mg by Zydus

searchText: ZYDOPENEM INJECTION 1GM (1G.Vial)Meropenem 1000 Mg by Zydus Zydus 5023876
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Meropenem is an injectable antibiotic used in hospitals to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, blood, and brain. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Meropenem is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, age, and medical condition. It should not be self-injected or stopped early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, skin rash, and pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to meropenem, penicillin, cephalosporin, or other antibiotics, and about any history of seizures or kidney disease. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, seizures, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Antibiotics should be used only when prescribed.

title: Zydryl-LS 100 ml Syp. (100ml.)Levosalbutamol 1 Mg + Ambroxol 30 Mg + Guaifenesin 50 Mg by Zydus

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with phlegm and chest congestion. It may also help open narrowed airways when coughing is associated with wheezing or breathing difficulty.

How does it work?
Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles of the airways to improve airflow. Ambroxol and guaifenesin help loosen and thin mucus, making it easier to cough out.

How to take/use it
Take it only in the dose and for the duration prescribed by the doctor or stated on the label. Do not exceed the recommended dose or use it for longer than advised. If it is a liquid, measure it with the supplied measuring device.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache, shakiness, nervousness, or a fast heartbeat/palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain, severe palpitations, or an allergic or blistering skin reaction. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if allergic to any ingredient.

Used for temporary relief of cough, including cough associated with a cold. It may help soothe throat irritation and loosen mucus.

How does it work?
Diphenhydramine helps reduce cough and allergy-related symptoms, while ammonium chloride and sodium citrate help loosen and clear mucus. Menthol provides a cooling, soothing effect in the throat.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not use for longer than advised if the cough does not improve.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, thickened mucus, nausea or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol until the effect is known. Use carefully in older adults and in people with glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems or severe liver disease. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Use in children only as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice for breathing difficulty, high fever, coughing up blood, or a persistent or worsening cough.

Used for temporary relief of cough and throat irritation, particularly with the common cold. It may help suppress coughing and loosen mucus.

Diphenhydramine helps reduce the urge to cough and may cause drowsiness. Ammonium chloride helps loosen mucus, while sodium citrate and menthol soothe throat irritation.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Use a proper measuring device if it is supplied as a liquid. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol. Do not combine with other medicines that cause drowsiness unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek advice before use in young children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is asthma, breathing difficulty or persistent cough. Seek medical care if the cough is severe, lasts several days or is accompanied by high fever or breathing difficulty.

Used to relieve a wet or productive cough with thick mucus and to help open the airways when wheezing or bronchospasm is present.

Ambroxol and guaifenesin help loosen and clear mucus from the airways. Terbutaline relaxes the airway muscles, helping improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Do not combine with other cough or cold medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache, tremors, nervousness, palpitations or a fast heartbeat.

Use only on medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, seizures or a history of irregular heartbeat. None expected when used correctly.

Do not use if the thermometer is damaged. Keep it away from children unless supervised, and do not allow them to chew or swallow any part. Follow the manufacturer’s cleaning, storage and battery instructions.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
It is used as an omega-3 dietary supplement to provide EPA and DHA, which are important fatty acids. A healthcare professional may recommend omega-3 products to help manage high triglyceride levels.

How does it work?
EPA and DHA are incorporated into cell membranes and support normal heart and blood vessel function. At appropriate doses, they can help reduce the production of triglycerides in the liver.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth with food and follow the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Fishy taste or burping, indigestion, nausea, stomach discomfort, and loose stools may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to fish or other ingredients in the product. Consult a healthcare professional before use if taking blood-thinning medicines, having a bleeding disorder, or planning surgery. Seek medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop use and seek advice if unusual bleeding occurs.

title: Zydus Warm Bag (1)Warm Bag by Zydus

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
A warm bag is used to apply gentle heat to areas of discomfort. It may provide temporary relief from muscle aches, stiffness, cramps and minor joint pain.

How does it work?
The warmth helps relax tense muscles and may increase blood flow in the treated area, which can ease discomfort.

How to take/use it
Use externally only and follow the product instructions. Apply it over clothing or with a protective cover, and check the temperature before use. Do not leave it in one place for a long period or use it while sleeping.

Common side effects
Skin redness, irritation or burns may occur if the bag is too hot or used for too long.

Precautions
Do not use on broken, infected or numb skin. Avoid use in people who may not be able to feel heat properly. Stop use if there is pain, excessive redness or blistering. Do not use a damaged or leaking bag, and keep it away from children unless supervised.

title: Zyether Inj. (2ml.)Arteether 150 Mg by Zydus
name: Zyether Inj. (2ml.)Arteether 150 Mg by Zydus
searchText: Zyether Inj. (2ml.)Arteether 150 Mg by Zydus Zydus 5000881
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Arteether injection is used to treat severe malaria, especially malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. Severe malaria requires urgent hospital treatment and monitoring.

How does it work?
Arteether is converted into an active substance that damages malaria parasites and helps clear them from the blood.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or clinic. The exact dose and treatment schedule depend on the severity of malaria and the patient's condition. Do not self-inject or stop treatment without medical advice; further antimalarial treatment may be needed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, weakness, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to artemisinin medicines, pregnancy or breastfeeding, liver or kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, or blood disorders. Severe malaria is a medical emergency and requires close monitoring. Seek urgent medical attention for breathing difficulty, severe rash, fainting, palpitations, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual weakness after treatment.

title: Zyfoly Tab (50X10)Folic Acid 5 Mg by Zydus
name: Zyfoly Tab (50X10)Folic Acid 5 Mg by Zydus
searchText: Zyfoly Tab (50X10)Folic Acid 5 Mg by Zydus Zydus 5007450
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Folic acid 5 mg is used to prevent or treat folate deficiency and the related type of anaemia. It may also be prescribed during pregnancy when a higher-strength folic acid supplement is needed, such as for prevention of certain birth defects.

How does it work?
Folic acid provides folate, a vitamin needed for making DNA and healthy red blood cells. It also supports normal growth and development of the baby during pregnancy.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. It can usually be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, bloating, gas, abdominal discomfort, or a mild skin rash may occur. Serious allergic reactions are rare.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about vitamin B12 deficiency or unexplained anaemia, as folic acid may improve the anaemia while allowing nerve damage from B12 deficiency to continue. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines for epilepsy. During pregnancy, use the prescribed strength and duration only.

title: Zygenta Plus Inj 20 ml (20ml)Gentamicin 40 Mg by Zydus

searchText: Zygenta Plus Inj 20 ml (20ml)Gentamicin 40 Mg by Zydus Zydus 5032483
bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Gentamicin is an antibacterial antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by susceptible bacteria. It is generally reserved for use under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria or prevents their growth.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The dose, route of administration and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. If supplied as an injection, it must be administered by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain or irritation, nausea, dizziness and headache may occur. Kidney problems and hearing or balance changes are important but potentially serious side effects.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy, or neuromuscular disorders. Kidney function and, when needed, hearing should be monitored during treatment. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that may affect the kidneys, hearing or muscles. Seek medical help promptly for reduced urination, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, severe dizziness or muscle weakness.

title: Zygenta Plus Inj 2 ml (2ml)Gentamicin 40 Mg by Zydus

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Gentamicin is an antibacterial medicine used to treat serious bacterial infections caused by susceptible bacteria. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria or prevents their growth.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The exact dose, treatment duration and method of use depend on the infection, kidney function and product form. If supplied as an injection, it should be given by a healthcare professional. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain or irritation, nausea, dizziness, or headache may occur. Serious effects can include ringing in the ears, hearing or balance problems, unusual weakness, or reduced urine output.

Tell the doctor about all medicines being used, particularly medicines that affect heart rhythm or serotonin. Do not use with apomorphine unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including nausea and vomiting related to surgery, cancer treatment, or other medical conditions.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals that can trigger nausea and vomiting in the brain and digestive system.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the instructions on the label and do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, dizziness, and tiredness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart rhythm problems, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or an allergy to ondansetron. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that can affect heart rhythm or serotonin levels. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms, or agitation with fever and muscle stiffness.

bodyHtml:
What is it used for?
Piperacillin and tazobactam is an injectable antibiotic used in hospitals to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, and blood. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Piperacillin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect piperacillin from enzymes that can otherwise make some bacteria resistant to it.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, and medical advice. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, rash, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to penicillin, cephalosporin or other antibiotics, kidney disease, bleeding or blood disorders, or previous antibiotic-associated diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or unusual bleeding. Use only when prescribed and complete the prescribed treatment.

What is it used for?
Ketorolac 10 mg is used for the short-term relief of moderate to severe acute pain, such as pain after surgery or injury. It is not usually intended for long-term pain treatment.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it for longer than directed, or combine it with other NSAID painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Stomach pain or discomfort, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or dehydration. It can cause stomach bleeding and kidney problems; seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, swelling or a serious skin rash. Avoid during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, particularly after 20 weeks and in the third trimester. Tell the doctor about blood thinners, steroids or other medicines being used.
